comments.author: david
comments.text: S2 result (SPIKES.md): vendor only hyperframe.runtime.iife.js (not the player). The edge serves /preview/<cap>/index.html with the runtime injected first and the bridge last; every CSP source is the capability path (<origin>/preview/<cap>/) instead of 'self', including connect-src for nested scenes; Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * on bundle files; authorize by capability only and never vary on cookies (they do arrive, same-site). The capability is one path segment for the whole bundle (not ?exp&sig per file).

Render picture first when timing edits are pending; approximate A/B cleanup preview; pre-ducked monitor music;

illegal under validate()/relayout()); the bus is stored by reference outside the 10 MiB tar limit; raw takes never
enter video/, archives or previews; recording uses the base MP4 muted as the picture with requestVideoFrameCallback
anchors and a Web Audio stem monitor on one clock; deterministic scripts/narration.ts with a receipt; recompute
guards (checkNarration, narration_modified); narration caption cue kind; caption revisions without render;
media_refs + lock protocol + two-phase GC; one canReadTake predicate.

title: Spike S10: browser sync + capture harness (needs owner hardware)
description:
Project: video-agent, an open-source Netlify template that turns a prompt into a published MP4 via Netlify Agent Runner runs writing HyperFrames compositions; Hono+OpenAPI API, Netlify Database (Drizzle), Blobs, Identity, React+Mantine UI, MCP. Plan section(s): §5.1, §5.3, §5.4, §9 (S10).

## Background
The sync promise rests on: a muted MP4 in the parent document with requestVideoFrameCallback giving presented-frame
times on the parent performance.now() clock; a Web Audio stem monitor in one AudioContext positioned from those
anchors; an AudioWorklet capturing mic PCM with sample indices; AudioContext.getOutputTimestamp() where available
(MDN: Safari 14.1+, Firefox 70+; one reviewer claimed Safari lacks it - feature-detect and measure); never adding
outputLatency on top of getOutputTimestamp (double count); mic input latency is not reliably reported
(getSettings().latency is a target, baseLatency is output-side), so it must come from calibration. Calibration must
work with headphones on - an acoustic loopback can't hear headphones. The composition iframe is sandbox=allow-scripts
(opaque origin, own time origin: CompositionPreview.tsx:235), which is why recording does not use it.

## Approach
Build one instrumented page (no app integration) that: plays a test MP4 muted with rVFC anchors; schedules stems in
one AudioContext; captures via worklet -> worker (24 kHz PCM16 streaming resample, incremental hash, IndexedDB from
chunk 1) and, for comparison, MediaRecorder (start delay, codec delay, memory); fits t = a + b*sample with residuals.
Measure on real Chrome, Safari, Firefox (macOS): built-in, USB and Bluetooth devices; headphones and speakers;
physical flash/beep loopback at start, middle, end and at punch boundaries; 10-minute drift; stall/hidden-tab/
device-change behaviour; stop -> hash -> upload -> recovery timing; multi-take audition memory under a 200 MB decode
budget. Compare calibration candidates: (a) one-time speaker input-latency loopback + getOutputTimestamp for output,
(b) clap-on-flash (8 claps, drop outliers), (c) manual offset only - report repeatability per browser/route.

## Done when
docs/spikes.md S10 section: per-browser API matrix; measured offset error at start/middle/end per setup; drift over
10 min; chosen calibration default with repeatability numbers; worklet vs MediaRecorder verdict; residual-stop
threshold recommendation (default proposal 10 ms); memory numbers for 10-min capture and multi-take audition;
explicit list of qualified setups for the <=1-frame promise; whether an iframe fallback is ever needed.

## Tests
Harness logs every anchor, fit and residual to a downloadable JSON; a script computes the error tables from the
JSON so numbers are reproducible. No unit tests required (spike).

Standard: Unit and integration with createApp(fakeDeps) and PGlite (migrations applied); Playwright on the mock build for UI; structured JSON logs (one event per step, with ids, durations and outcome) so failures are diagnosable from logs alone. ## Considerations
Owner must run the hardware matrix; prepare a checklist page so it takes < 30 minutes per browser.

budget at 90 s and 10 min. Record credits per run.

## Done when

credit delta per minute of narration, recommended STT deadline, and whether 10-minute narration fits the 22-min
budget (if not: the cap to enforce).

description:

## Background
Draft 4 assumes: one full-duration <audio data-va-layer="narration"> bus renders correctly at 90 s and 10 min;
the bus can be a bundle "reference entry" restored by key+sha256 outside the 10 MiB tar file limit
(src/lib/tar.ts:12-16; a 24 kHz PCM16 bus exceeds 10 MiB at ~218 s); mastering can be a re-mux of the final audio
stream (one master gain on the summed mix) rather than editing HTML data-volume (which would break the guards);
HyperFrames already enforces decoded-AAC true peak with bounded attenuation; an automation point cap (~512 reported by
one reviewer, not found by the other) and a degraded-automation fallback exist; a held final frame can be appended
under render-unchanged without disturbing earlier frames.

automation with 100/400/600 points and detection of degraded-mix warnings; post-render AAC decode + ffmpeg ebur128
measurement; re-mux with a master gain and re-measure; append a held-frame beat (data-va-hold) and verify frame-prefix
invariance by hashing pre-encode frames (or documented tolerance on encoded frames).

## Done when
docs/spikes.md S12: bus render verdicts and times; confirmed automation cap (or none) and the warning text to fail
on; re-mux mastering procedure + measured LUFS/true-peak; hold-frame method + invariance proof; credit numbers.

title: Spike S13: speech cleanup chain tuning (light + bypass)
description:
Project: video-agent, an open-source Netlify template that turns a prompt into a published MP4 via Netlify Agent Runner runs writing HyperFrames compositions; Hono+OpenAPI API, Netlify Database (Drizzle), Blobs, Identity, React+Mantine UI, MCP. ## Background
v1 ships cleanup 'light' (default) and 'off' (true bypass); 'heavy' (RNNoise arnndn, adeclick) is deferred to phase 6.
Proposed light chain (sample-count preserving, no trim, no time-stretch): highpass=f=80 -> afftdn (conservative) ->
gentle de-esser -> compressor 2:1, threshold -24 dBFS, attack 10 ms, release 120 ms, soft knee -> per-take gain toward a
speech target from gated integrated loudness of speech regions (silence-only takes: no gain + warning). ffmpeg runs
with -threads 1 -filter_threads 1 for determinism.

## Approach
Collect 5 real recordings (quiet room, noisy room, laptop mic, USB mic, clipping-near). Run raw vs light vs bypass
locally with the pinned ffmpeg; blind A/B with the owner; measure sample-count preservation, loudness, true peak,
intelligibility notes; tune parameters.

## Done when
docs/spikes.md S13: final light-chain parameters, A/B verdicts, sample-count proof, same-run determinism check (two
runs -> same PCM hash).

CI (typecheck, lint, vitest, Playwright, openapi:check, db:check) stays green.

## Considerations

description:

  (timestamptz), state gains 'deleting' (or a new deleting_at column if status enum is shared), index (uploader_id, role).
- media_refs: (media_id, owner_kind 'draft'|'frozen_attempt'|'version', owner_id, job_id, created_at), PK on all three
  owner columns + media_id, index on media_id and on (job_id, owner_kind).
- narration_locks: (job_id PK, holder_id, draft_id, acquired_at, heartbeat_at).
- versions.narration jsonb null (resolved op + recipe {pipeline, ffmpegVersion, settings} + bus {key, sha256,
  samples}); versions.captions jsonb null ({status 'ok'|'failed'|'off', policy 'sidecar'|'burned', rev, files {vtt,
  transcript}, sha256, generation}).
- settings: narrationEnabled boolean default true; transcriptionProvider 'local'|'elevenlabs'|'off' default 'local';
  takeQuotaBytes default 2 GiB.
Drizzle schema in db/schema.ts; store methods in src/store/drizzle.ts and the fake store; types in src/domain/types.ts.

title: canReadTake predicate enforced on every path that can expose a take
description:
Project: video-agent, an open-source Netlify template that turns a prompt into a published MP4 via Netlify Agent Runner runs writing HyperFrames compositions; Hono+OpenAPI API, Netlify Database (Drizzle), Blobs, Identity, React+Mantine UI, MCP. Feature: record your own voice-over. Plan: docs/plans/2026-11-02-record-your-own-voiceover.md (draft 4, commit cbdeaa4; §12 = settled owner decisions, §14 = review log). Line refs are as of 8649997.
Plan section(s): §1 goal 5, §2.7, §8.

## Background
Owner decision: a raw take is readable by its uploader and admins; once USED on a video (referenced by a version's
frozen narration, or by the uploader's saved draft of that video) any Creator who can read that video can read it,
so teammates can re-cut. Unused takes (flubs, discarded retakes) stay uploader-only. Reviewers/Viewers never read raw
takes - they get the rendered MP4 and narration.mp3. Private-video rules apply via "can read the video".

## Approach
Add canReadTake(principal, media, deps) in src/domain/policy.ts (or media.ts) using media_refs: true if uploader,
admin, or (creatorOrUp && exists ref with owner_kind='version' for a job the principal can read) or (creatorOrUp &&
exists ref owner_kind='draft' whose draft author == media.uploaderId and whose job the principal can read). Apply it in:
loadMedia/getMedia, signed-link issuance (media.ts:155-159), library list and music/library search, checkMedia
duplicate lookup (must not reveal others' takes - filter matches through the predicate), op resolution for narration
ops, renderEdit snapshots, upload finalization, and every MCP tool that lists or reads media. Non-take media keep
today's rules.

## Done when
One predicate used everywhere (grep shows no other take-read path); denial returns 404 (not 403) to avoid
existence leaks.

## Tests
Matrix test per path x principal: uploader, admin, Creator via used version ref, Creator via uploader-draft ref,
Creator with an unused take, Reviewer, Viewer, private video (Creator without access) - expected allow/404.

Standard: Unit and integration with createApp(fakeDeps) and PGlite (migrations applied); Playwright on the mock build for UI; structured JSON logs (one event per step, with ids, durations and outcome) so failures are diagnosable from logs alone. CI (typecheck, lint, vitest, Playwright, openapi:check, db:check) stays green.

## Considerations
Reusing a shared library audio item as narration must NOT change that item's existing access policy.
close_reason: Merged: canReadTake in src/domain/takes.ts enforced on loadMedia, mediaDto (signed links), list/search + MCP list_media, checkMedia, music search/picks, upload finalization; takes refused as library media; 8-case matrix (20 tests)

title: media_refs writers + take-row lock protocol
description:
Project: video-agent, an open-source Netlify template that turns a prompt into a published MP4 via Netlify Agent Runner runs writing HyperFrames compositions; Hono+OpenAPI API, Netlify Database (Drizzle), Blobs, Identity, React+Mantine UI, MCP. Feature: record your own voice-over. Plan: docs/plans/2026-11-02-record-your-own-voiceover.md (draft 4, commit cbdeaa4; §12 = settled owner decisions, §14 = review log). Line refs are as of 8649997.
Plan section(s): §6.1, §8 (GC and the lock protocol).

## Background
Draft save locks only the edit row; media lookup happens via deps.store outside that transaction
(src/domain/edits.ts:160,282-301) and getMedia has no lock option (drizzle.ts:440). Without a shared protocol a
concurrent save/freeze can add a reference after GC checked, and bytes still in use get deleted.

## Approach
Store helper lockTakes(tx, mediaIds) = SELECT ... FOR UPDATE on media rows in media-id order; rejects rows in
state 'deleting' (409 take_deleted). Every reference writer uses it inside its transaction and writes/updates
media_refs in the same transaction: narration op save (owner_kind draft, owner_id edit id; replace the set on each
save), renderEdit freeze (frozen_attempt, attempt id), attempt retry (re-asserts frozen_attempt), finalize (convert
frozen_attempt -> version), draft discard/expiry (delete draft refs; bump retain_until = now + 30 days on released
takes), version delete (delete version refs, bump retain_until).

## Done when
All writers go through lockTakes; media_refs always reflects references; retain_until updated on release.

## Tests
PGlite with two connections: concurrent save vs GC tombstone -> exactly one wins, no reference to a deleting row;
writer rejects deleting take; refs set equals op contents after save/discard/expiry.

Standard: Unit and integration with createApp(fakeDeps) and PGlite (migrations applied); Playwright on the mock build for UI; structured JSON logs (one event per step, with ids, durations and outcome) so failures are diagnosable from logs alone. CI (typecheck, lint, vitest, Playwright, openapi:check, db:check) stays green.

## Considerations
Lock order by media id prevents deadlocks between concurrent saves touching the same takes.
close_reason: Merged: Repo.lockMedia FOR UPDATE id-ordered, take_deleted 409, takes.ts lockTakes/replaceDraftRefs/addAttemptRefs/promoteAttemptRefs/releaseOwnerRefs (+30d retain_until), wired on draft discard/expiry and video delete; memory store tx now serializes via AsyncLocalStorage; 12 tests

title: Two-phase media GC for narration takes
description:
Project: video-agent, an open-source Netlify template that turns a prompt into a published MP4 via Netlify Agent Runner runs writing HyperFrames compositions; Hono+OpenAPI API, Netlify Database (Drizzle), Blobs, Identity, React+Mantine UI, MCP. Feature: record your own voice-over. Plan: docs/plans/2026-11-02-record-your-own-voiceover.md (draft 4, commit cbdeaa4; §12 = settled owner decisions, §14 = review log). Line refs are as of 8649997.
Plan section(s): §8 (GC).

## Background
No media GC exists today; soft delete keeps bytes forever. Owner decision: 30-day grace after last reference plus an
explicit "Delete unused recordings"; discarding a draft releases references only. Soft delete stops new picks but
never overrides retained references.

## Approach
Add a sweep step (src/domain/cleanup.ts) bounded per tick: candidates = narration takes with no media_refs and
(retain_until < now OR user-requested delete). Phase 1 in a transaction: lockTakes, re-check media_refs is empty,
set state='deleting' and insert a deletion work item. Phase 2 outside the transaction: delete Blobs original, peaks.bin,
cached transcripts; retry with backoff; mark deleted. Also expire narration_locks with stale heartbeats. Add
POST /api/v1/media/recordings/delete-unused (uploader's own unreferenced takes, immediate).

## Done when
Unreferenced expired takes lose their bytes; referenced takes never do; Blob failures retry; sweep stays bounded.

## Tests
Unit: candidate selection; race test with concurrent save (from 1.3 harness); retry after simulated Blob failure;
delete-unused endpoint only touches the caller's unreferenced takes.

Standard: Unit and integration with createApp(fakeDeps) and PGlite (migrations applied); Playwright on the mock build for UI; structured JSON logs (one event per step, with ids, durations and outcome) so failures are diagnosable from logs alone. CI (typecheck, lint, vitest, Playwright, openapi:check, db:check) stays green.

## Considerations
Log each deletion with media id and reason (no user content).
close_reason: Merged (242bfac): sweepTakes 20/tick, cleanup row kind delete_take (no migration), phase-2 deletes media/<id>/ incl peaks + transcripts with backoff, stale lock reaping, POST /media/recordings/delete-unused; 14 tests

title: Upload sessions: role, scopeJobId, client sha256; peaks blob storage + serving
description:
Project: video-agent, an open-source Netlify template that turns a prompt into a published MP4 via Netlify Agent Runner runs writing HyperFrames compositions; Hono+OpenAPI API, Netlify Database (Drizzle), Blobs, Identity, React+Mantine UI, MCP. Plan section(s): §5.1 (Upload), §6.1 (peaks), §7.

## Background
The recorder computes the file hash incrementally in a worker; today's uploader hashes the whole file in memory
(ui/src/lib/upload.ts:109 `await f.arrayBuffer()`), which a 10-minute WAV makes expensive. Completion can return before
media is ready, so clients must wait for ready. Waveforms need peaks without decoding full takes.

## Approach
Server: upload session create accepts role ('narration-take'|'narration-upload'), scopeJobId (must be a job the
caller can read) and an optional client sha256 (server still verifies per-part and whole-file hashes as today).
Store peaks at Blobs media/<id>/peaks.bin (multiresolution Int8 min/max pyramid, ~60 KB per 10 min; format documented
in src/lib/peaks.ts) uploaded as a small extra part or a follow-up PUT; speech-span summary stored in meta.json.
Serve peaks via the media file route under canReadTake. Client: uploadFile gains {sha256, role, scopeJobId, extra:
{peaks, speech}} options and a waitReady() helper.

## Done when
A take can be uploaded without the client reading the whole file into memory; peaks are retrievable for readable
takes; ready-wait works.

## Tests
Integration: create session with role/scope/sha; mismatch rejected; peaks round-trip; scope job must be readable;
ready-wait resolves.

Standard: Unit and integration with createApp(fakeDeps) and PGlite (migrations applied); Playwright on the mock build for UI; structured JSON logs (one event per step, with ids, durations and outcome) so failures are diagnosable from logs alone. CI (typecheck, lint, vitest, Playwright, openapi:check, db:check) stays green.

## Considerations
Resume state is bound to user, role and scope.

title: src/lib/timeline.ts: integer-sample timeline model (shared UI/server)
description:
Project: video-agent, an open-source Netlify template that turns a prompt into a published MP4 via Netlify Agent Runner runs writing HyperFrames compositions; Hono+OpenAPI API, Netlify Database (Drizzle), Blobs, Identity, React+Mantine UI, MCP. Plan section(s): §5.5 (Model), §6.1 (op), §6.3 step 3.

## Background
The browser preview, the server validator and the run's bus mixer must agree exactly, so all timeline math lives in
one pure TS module. Coordinates are integer samples at 24 kHz; only visuals quantize to frames.

## Approach
Exports: resolve(clips) -> non-overlapping clips (later clip wins; older clips trimmed/split non-destructively),
crossfade constant 20 ms (480 samples) using handle audio where both sides have it else edge fades, gain dB<->linear
(null = silent), fade curves, clip composition time t = start + (sourceSample - srcStart) (sync fit + offset applied
when placing a recorded take), output-duration limit (last end <= base + 120 s and <= 15 min), duck release-after-pause
constant 1,500 ms, frame quantization helpers, mixToBuffer(clips, takes, targetSamples) for both the browser
(OfflineAudioContext-free path) and Node.

## Done when
Module + docs comments; used by later beads; no I/O.

## Tests
Unit + property tests (fast-check): no overlaps after resolve; each source sample's composition time is preserved
through split/trim/move; crossfade sums to unity gain; limits enforced; mix of known impulses lands at exact samples.

Standard: Unit and integration with createApp(fakeDeps) and PGlite (migrations applied); Playwright on the mock build for UI; structured JSON logs (one event per step, with ids, durations and outcome) so failures are diagnosable from logs alone. CI (typecheck, lint, vitest, Playwright, openapi:check, db:check) stays green.

## Considerations
Keep it framework-free; ESM; runs in browser workers and Node.

title: Mastering re-mux + decoded-AAC loudness measurement
description:
Project: video-agent, an open-source Netlify template that turns a prompt into a published MP4 via Netlify Agent Runner runs writing HyperFrames compositions; Hono+OpenAPI API, Netlify Database (Drizzle), Blobs, Identity, React+Mantine UI, MCP. Feature: record your own voice-over. Plan: docs/plans/2026-11-02-record-your-own-voiceover.md (draft 4, commit cbdeaa4; §12 = settled owner decisions, §14 = review log). Line refs are as of 8649997.
Plan section(s): §6.3 step 7.

## Background
Changing HTML volumes after render would break the exact-transform guard; HyperFrames already enforces AAC true peak
with bounded attenuation; hyperframes audio analyses sources, not the mix.

## Approach
After hyperframes render: decode the final AAC, measure with ffmpeg ebur128; if outside -14 +/- 1 LUFS (non-silent
mixes), apply one master gain to the summed mix by re-muxing the audio stream (procedure from S12), peak-first
(true peak <= -1 dBTP wins; record measured LUFS + warning when both can't be met); silent/near-silent mixes exempt;
any HyperFrames degraded-automation warning fails the run. Record measurements in the run report.

## Done when
Delivered audio meets targets or the run reports why; video stream untouched by re-mux.

## Tests
Script tests with fixture MP4s: loud, quiet, silent, peak-limited cases; video stream hash unchanged after re-mux.

Standard: Unit and integration with createApp(fakeDeps) and PGlite (migrations applied); Playwright on the mock build for UI; structured JSON logs (one event per step, with ids, durations and outcome) so failures are diagnosable from logs alone. CI (typecheck, lint, vitest, Playwright, openapi:check, db:check) stays green.
close_reason: Merged (87ad20f): mastering for narrated renders: ebur128 measure, exempt < −50 LUFS/no speech, one gain peak-capped at −1.2 dBTP, audio-only re-encode (S12 settings), framemd5 video identity check, callback mastering {status,before,after,gainDb,warnings}; automation cap 400 narrated / 512 others (fixup); tests

comments.author: david
comments.text: S12+S13: master by re-encoding audio only (video packets byte-identical); speech target -18 LUFS means the -14 LUFS mix needs ~1.5 dB limiting at -1 dBTP; HyperFrames silently truncates automation > 512 points with no warning, so fail ourselves above 400 (no warning text to grep).

comments.author: david
comments.text: From va-2qq.3.9: bus limiter is a TS look-ahead limiter at a fixed −2 dBTP (receipt.recipe.limiter); at ~−18 LUFS speech it barely changes PLR - mastering likely needs the ceiling/gain revisited to reach −14 LUFS.

## Background

provider, model, language). Status reported to the version (ok/failed/off).

## Done when
Transcripts produced within the deadline or the run continues with status failed.

for the chosen provider's JSON schema (fixture).

English only in v1.

title: Caption revisions without render (signed paths, CAS, mirror generations, editor)
description:
Project: video-agent, an open-source Netlify template that turns a prompt into a published MP4 via Netlify Agent Runner runs writing HyperFrames compositions; Hono+OpenAPI API, Netlify Database (Drizzle), Blobs, Identity, React+Mantine UI, MCP. Plan section(s): §2.6, §6.6 (Caption revisions).

## Background
Transcription errors are common and user-visible, so fixes ship with the first recording release. Private file URLs
are signed for fixed names (src/domain/files.ts:44) and the files edge function matches a fixed regex, builds the
key from the path and caches private+immutable (netlify/edge-functions/files.ts:18,37-47). Publication writes happen
after DB transactions (src/domain/videos.ts:640-690).

## Approach
POST /api/v1/videos/:id/versions/:n/captions {expectedRev, cues}: owner/admin (+ publish authority when published);
CAS on versions.captions.rev; escape text; refuse when policy='burned'. Write immutable captions.r<k>.vtt and
transcript.r<k>.txt; files.ts signs names from versions.captions.files; edge regex accepts captions(?:\.r\d+)?\.vtt
and transcript(?:\.r\d+)?\.txt; render hashes untouched (revision hashes live in versions.captions); bump video ETag;
publication mirror carries captionsGeneration and is updated with CAS after commit with durable retry (late corrections
never overwrite newer ones; correction after unpublish is a no-op). Carry-forward: a new version from n with an
unchanged narration op hash copies n's latest caption revision; otherwise re-transcribe. UI: transcript cue editor on
the Video page (text-only edits, timings fixed).

## Done when
Fixes appear on private and public VTT without a render; no stale or resurrected mirrors.

## Tests
Integration: CAS conflict; signed path for revision; edge serving; mirror generation ordering incl. unpublish race;
carry-forward by op hash; Playwright: edit a cue and see it in the player.

Standard: Unit and integration with createApp(fakeDeps) and PGlite (migrations applied); Playwright on the mock build for UI; structured JSON logs (one event per step, with ids, durations and outcome) so failures are diagnosable from logs alone. CI (typecheck, lint, vitest, Playwright, openapi:check, db:check) stays green.

title: Contract: narration audio role, bus element, draft vs materialized validator, speech spans
description:
Project: video-agent, an open-source Netlify template that turns a prompt into a published MP4 via Netlify Agent Runner runs writing HyperFrames compositions; Hono+OpenAPI API, Netlify Database (Drizzle), Blobs, Identity, React+Mantine UI, MCP. ## Background
AUDIO_ROLES is ['music','voice','sfx'] (src/lib/contract.ts:236) and validate() rejects other values (:423-425); the
DTO enum excludes narration (src/schemas.ts:753). Layers must be on track >= 1 and span the video (:337-347) and
relayout() resets every layer to start 0/full duration then runs applyDucking (:569-573) - so only one full-duration
narration bus survives saves.

## Approach
Add 'narration' to AUDIO_ROLES, the AudioRole type, audioOf(), the DTO enum and the editor's track mapping in one
change. Writer: one element <audio id="va-narration" data-va-layer="narration" data-va-audio="narration"
data-track-index="4" data-start="0" data-duration="<root>" data-volume="1" data-va-speech='[[s,e],...]'
src="assets/narration/bus.wav">. read() classifies it as narration (not SFX). Validator: at most one; src fixed;
draft state = no file present and data-va-speech computed from the op + each take's stored speech-span summary;
materialized state = referenced file's sample count equals root duration. AI voice modes reuse existing mute semantics
(data-volume=0 + data-va-muted, level in data-va-volume; contract.ts:696-718): replace mutes all data-va-voice, under
sets level, keep unchanged. No per-clip attributes in HTML.

## Done when
Applying a narration op to a contract-1 composition yields a valid draft; relayout keeps it valid; materialized
validation enforced in the run.

## Tests
Unit: role acceptance; validator draft/materialized; relayout with root-duration change; AI voice modes; speech
span computation from summaries (bounded count, frame-quantized).

Standard: Unit and integration with createApp(fakeDeps) and PGlite (migrations applied); Playwright on the mock build for UI; structured JSON logs (one event per step, with ids, durations and outcome) so failures are diagnosable from logs alone. title: Peaks + speech-span summary module (browser worker and Node)
description:
Project: video-agent, an open-source Netlify template that turns a prompt into a published MP4 via Netlify Agent Runner runs writing HyperFrames compositions; Hono+OpenAPI API, Netlify Database (Drizzle), Blobs, Identity, React+Mantine UI, MCP. Plan section(s): §5.1 (Worker), §6.1 (peaks), §6.2 (draft spans).

## Background
Draft-state duck lanes need speech spans without the bus; waveforms need peaks without full decodes. Both are
computed where the audio is: the recorder worker for takes, and the browser (decode in a worker) for uploads.

## Approach

title: Redo a scene: regenerate one or more beats as a scoped revision, everything else frozen and checked twice
description:
Project: video-agent, an open-source Netlify template that turns a prompt into a published MP4 via Netlify Agent Runner runs writing HyperFrames compositions; Hono+OpenAPI API, Netlify Database (Drizzle), Blobs, Identity, React+Mantine UI, MCP. Feature: redo a scene (a scoped revision: pick one or more scenes (beats) of a finished version, say what should change, and get a new version where only those scenes changed; everything else is frozen, spliced back deterministically and checked twice, in the run and in finalize). Spec: docs/plans/2026-11-04-regenerate-beat.md (draft 3, commit e477294; review logs at its end, §13). Line refs are as of e477294; main keeps moving (videos.ts, app.ts, schemas.ts, mcp.ts and the UI pages drifted by 4c573aa), so search by the named symbol when a line is off.
Spec key: RB
Spec section(s): all (§0-§13)

## Background
Why the feature exists (spec §1): a whole-video revision restores the parent and asks the agent to 'Change only what the request asks for' (src/domain/prompt.ts:215-217), which nothing checks, so revisions drift (agents tidy, retime and rephrase things nobody mentioned). A scoped revision makes 'only this part' a checked guarantee, should cost less (a run is fixed overhead plus what the agent reads/writes/renders: hello run 14.4 credits docs/spikes.md:8; render-unchanged 33.6-34.4 :164-175; authoring 90-250 :34-49; a revision-kind remix 120.3, docs/plans/2026-11-03-remix.md:307), and is the natural action for comments pinned to a moment (each moment falls in exactly one beat). Editing contract v1 makes it possible: beats are direct children of the root, each animates itself with one vaBeat script selecting inside its own element, nothing animates across a boundary (video/AGENTS.md 'Editing contract v1'; validate src/lib/contract.ts:395-450).

What is guaranteed (spec §0, §4.9, after review R4): the SAVED COMPOSITION. Outside the scope, the uploaded index.html and summary.json are byte-for-byte what splicing the parent produces, and every other existing file is the parent's. The MP4 is trusted like every run's (finalize never derives the MP4 from the archive for any run kind, src/domain/finalize.ts:131-236), bound to the composition by its length (±0.25 s), and the live test checks frozen scenes' frames by SSIM. Script isolation is a heuristic; SSIM is the only pixel check.

Reviews: draft 1 by an independent Fable 5.1 review and the cross-plan seam review; draft 2 by a remote Fable 5.1 high review (Netlify Agent Run at 19740d8). Every claim was checked against the code (spec §13 review logs). Key review outcomes: splice-then-compare with the render using the splice's bytes; a scope-aware relayout that keeps frozen durations verbatim (authored parents are never relaid); semantic compare in the run, byte equality in finalize; css-tree style allow-list; GSAP string targets refused; beats read route for old versions; stills made last with feedbackStills (it wipes video/feedback/).

## Approach
Phases (spec §7), each ending with a gate bead; gates chain:
- Phase 0: spikes B2 (frozen beats render the same: SSIM threshold) and B3 (one hand-made scoped run, ~100 credits). B1 (@scope in the renderer) is a phase 1 fixture task.
- Phase 1: the splice and the checks, run side (contract-core.ts relayoutScoped, src/lib/scope.ts, style/script checks, manifest scope, prepare-run, check-contract --fix, render-job guard, engine scopeCheck hook).
- Phase 2: the service (migration versions.scope/versions.beats, finalize beats + server-side byte check + MP4 binding, reviseVideo rules, reconciler + prompt, GET beats route, REST/OpenAPI/features/MCP/skill, the live test script) + live test part 1.
- Phase 3: the UI (revise panel scene picker, Redo this part on a comment, Incorporate scoped switch, history label, Revise the whole video after a scope refusal) + a production check.
- Phase 4: SDK and CLI (redoScenes, scenes, revise --scene, redo), local mode's local revise --scene (4.1c), README, live test part 2, as-built numbers; then the after-the-gate items (editor beat card, timeline menu, hover-to-seek, version switcher jump, backfill-beats script, SCOPED_AGENT_* knob and its measured comparison).

Architecture in one paragraph (spec §0): POST /api/v1/videos/{id}/versions takes scope: { beats } with a required fromVersion. The run is still the revision kind; the manifest gains an optional scope. Before rendering, a deterministic splice (src/lib/scope.ts spliceScoped) builds what the composition must be: the parent with the agent's scoped beats put in, re-laid with frozen durations kept verbatim, later captions shifted, ducking rewritten. check-contract --fix writes the splice and reports what it put back; render-job refuses anything left outside the scope and renders the splice's bytes; finalize re-splices from the parent archive on the server and requires byte equality plus the MP4 length binding. HyperFrames only in v1 (engine capability scopedRevision).

Release order inside the epic (polish round 1): every merged bead deploys to production (repo rule), so nothing may accept a scope before the server enforces it. The public switch is task 2.6 (ReviseSchema accepts scope; features lists scoped_revision), and it waits for reviseVideo (2.3), the reconciler + prompt (2.4) and finalize's byte check (2.2b); MCP (2.6b) follows 2.6. Data work (2.1 migration, 2.2 finalize beats, 2.5 beats route) doesn't need phase 1 (spec §7), and the UI's layout tasks start once 2.6 fixes the DTO and mock data; the UI gate (3.G) still waits for phase 2's gate. Shared constants live in src/lib/scope.ts: SCOPE_VIOLATED, SCOPE_REFUSED_PREFIX, isScopeRefusal, isLockedLength, spliceBytes.

Cross-plan dependencies (roadmap build order; the orchestrator adds the edges): phase 1 needs render-engines phase 1 (contract-core.ts, Engine interface with capabilities.scopedRevision, versions.engine; if this plan lands first it creates contract-core.ts under that name); phase 2 needs cli-and-sdk phase 1 (operationIds, features in /api/v1/config) and merges after Looks phase 2 (template bump order Looks 2 -> redo 2; migration order engines 1 -> Looks 2 -> redo 2); phase 4 needs cli-and-sdk phases 2-3 (SDK, remote CLI). render-engines phase 3 needs this plan's phase 1 (the scopeCheck hook). The GitHub Action's '/video redo' uses scope.beats.

Owner questions (spec §12). All are built on their recommended defaults; none blocks work:
1. Length: may redoing a scene change its length, moving later scenes? Built: yes, except with recorded narration (then exact).
2. Cheaper model for scoped runs: no knob in v1; SCOPED_AGENT_MODEL/SCOPED_AGENT_EFFORT only after a measured comparison shows a win. Built: knob after the gate (phase 4 after-gate tasks), unset by default.
3. Who can redo scenes: anyone who can revise (version:create; Admin, Creator). Built: yes.
4. How many scenes at once: 1-20, never all. Built: yes.
5. Scoped Incorporate feedback default: switch shown when every picked comment is pinned; starts ON when pins fall in fewer than half the scenes, OFF otherwise. Built: yes.
6. Variations (2-3 takes of a scene): later, as their own plan. Built: not in v1.
7. Held last frame: refuse va-hold and the last real beat when the version ends with va-hold, in v1. Built: refuse.
8. Finalize sets versions.contract atomically with ready (and beats), using ensureBundle's inputs (contractOf over the archive PLUS missingLocalFiles with references and library media, src/domain/bundles.ts:170-188), not index.html alone. Built: yes, with those inputs.
9. Editor entry points (beat card, timeline menu): after the live gate. Built: after the gate (phase 4 after-gate tasks).
10. New fonts in a scoped scene: not allowed in v1 (only fonts the composition already loads). Built: not allowed.
Decided (2026-11-04, roadmap): people-facing words are "scene" and "Redo this scene"; code/API say beat and scope; CLI flag --scene; feature string scoped_revision; packages netlify-video-agent (CLI, bin video-agent) and netlify-video-agent-sdk; local mode ships ("make one locally, then deploy it for your team"); live tests run --dry then ask the owner before each run.

## Done when
Every phase epic closed; live tests LT-1 and LT-2 passed on production (after the owner's go-ahead); CI green; docs/spikes.md has the B2/B3 and gate numbers; the spec gets an 'As built' note.

## Tests
Each phase has a gate bead; unit/integration/UI tests are listed per bead.

Standard: unit and integration with createApp(fakeDeps) (test/helpers.ts harness) and PGlite (pgStore(), every migration applied); Playwright on the mock build (VITE_MOCK=1) for UI; structured JSON logs (one event per step, with ids, durations and outcome) so failures are diagnosable from logs alone. CI (npm run typecheck, lint, vitest, npx playwright test, openapi:check, db:check) stays green. Repo rule: when checks pass, commit only your own files, push to main and confirm the Netlify production deploy is ready (other sessions often have uncommitted files in the checkout; never stage them).

## Considerations
Not in v1 (spec §11), kept for later; these need their own design and have no beads here:
- Variations ("three takes of this scene, let me pick"): versions are one at a time (hasUnfinished, videos.ts:423) and three runs cost 3x. Cheap design: one run authors N alternatives as hidden sibling sections, renders a short audition clip (or stills), the pick is applied with a render-unchanged splice (~34 credits). Needs an "audition" output kind and a picker; its own plan once scoped runs are measured.
- Adding, splitting, merging or removing scenes through the agent ("add a scene after this one"): needs new-id rules and comment/caption mapping.
- Redo from an unrendered editor draft: needs a scoped author_from_frozen; v1 starts from the rendered version.
- Rendering only the changed frames and splicing them into the parent MP4 (audio continuity, GOP boundaries, poster and GIF).

description:

Spec key: B2
Spec section(s): §7 Phase 0, §9 (frozen beats render slightly differently), §10

## Background
The guarantee is on the composition (frozen scenes' HTML is the parent's), but people judge pixels. H.264 at different time offsets won't be bit-identical even for identical HTML (GOP boundaries move), so the live test needs an SSIM threshold measured on real renders, not guessed. No credits: local renders only.

## Approach
Measures: SSIM of untouched beats' frames between a parent render and a render where one middle beat was replaced AND its length changed (so later beats are time-shifted).
Steps:
1. Pick or build a contract-v1 fixture with >=4 beats and music (test/fixtures has compositions; or restore a real version's source.tar.gz locally). Render it locally the way render-job does (npx -y hyperframes render --quality standard --output …, scripts/render-job.ts:202, from the fixture dir).
2. Replace beat 2's section by hand (new text, new animation), lengthen it by 1.37 s (not frame-aligned on purpose), re-lay the beats (use the editor's relayout via applyEdits retime, or the phase 1 relayoutScoped if it exists), render again.
3. Sample frames of beats 1, 3, 4 every 0.5 s at matched beat-relative times (beat 3/4 shifted by the delta) with ffmpeg -ss … -frames:v 1, compare with ffmpeg's ssim filter (ffmpeg -i a.png -i b.png -lavfi ssim -f null -).
4. Repeat on a 9:16 and a 1:1 fixture.
Pass bar: a clear separation between frozen frames (expected >= 0.99) and changed frames (beat 2, expected well below). Results change the plan: the threshold becomes SSIM_MIN in scripts/e2e/regen-beat.ts (task 2.7, va-8cy4.3.9) and is quoted in docs/spikes.md; if frozen frames ever fall below ~0.97, investigate determinism (fonts, time-dependent CSS) before building phase 2.

A table (fixture, aspect, beat, min/median SSIM) and the chosen threshold written to docs/spikes.md under 'B2'.

## Tests
The comparison script (scripts/e2e/lib/ssim.ts or inline in the spike folder) logs one JSON line per sampled frame { beat, tParent, tChild, ssim }. Keep the script: task 2.7 (va-8cy4.3.9) reuses it for --selftest and the live steps, so write it as scripts/e2e/lib/ssim.ts with a small exported API (sampleFrame(mp4, atSec, out), ssim(a, b): number).

## Background
relayout (src/lib/contract.ts:1026-1058) lays beats back to back snapping each CUMULATIVE end to whole frames, so a non-aligned beat pushes its rounding into the next one; syncCaptions (:1060-1085) snaps every cue (:1072-1073). relayout runs only on editor, narration and re-voice paths (callers :901 applyFitNarration, :984/:998 held frame, :1093 applyEdits, :1268 applyRevoice); an AUTHORED composition is never relaid, and validate only needs each start within half a frame of the running sum (:424). So an authored contract-v1 parent can have non-aligned beats (3.85 s = 115.5 frames). Re-laying it with plain relayout would change frozen beats' durations (3.833/3.867 s): the remote review's R1 finding. Roadmap shared rule 6: frame math on the Composition model lives in src/lib/contract-core.ts (name owned by render-engines); import it, don't re-export from contract.ts.

## Approach
- If render-engines phase 1 has landed: import relayout and syncCaptions from src/lib/contract-core.ts and add relayoutScoped there. If not: create src/lib/contract-core.ts with relayout and syncCaptions moved verbatim from contract.ts (contract.ts imports them back; no behaviour change) plus relayoutScoped.
- relayoutScoped(d: Doc, scoped: ReadonlySet<string>): frozen beats keep their data-duration STRING verbatim; scoped beats are already snapped by the caller (whole frames, frames() at :67); each beat's data-start = fmt(sum of the durations before it) (what validate expects at :424); root data-duration, every data-va-layer's data-start=0/data-duration, and video slots' data-start=0/data-duration=beat duration (as relayout does) get the new total; speech spans on narration buses are trimmed and applyDucking(d) is called exactly as relayout does.
- Also export a caption shifter for frozen beats: shiftCues(cues, beatStartDelta) that adds a delta WITHOUT re-rounding (unshifted beats keep exact times).

contract-core.ts exists with relayout, relayoutScoped, syncCaptions (and the shifter); the editor's behaviour is unchanged; relayoutScoped keeps frozen durations byte-identical.

## Background
render-job runs ONE guard from an else-if ladder (scripts/render-job.ts:104-176); the narrated-revision branch catches every revision of a narrated parent, so the scope check must be a SEPARATE if after the ladder: a scoped revision of a narrated parent gets both the narration check (checkNarrationKept) and the scope check.

## Approach
Where: a separate `if (m.attemptId === attempt && m.scope)` block, not another `else if` in the guard ladder (scripts/render-job.ts:104-176), so a scoped revision of a narrated parent gets the narration check (checkNarrationKept, :147-158) AND the scope check. Place it BEFORE render-job's generic contract validate (:86-97), not after the ladder: that validate checks derived values, so on an agent file with stale starts it would fail with misleading 'should start at' messages (spec §3 gotcha 2) before the clear scope message. Order for a scoped run: scope guard (refuse, or write the splice) -> generic validate (runs on the splice and passes) -> the ladder (narration check on the spliced files). The plan said 'after the ladder'; what matters is that it's a separate if (review A1.5), and running it first gives the agent the right error.
- The guard: engine.scopeCheck(.render/frozen, video/, m.scope.beats) (RunEngine hook, task 1.3). Any problem -> throw StepError(`${SCOPE_VIOLATED}: ${problems[0]}`) with the full list and 'Run npx tsx scripts/check-contract.ts --fix, put those parts back, and run render-job again.' Nothing is rendered or archived.
- On success write files (index.html, summary.json = spliceBytes) into video/, so the render, the archive (source.tar.gz) and the uploaded hashes are exactly the splice; then continue as today. Log scope.verified { beats, lengthDelta, newFiles, ms }.
- Mechanics: the manifest is read at :101-103 today, after the contract block; read it before the contract block for this check, and re-read indexHtml and summary (:74-86) after writing the splice so every later step sees the splice. If render-engines' refactor (va-ed2s.2.6, render-job calls engine.contract) has landed, put the guard before engine.contract the same way.
- Missing .render/frozen with a scope -> StepError 'The frozen copy of the parent is missing (prepare-run makes it). Stop and report this.'

title: Scoped-beat style and markup checks with css-tree (one prelude-less @scope; at-rule allow-list)
description:
Project: video-agent, an open-source Netlify template that turns a prompt into a published MP4 via Netlify Agent Runner runs writing HyperFrames compositions; Hono+OpenAPI API, Netlify Database (Drizzle), Blobs, Identity, React+Mantine UI, MCP. Line refs are as of e477294; main keeps moving (videos.ts, app.ts, schemas.ts, mcp.ts and the UI pages drifted by 4c573aa), so search by the named symbol when a line is off.
Spec key: 1.2d
Spec section(s): §4.6, §3 gotcha 5, reviews A3 and R6

## Background
Shared CSS lives outside beats (<head>, root-level <style>: fonts, classes, --va-color-*). Inside a beat there are many ways to leak styles: <link rel=stylesheet>, a second <style> (also inside <svg>), --va-color-* declarations (readColors src/lib/contract.ts:249-256 reads EVERY <style> and the editor's colour op rewrites each one, :1143-1151, so a scoped declaration would become an editor colour role), data-composition-src sub-compositions (separate HTML outside every check), global at-rules. css-tree 3.2.1 is installed via hyperframes (npm ls css-tree) and becomes a direct dependency. A prelude-less @scope inside a <style> scopes to the style's parent element (CSS spec, MDN @scope), so the agent can't write the wrong beat id.

## Approach
In src/lib/scope.ts (or src/lib/scope-style.ts imported by it): scopedStyleProblems(beatEl, beatId): string[].
- Add css-tree to package.json dependencies pinned to the installed 3.2.x (install with npx npm@11 install, since local npm 10 strips package-lock libc fields; check the lockfile diff only adds css-tree's own entry). Use css-tree's parse + walk; also handle a <style> whose text fails to parse ('Scene "Features": its <style> isn't valid CSS: <css-tree message>').
- At most one <style>, a DIRECT child of the beat, whose text parses (css-tree parse) to exactly one top-level @scope rule with NO prelude.
- Inside it, an at-rule ALLOW-list: @media, @supports, unnamed @container, @keyframes. Every other at-rule refused by name (@import, @font-face, @namespace, @layer, @property, @counter-style, @page, @font-palette-values, @position-try, @view-transition, named @container, anything added later). Allow-list so it doesn't age with Chrome.
- Selectors: no :root, html, body, :scope's ancestors (:scope + x, x :scope), and no :has() whose argument starts with a combinator reaching outside the scope root; @scope's implicit root is the beat, so plain selectors are fine.
- url(): only plain relative paths under assets/ (no //, no scheme such as data:, http:, javascript:, no ..).
- @keyframes names must start with '<beatId>-' (keyframe names are global even inside @scope).
- No custom property declarations named --va-color-* (in the style or any style attribute in the beat).
- Markup in the scoped beat: no other <style> anywhere (including <svg><style>), no <link>, no data-composition-src.
- Fonts: no @font-face (refused above); the beat may use only fonts the composition already loads (owner Q10).
- Fallback if B1 shows prelude-less @scope misbehaving: accept @scope ([data-va-beat="X"]) with the prelude checked against the id (keep both paths behind one function).
Messages in plain words, naming the scene by label: 'Scene "Features": its <style> declares --va-color-accent; use the root's colour roles.'

## Done when
Every rule above enforced with a plain-words message; css-tree is a direct dependency; no CSS parsing by regex.

## Tests
Unit tests (src/lib/scope-style.test.ts, fixtures as inline strings plus test/fixtures/scope/styles/*.html):
- fine: valid prelude-less @scope with @media/@supports/unnamed @container/prefixed @keyframes (features-pulse); url(assets/beats/features/a.png); url("assets/x.svg"); var(--va-color-surface) uses; a style attribute without --va-color-*.
- reported (one message each, naming the scene by its data-va-label): prelude naming another beat; prelude naming this beat (until B1 says the prelude form is the fallback); two @scope blocks; a top-level rule outside @scope; a block that closes early and continues (} body {); unparseable CSS; @import; @font-face; @property; @counter-style; @page; @layer; @namespace; @position-try; named @container; :root/html/body selectors; url(https://…), url(//x), url(data:…), url(javascript:…), url(../x), url(/abs); unprefixed @keyframes; --va-color-accent in the style or a style attribute; a second <style>; <svg><style>; <link rel=stylesheet>; data-composition-src.
- Frozen beats with the same CSS are never checked (the function only takes scoped beats).

description:

## Background
validate's isolation check is a regex, /\bdocument\s*\.|window\.__timelines/ (src/lib/contract.ts:436). el.parentElement, ownerDocument, closest(), getRootNode() and globalThis tricks escape it. GSAP resolves STRING targets (tl.from('.card', …), gsap.utils.toArray('.card')) against the whole document, not the beat (video/vendor/va-contract.js:9-16 hands the beat a plain timeline), and it's the most common way an agent selects. Applied to SCOPED beats only, not every beat: validate runs on every new run and on bundles of existing versions, so tightening it everywhere would make working videos non-editable (review A4 adopted with that change).

## Approach
scopedScriptProblems(beatEl, beatId): string[] in src/lib/scope.ts.
- On the beat's vaBeat script text, refuse matches of: parentNode|parentElement|ownerDocument|getRootNode|closest\(|previousElementSibling|nextElementSibling|globalThis|self\.|\bwindow\b|\beval\b|\bFunction\( (on top of the existing document/__timelines check).
- Refuse GSAP string targets: /\b(tl|gsap)\.(from|to|fromTo|set|timeline)\(\s*['"`]/ and /gsap\.utils\.toArray\(\s*['"`]/.
- Do NOT add \btop\b, \bparent\b, \bframes\b (review R5 partly rejected): top is a CSS property GSAP animates ({ top: 10 }), parent/frames are common names; they'd refuse honest scripts.
- Message: 'Scene "Features"'s script uses a selector string in tl.from(…): select with el.querySelector(All) and pass elements.'
- Isolation remains a heuristic; the live test's SSIM over frozen scenes is the pixel check (say so in a code comment).

## Done when
Scoped beats with escapes or string targets are reported; frozen beats and honest code are not.

## Tests
Unit tests (src/lib/scope-script.test.ts or a describe block in scope.test.ts):

title: src/lib/scope.ts spliceScoped: parent + agent's scoped beats -> the composition the scope allows
description:
Project: video-agent, an open-source Netlify template that turns a prompt into a published MP4 via Netlify Agent Runner runs writing HyperFrames compositions; Hono+OpenAPI API, Netlify Database (Drizzle), Blobs, Identity, React+Mantine UI, MCP. Line refs are as of e477294; main keeps moving (videos.ts, app.ts, schemas.ts, mcp.ts and the UI pages drifted by 4c573aa), so search by the named symbol when a line is off.
Spec key: 1.2
Spec section(s): §4.5 (steps 1-9), §4.4 table, §4.7, §3 gotchas 2-4/7-10, reviews A1, A8, R1

## Background
The splice says exactly what the result must be, so the check can't drift from the rule, and the render uses the splice so what people get is what was checked (the re-voice guard proved the shape: checkRevoiced compares with applyRevoice's output, src/lib/revoice.ts:84-169). Review A1: don't validate the agent's file first (validate checks derived values too, src/lib/contract.ts:395-450, so the normal 'I made Features 2 s longer and didn't move the later scenes' case would fail with misleading messages).

## Approach
src/lib/scope.ts:
interface ScopeInput { parent: { html; summary: Summary; voice?: VoiceFile|null; script?: VoiceScript|null }; agent: { same }; beats: readonly string[]; lockedLength: boolean /* recorded narration */ }
spliceScoped(i): { html: string; summary: Summary; putBack: string[]; problems: string[] }
Steps (spec §4.5):
1. validate(parent) only; a failure is a server bug (not_editable should have stopped it) -> problems with that wording. load(agent.html) WITHOUT validating (its derived values are expected to be stale).
2. Beat list: agent beats = parent's ids, same order, each once; report added/removed/renamed/moved by label.
3. Start from the parent Doc; replace each scoped <section data-va-beat> with a deep clone of the agent's.
4. Scoped beats: snap data-duration to whole frames (frames(), contract.ts:67); refuse a change when lockedLength ('Keep each scoped scene exactly as long as it is now: the recorded narration is locked'); set data-va-authored-duration = data-duration (freshly authored, so its captions don't stretch); bounds 0.5-120 s (the editor's retime bounds, contract.ts applyOne); run scopedStyleProblems (1.2d) and scopedScriptProblems (1.2e).
5. relayoutScoped(d, scoped) (task 1.1). Then assert every frozen beat's data-duration string equals the parent's (runtime assertion -> problems 'internal: frozen beat X changed length').
6. Captions: keep the agent's cues whose beat is scoped, deriving a missing beatStart/beatEnd as start - beat.start, then absolute times from beat-relative ones snapped as syncCaptions does (fresh beat). Keep the parent's other cues, including recorded-narration cues (narration: true, no beat), shifting each frozen beat's cues by that beat's start delta WITHOUT re-rounding (shiftCues from 1.1). Voice cues of voiced scoped beats are recomputed from voice.json with the code syncVoice uses (scripts/voice.ts:145-171, voiceCaptions) so they can't be hand-edited; syncVoice drops non-voice cues of voiced beats, keep that rule. Sort by (start, beat, textId).
7. title and summary from the agent; credits = parent ∪ agent, de-duplicated, order kept.
8. validate(splice, summary, narration bus opts when locked); its violations are reported as the agent's ('Scene "Features": its voice-over runs to 5.2 s; make the scene longer').
9. putBack: every difference between the agent's file and the splice outside the scope, from scopeProblems. That function is task 1.2b, which depends on this one: here spliceScoped returns putBack: [] behind a single call site (const putBack = comparePutBack(i, splice)), and 1.2b fills it in. Steps 1-8 and their tests are this task.
Also (defence in depth, reviseVideo refuses these first): a scope naming va-hold (HOLD_BEAT, contract.ts:909) or the last real beat before it, or an id that isn't a parent beat, is a problem ('internal: …'), and the splice is not built.
lockedLength helper: export isLockedLength(parentHtml) = the parent has the va-narration element (NARRATION_ID, contract.ts:685); check-contract, render-job and finalize all derive lockedLength with it, so the three places can't disagree.
What the agent may change (§4.4): inside scoped beats anything (children, text, media slots, script, sfx <audio id>, voice line); keep data-va-beat, data-composition-id, position, track 0; one beat in, one beat out (no add/split/remove in v1); text ids unique and should start with '<beat>-'. Everything else frozen: other beats, <head>, root attributes except data-duration, root-level <style>/<script>, layers except data-duration and the music's ducking data-automation; the narration element untouched.
Serialization: the render uses save(splice) for index.html and JSON.stringify(splice.summary, null, 2) for summary.json; export a helper spliceBytes() returning both so render-job and finalize produce identical bytes. Splicing a splice must be a fixed point (finalize relies on byte equality, review R4).
Constants exported here for every consumer (render-job, finalize, the reconciler's retry line and the UI's refusal state): SCOPE_VIOLATED = 'scope_violated' (render-job's StepError prefix) and SCOPE_REFUSED_PREFIX = 'This run changed parts of the video outside the scenes it was asked to redo' (finalize's invalid_output message), plus isScopeRefusal(message: string | null): boolean matching either.
Logs (the callers log; spliceScoped returns the data): scope.splice { beats, lengthDelta, putBack: n, problems: n, ms }.

## Done when
spliceScoped implements steps 1-9 with plain-words problems; fixed point holds; frozen durations preserved.

## Tests
src/lib/scope.test.ts with fixtures under test/fixtures/scope/ (built from test/fixtures/contract1-music and contract1-voice: a 4-beat parent with music, a voiced parent, a narrated parent with va-narration, and a parent ending with va-hold):
- Only the scoped beat changed -> no problems; splice equals the agent's file semantically.
- Scoped beat grew 2 s and the agent left later starts stale -> splice re-lays it, no problems: later beats start 2 s later, root and layers +2 s, later text cues +2 s, voice cues follow their beats, ducking lane equals applyDucking on the result.
- A 3.85 s SCOPED beat (115.5 frames) is snapped to 3.833333 or 3.866667 (frames(), contract.ts:67); every frozen beat after it keeps the parent's exact data-duration string.
- A parent whose FROZEN beats are 3.85 s (authored, never relaid): splice keeps them verbatim, starts validate, cues of frozen beats before the scope keep exact times, cues after it shift by exactly the delta.
- Shrunk below its voice's end -> splice validation's 'make the scene longer' message naming the scene.
- Bounds: a scoped beat of 0.4 s or 121 s -> problem naming the 0.5-120 s range.
- Beat renamed/removed/added/moved -> reported by label (one message each).
- lockedLength (narrated fixture): a length change refused; the same length passes; isLockedLength true for the narrated fixture, false otherwise.
- va-hold fixture: scope on va-hold or on the last real beat -> 'internal: …' problem, no splice.
- Captions: missing beatStart/beatEnd derived from start - beat.start; agent cues of frozen beats ignored (taken from the parent); recorded-narration cues (no beat) kept verbatim; output sorted by (start, beat, textId) whatever the input order.
- Voice: a voiced scoped beat's cues are recomputed from voice.json (a hand-edited voice cue is replaced).
- credits: parent ∪ agent, de-duplicated, order kept.
- Fixed point: spliceBytes of the splice fed back in as the agent's files is byte-identical to the first spliceBytes (index.html and summary.json).
- Determinism: the same inputs give the same bytes twice in a row.
- isScopeRefusal: true for 'scope_violated: …' and the finalize prefix, false for other invalid_output messages and null.

title: scope.ts scopeProblems: semantic compare outside the scope, every difference named in plain words
description:
Project: video-agent, an open-source Netlify template that turns a prompt into a published MP4 via Netlify Agent Runner runs writing HyperFrames compositions; Hono+OpenAPI API, Netlify Database (Drizzle), Blobs, Identity, React+Mantine UI, MCP. Spec: docs/plans/2026-11-04-regenerate-beat.md (draft 3, commit e477294; review logs at its end, §13). Line refs are as of e477294; main keeps moving (videos.ts, app.ts, schemas.ts, mcp.ts and the UI pages drifted by 4c573aa), so search by the named symbol when a line is off.
Spec key: 1.2b
Spec section(s): §4.5 'scopeProblems compares semantically', review A1.2

## Background
Byte comparisons of hand-written HTML are fragile: load/save is a parse5 round trip that keeps whitespace text nodes, attribute order and script/style text (src/lib/contract.ts:231-243), so prettier re-indenting frozen beats would look like violations. The run side compares semantically and reports; finalize (task 2.2b) requires bytes, which is fine because render-job writes the splice's bytes.

## Approach
scopeProblems(i: ScopeInput, splice: { html; summary }): string[]
Walk the agent's tree and the splice's, skipping scoped sections:
- drop whitespace-only text nodes; collapse whitespace in text except inside script, style, pre, textarea (trim those);
- compare attributes as a sorted map;
- skip derived values: data-start on beats; data-duration on the root, layers and video slots; the ducking data-automation on a data-va-duck layer.
Name each difference: '<head> changed (a <style> was added)', 'Scene "Opening" changed (its headline text)', 'The music layer's volume changed', 'Root attribute data-va-contract changed', 'A root-level <script> changed'.
Also compare: summary.json cues of other scenes order-insensitively (by beat, textId, text and beat-relative times); other beats' voice.json entries and script.json lines; provider, voice and speed.
Wire it into spliceScoped's step 9 (task 1.2 left putBack: [] behind one call site): putBack = scopeProblems(i, splice). ## Background
New files are fine (every frozen part of the HTML is frozen, so only scoped beats can reference them), but existing files may be used by frozen beats, so they must not change or disappear. Cross-plan: other features append derived files (screen-recording draft 3: assets/recording/plan.json, and for scoped recording steps assets/recording/<step>.cursor.js and assets/recording/<step>.hold.jpg).

## Approach
- scopeFileProblems(parent: Map<path, sha256>, agent: Map<path, sha256>, derived: readonly string[]): string[] — every parent file outside the derived set present and byte-identical in the agent's set; reference files (the narration bus, src/lib/bundle-references.ts isReference) excluded (narration lock covers them); excluded() paths (src/lib/bundle-manifest.ts:28-41: dot folders, feedback/, hydrated assets/media/med_*) never count.

Export registerDerivedFiles(fn) (pushes onto DERIVED_FILES) and derivedFiles(beats, comp): string[] (the union); the screen-recording plan calls registerDerivedFiles from its own module.
- creditsAppendOnly(parentJson, agentJson): existing entries unchanged and in order; new ones may follow.
- Voice checks (re-voice guard rules, src/lib/revoice.ts:110-150): voice.json provider/voice/speed unchanged; entries of unscoped beats unchanged; scoped entries may change or be added (a scoped beat in a voiced video may gain a line); no other beat's entry removed; script.json lines of unscoped beats unchanged; each changed WAV's length matches voice.json (PCM16 24 kHz, (size-44)/2/SAMPLE_RATE within FPS_TOLERANCE). A parent with no voice.json has no assets/voice/ in its archive: skip the voice checks.

## Done when
File, credits and voice rules enforced with plain-words problems; DERIVED_FILES extensible.

## Tests

- a registerDerivedFiles extension entry -> excluded; the registry is reset between tests;

## Approach
In src/lib/run-manifest.ts:
- Type: RunManifest gains scope?: { beats: string[]; stills: { atSec: number; path: string; what: 'before' | 'after'; beat: string }[] } | undefined (the file's existing exactOptionalPropertyTypes style, like bundle.revoice).
- serializeRunManifest (:177, 'Stable bytes'): it lists fields explicitly, so scope is dropped unless added. Spec key: 1.5
Spec section(s): §4.3, §3 gotcha 16, reviews A7, R2

## Background
The run needs the parent as restored (.render/frozen) for check-contract --fix and render-job. Today prepare-run copies it there only for narrated parents (scripts/prepare-run.ts:375-395). Stills: feedbackStills EMPTIES video/feedback/ first (rmSync at :65) and runs last in prepare() (:452-460), so scope stills written earlier would vanish (review R2). The step order is render-engines' (shared rule 5): restore+hydrate, library media, look, recording and scope files; the stills come last with the feedback stills (recommended note for the engines plan: 'feedback and scope stills, last').

## Approach
- Frozen copy, right after the restore: today prepare() copies the restored composition into .render/frozen (FROZEN_DIR, src/lib/revoice.ts:29) only for narrated parents, immediately after restoreArchive/restoreReferences (scripts/prepare-run.ts:386-395) and before library media, so it's the parent exactly as archived. Extend that condition to `narrated || m.scope` (one copy serves both checks; a scoped revision of a narrated parent needs both). Do NOT take the copy later in the step order: library media, look and recording steps write into video/ and the frozen copy must be the parent's archive. Log scope.frozen { parentN, files }.
- scope.json, in the scope step (render-engines' prepare-run order, engines bead va-ed2s.2.7: restore + hydrate, library media, look, recording and scope files, then feedback and scope stills last): write .render/frozen/scope.json { beats, layout: [{ id, label, start, duration }] } with the layout read from the FROZEN index.html (read(load(html)), src/lib/contract.ts:272). check-contract and render-job read the beats from the manifest and the layout from here.
- Stills: extend feedbackStills(root, parentMp4, pins, scopeStills = []) (scripts/prepare-run.ts:63) so ONE call writes pin stills and scope stills from the one downloaded MP4: scope stills at manifest.scope.stills[].path (feedback/scope/<beat>-<what>.jpg), at the manifest's atSec clamped like pins (:72), scaled like pins, no dot; then one feedback/index.json listing pin entries as today ({ still, commentId, timeSec, x, y }) followed by scope entries ({ still, beat, what, atSec }). prepare-run doesn't compute times: the reconciler does (task 2.4), from versions.beats.
- The download: prepare() fetches feedback.video whenever m.feedback is set (:452-460). A scoped manifest with stills: [] and no pins has feedback null (the reconciler decides, parent MP4 over 300 MB), so nothing is downloaded and no stills are made.
- Logs: scope.frozen { parentN, files }, scope.layout { beats: n }, feedback.stills { pins, scope }.

## Done when
Scoped runs get .render/frozen + scope.json; pin and scope stills coexist; no stills when the manifest says none.

## Tests
test/run-manifest.test.ts (where feedbackStills is already tested with ffmpeg on a fixture MP4) and the prepare() tests with an injected fetch:
- pin stills and scope stills from one feedbackStills call: neither deletes the other; both listed in feedback/index.json in that order; scope stills have no red dot (pixel sample at the pin spot equals an unpinned frame).
- A scoped manifest: .render/frozen is byte-equal to the restored archive's files (not including library media hydrated afterwards, nor files a later step writes into video/); scope.json's layout equals read(load(frozen index.html)).
- A scoped revision of a narrated parent: one frozen copy, both narration.locked and scope.frozen logged.
- stills: [] with feedback null: the fake fetch is never called for 'videos'.
- An unscoped revision: no .render/frozen unless narrated (unchanged behaviour).

title: Finalize: server-side scope check (byte equality with the splice, file hashes, MP4 length binding)
description:
Project: video-agent, an open-source Netlify template that turns a prompt into a published MP4 via Netlify Agent Runner runs writing HyperFrames compositions; Hono+OpenAPI API, Netlify Database (Drizzle), Blobs, Identity, React+Mantine UI, MCP. Feature: redo a scene (a scoped revision: pick one or more scenes (beats) of a finished version, say what should change, and get a new version where only those scenes changed; everything else is frozen, spliced back deterministically and checked twice, in the run and in finalize). Spec: docs/plans/2026-11-04-regenerate-beat.md (draft 3, commit e477294; review logs at its end, §13). Line refs are as of e477294; main keeps moving (videos.ts, app.ts, schemas.ts, mcp.ts and the UI pages drifted by 4c573aa), so search by the named symbol when a line is off.
Spec key: 2.2b
Spec section(s): §4.9 point 3 and 'What this guarantees', §0, reviews A2, R4

## Background
The run-side checks are for the agent; this is the guarantee. A run executes the repo's scripts in its own Git checkout (Agent Runners work from Git, README.md:33), so it could change render-job; finalize re-checks on the server. Finalize stores the uploaded archive as is (src/domain/finalize.ts:217), so a semantic-only check would let whitespace-sensitive differences in frozen scenes into the saved composition; render-job writes the splice's bytes and a splice of a splice is a fixed point, so BYTE equality is stricter and honest runs always pass (review R4).

What is guaranteed (spec §0, §4.9, after review R4): the SAVED COMPOSITION. Outside the scope, the uploaded index.html and summary.json are byte-for-byte what splicing the parent produces, and every other existing file is the parent's. The MP4 is trusted like every run's (finalize never derives the MP4 from the archive for any run kind, src/domain/finalize.ts:131-236), bound to the composition by its length (±0.25 s), and the live test checks frozen scenes' frames by SSIM. Script isolation is a heuristic; SSIM is the only pixel check.

## Approach
For a version with scope (version.scope non-null):
- WHEN: after the MP4/poster/GIF/VTT checks and BEFORE any blobs.set (src/domain/finalize.ts:201), using the uploaded archive map task 2.2 reads there.
- Parent archive: parentOutput = store.getOutput(jobId, version.parentN); blobs.get('sources', parentOutput.sourceKey), hash-checked against parentOutput.sha256['source.tar.gz']; readReferences(deps, parentOutput) for its references (their paths join the parent map; the bus bytes are not needed). Missing or mismatched -> Invalid('source_unavailable', 'Version N's saved composition is missing, so this scoped run can't be checked.').
- Both archives parsed with readTarGz(…, SOURCE_READ_LIMITS) (:435-439), never the BUNDLE_LIMITS default (src/lib/tar.ts:12-16, :48).
- The check: scopeCheckFor(version.engine ?? 'hyperframes') (task 1.3) on (parent map, uploaded map, scope.beats). Require problems = [] AND the uploaded index.html and summary.json byte-identical to the returned files. scopeProblems only writes the message; scopeFileProblems runs on file hashes and the voice files; credits.json append-only.
- MP4 binding: |info.durationSec - splice root data-duration| <= 0.25 s, else Invalid('invalid_output', 'The video is X s long but its composition is Y s; …') and log finalize.scope_duration_mismatch.
- Failure: Invalid('invalid_output', `${SCOPE_REFUSED_PREFIX}: ` + first 10 items joined with '; ' (+ 'and N more')). invalid_output, not a new category: the UI already explains it and offers Retry (Video.tsx Retry button, ~:683), and isScopeRefusal() recognizes the message for the retry prompt (2.4) and the UI fallback (3.3).
- Logs: finalize.scope_ok { beats, lengthDelta, ms }, finalize.scope_violated { problems: first 20 }, finalize.scope_duration_mismatch { mp4, composition }.

## Done when
A scoped version can only become ready when its archive is exactly the splice and the MP4 length matches.

## Tests
test/scoped-finalize.test.ts (memory + PGlite; parent and upload archives built from test/fixtures/scope/ with spliceBytes; a fake MP4 probe):
- matching upload -> ready with beats and contract set in the same tx; finalize.scope_ok logged.
- one that changed another scene -> failed invalid_output whose message starts with SCOPE_REFUSED_PREFIX and names the scene; NO blobs written (the fake Blobs records no set for this attempt).
- uploaded index.html semantically equal but byte-different (re-indented frozen scene) -> invalid_output (finalize requires bytes).
- an existing file changed or deleted; credits.json entry removed -> invalid_output naming the file.
- parent archive missing; parent archive hash mismatch -> source_unavailable.
- MP4 0.5 s off the splice's length -> invalid_output and finalize.scope_duration_mismatch; 0.2 s off -> ready.
- parent archive over 50 MB but under SOURCE_READ_LIMITS -> read fine.
- a narrated parent: lockedLength applies (a length change is refused) and the bus reference path counts as present.
- an unscoped revision: no parent archive read (the fake Blobs records no get of the parent's source).

description:

Spec key: 2.3

## Background
A scoped revision is a revision in every other way (history, attempts, retries, comments, webhooks, credits), so it's one optional field on POST /api/v1/videos/{id}/versions rather than a new endpoint: one code path for REST, MCP, SDK and CLI. reviseVideo (src/domain/videos.ts, ~:407-495 at 4c573aa) runs inside deps.store.tx: checks version:create, refuses while another version is unfinished (hasUnfinished), picks the parent, snapshots comments (snapshotFeedback, owner/admin via video:incorporate), consumes a plan, inherits media/sound/voice-over, inserts a queued version and attempt.

## Approach
ReviseInput gains scope?: { beats: string[] }. When present:
- Feature: the same features helper /api/v1/config uses must list scoped_revision, else 400 invalid_request 'This server can't redo single scenes yet.' (task 2.6 adds the string; until then reviseVideo refuses a scope even if a caller sends one).
- Engine: the parent's engine must have capabilities.scopedRevision (render-engines; HyperFrames only in v1); else 409 not_editable 'Version 3 was made with Remotion, which can't redo scenes one by one yet. Revise the whole video instead.'
- fromVersion REQUIRED (400 'Say which version the scenes are from (fromVersion): scene ids belong to one version').
- Parent ready and contract === 1, else 409 not_editable 'Version 3 can't be edited scene by scene (it doesn't keep the editing contract). Revise the whole video instead.'
- BEFORE the transaction, when the parent's beats are null: fillBeats (task 2.5; visibility check first). Inside the tx, read versions.beats.
- beats: 1-20 ids /^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{0,40}$/, de-duplicated; each a beat of the parent (unknown -> 400 invalid_request naming them and listing real ones with labels: 'There's no scene "feature". This video's scenes: intro (Opening), features (Features), …'); not every beat (400 'That's every scene: revise the whole video instead (leave out scope)' — refused, not silently widened, so a script that thinks it froze something finds out); not va-hold and not the last real beat when the version ends with va-hold (400 'This scene ends the video under your recorded narration and holds its last frame; redo it with a whole-video revision', owner Q7).
- Put the pure beat rules (count, format, known ids, not every beat, held frame) in scopeRules(parentBeats, scoped) in src/lib/scope.ts returning { beats (parent order) } or a { code, message } refusal; reviseVideo maps it to ApiError, and local mode (task 4.1c) reuses it so both refuse with the same words.
- Refused combinations: planId, durationSec, sound, voiceover (400, one message per field); look -> 400 look_not_allowed (defined by the Looks plan). Allowed: commentIds (owner/admin rule unchanged), mediaIds, webhookUrl, Idempotency-Key.
- Store versions.scope with the beats de-duplicated and in the PARENT's order (not the request's), so the manifest, the prompt and the DTO are deterministic whatever order a client sends; targetDurationSec inherited from the parent; finalize length notice unchanged.
- New ErrorCode not_editable (409) in src/lib/errors.ts (add to the ErrorCode union and STATUS map). look_not_allowed comes from the Looks plan; if it isn't in ErrorCode yet when this lands, that's a cross-plan ordering bug (Looks phase 2 merges first): stop and report rather than adding it here.
- Logs: video.revise_requested gains scope: beats.
Permissions (§6): same as revising (version:create: Admin, Creator); a Creator can redo scenes of someone else's video, adding a version they author. Private videos stay private. Credits like any run.
Needs: render-engines phase 1 (capabilities on versions.engine); Looks plan (look field + look_not_allowed code); cli-and-sdk phase 1.2 (features).

Every rule and message enforced; scope stored; no Blobs I/O inside the tx.

- allowed: commentIds as owner/admin (snapshotted as today); commentIds as a Creator on someone else's video -> forbidden, the same request without commentIds -> ok; mediaIds; webhookUrl.
- stored: versions.scope in parent order and de-duplicated (['outro','intro','intro'] -> ['intro','outro']).
- idempotent replay through the route with the same Idempotency-Key returns the same version and creates no second attempt.
- the lazy fill happens before the transaction: with parent beats null, fillBeats runs, and the fake store records no Blobs call while a tx is open; a private video the caller can't see -> 404 with no Blobs call.
