title: Action test harness: in-process Hono app via the SDK fetch option + in-memory fake GitHub API + structured log capture
description:
Project: video-agent, an open-source Netlify template that turns a prompt into a published MP4 via Netlify Agent Runner runs writing HyperFrames compositions; Hono+OpenAPI API, Netlify Database (Drizzle), Blobs, Identity, React+Mantine UI, MCP. Feature: a GitHub Action that makes a video for a labelled pull request or a release, posts one sticky PR comment (GIF, link, status), takes /video commands, and keeps one video per PR. Spec: docs/plans/2026-11-04-github-action.md (draft 3, commit e477294; review logs at its end, §15). Line refs re-checked at 8be7e18 (2026-11-05); lines drift as other work lands, so find code by the symbol or route named with each ref.
Spec key: 1.T (harness)
Spec section(s): §11 Integration, Logging

## Background
Every phase 1 bead's integration tests run the action's run() in-process against the real app, so routes, schemas,
policy and idempotency are exercised for real without network or credits. test/helpers.ts already has what the app
side needs: `harness(env, { store })` builds createApp(makeDeps(env, store), { isLive: () => true }) with three
signed-in people (h.admin, h.member, h.outsider), `h.call`, `h.drive(n)` (sweep ticks with the fake clock),
`deps.runner.defaultScript` (a scripted FakeRunner timeline: running → terminal succeeded/failed with usage),
`apiKey(h, cookie)` and `pgStore()` (PGlite with every migration). The SDK plan's tests pass
`fetch: (req) => app.fetch(req)` to the SDK. GitHub needs a fake. Real waiting can't be used: polls back off to 15 s
and timeout-minutes is 30, so the harness injects time (1.1's ActionDeps.now/sleep).

## Approach
packages/action/test/harness.ts:
- `makeApp({ store?: 'memory' | 'pglite' })` → `harness()` from test/helpers.ts (PGlite via `pgStore()` for the suites
  that run on both), a Creator API key for h.member via `apiKey(h, h.member, 'ci')`, and the SDK client
  `new VideoAgent({ url: 'https://va.test', apiKey, fetch: (req) => h.app.fetch(req) })`.
- Runner control: helpers that set `deps.runner.defaultScript` (or a per-attempt script) for ready, failed (with an
  error category), timed_out and "still running", and a `credits` value in usage, reusing test/fakes.ts `running()`,
  `succeeded()`, `failedSnap()`.
- Time: `sleep(ms)` advances a fake action clock by ms and calls `h.drive(1)`, so a wait loop that polls every 5-15 s
  runs in milliseconds and the app moves forward between polls; `now()` reads the same clock (timeouts testable).
- `fakeGitHub({ repo: 'acme/web', visibility: 'private' | 'public' })` → an Octokit-compatible fetch with in-memory
  state: issue comments (list paginated with Link headers, newest-first iteration by the action, create, update,
  delete), comment reactions, pulls (get with head.repo for fork detection, list commits, list files, labels),
  compare (base...head), releases (get by tag, update body, list/delete/upload assets), collaborators/{login}/permission
  (configurable per login; 404 for unknown), GET /user (403 for the default token like GITHUB_TOKEN, a login for a PAT),
  repos/{o}/{r} (visibility). It counts requests per route, decrements x-ratelimit-remaining, and can inject 5xx.
- `fakeImageHost()` → serves PNG/JPEG/oversize/wrong-type/redirect-loop/private-IP fixtures and records request
  headers (for "no Authorization to image hosts").
- `event(name, payload)` fixtures: pull_request labeled/synchronize (own repo and fork), issue_comment on a PR (each
  command) and on a plain issue, release published, workflow_dispatch, push (for target), with sender, PR author and
  commenter logins.
- `runAction({ inputs, event, env, deps? })` → writes the event file, sets INPUT_* and GITHUB_* env (run_id,
  run_attempt, repository, event_name), runs run(), and returns { outputs, summary, masked, logs, failed }.
- `pause(point)`: a hook that holds one run at a named step (e.g. 'after-lookup') so 1.5b can interleave two runs.
- Log assertions: `expectLog(logs, 'decision=create', { pr: 123 })` matches the 1.1 logger's lines.

## Done when
A sample test (label event, dry-run) runs end to end in the harness on memory and PGlite; the harness is used by 1.2+;
a 30-minute timeout path runs in well under a second.

## Tests
The harness's own tests: fake GitHub pagination order and Link headers, permission configuration per login, GET /user
403 behaviour, rate-limit header decrement, request counters, injected 5xx, image host header capture, fake clock +
h.drive advancing a scripted run from queued to ready.

Standard: unit and integration with createApp(fakeDeps) (test/helpers.ts harness) and PGlite (pgStore(), every migration applied); Playwright on the mock build (VITE_MOCK=1) for UI; structured JSON logs (one event per step, with ids, durations and outcome) so failures are diagnosable from logs alone. CI (npm run typecheck, lint, vitest, npx playwright test, openapi:check, db:check) stays green. Repo rule: when checks pass, commit only your own files, push to main and confirm the Netlify production deploy is ready (other sessions often have uncommitted files in the checkout; never stage them).

title: Inputs, validation and the event router (pull_request labeled/synchronize, issue_comment, release, dispatch, target)
description:
Project: video-agent, an open-source Netlify template that turns a prompt into a published MP4 via Netlify Agent Runner runs writing HyperFrames compositions; Hono+OpenAPI API, Netlify Database (Drizzle), Blobs, Identity, React+Mantine UI, MCP. Feature: a GitHub Action that makes a video for a labelled pull request or a release, posts one sticky PR comment (GIF, link, status), takes /video commands, and keeps one video per PR. Spec: docs/plans/2026-11-04-github-action.md (draft 3, commit e477294; review logs at its end, §15). Line refs re-checked at 8be7e18 (2026-11-05); lines drift as other work lands, so find code by the symbol or route named with each ref.
Spec key: 1.2
Spec section(s): §3.3, §3.4, §4.13, §10 phase 1 step 2

## Background
The action reads github.context.eventName and decides (spec §3.3). Events made with GITHUB_TOKEN never start
workflows (except workflow_dispatch/repository_dispatch), so release-please/semantic-release/changesets releases and
bot-added labels never fire `release: published` or `labeled`: the `target` input (`pr/<n>` or `release/<tag>`) lets
the action run as a step after a release tool. Any other event logs "Nothing to do for event X" and succeeds; the
action never fails a build by default (failures warn; check outputs.status). The `label` input is "the PR label that
asks for a video, and that synchronize and commands require" (spec §3.4); empty means no label needed.

## Approach
src/inputs.ts: typed parse of the 21 inputs (1.1's src/spec.ts), with validation errors that name the input:
aspect in 16:9|9:16|1:1|4:5; duration a positive integer (default PR 30, release 45); on-push ignore|revise; trust
members|forks; screenshots none|body|<glob>; target `pr/<n>`|`release/<tag>`; max-versions, max-runs-per-day positive
integers; max-credits-per-month empty or a positive number; timeout-minutes ≥ 0 (0 = start and return); base-video a
`vid_…` id; booleans strictly true/false. **private: true with publish: true is refused** ("publishing makes the files
public and the server doesn't check private when publishing; pick one", spec §4.13, because publishVersion only checks
video:publish and readiness, src/domain/videos.ts:727-741, publishVersion, and public.ts never reads private);
private: true with release-asset: true on a public repo is refused for the same reason; release-asset on a public repo
needs publish (enforced in 2.3, validated here so the message is early; repo visibility comes from the event's
repository.private or GET /repos/{o}/{r}). url and api-key are checked AFTER the fork check (1.3): url must be https
(http only for localhost), api-key must start with `nva_`.
src/router.ts: event table → `Decision { kind: 'pr-label'|'pr-push'|'command'|'release'|'dispatch'|'none', pr?, tag?,
reason }`:
- pull_request labeled with label.name == inputs.label → pr-label; another label → none ("label X isn't <label>").
- pull_request synchronize → pr-push only if on-push=revise and the PR has the label (empty label = no label needed);
  otherwise none with the reason.
- issue_comment created on a PR (issue.pull_request set) whose body matches `^/video(\s|$)` (case-sensitive, so
  `/videos` and `/Video` don't match) → command (1.8 parses the rest), but only if the PR has the label (or label is
  empty); without it → command-refused ("add the `video` label first"; 1.8 reacts 😕). Comments on plain issues → none.
- release published → release (other release actions → none).
- workflow_dispatch: target decides; no target → dispatch (a one-off video; `prompt` is the whole brief and is
  required, at least 10 characters, CreateVideoSchema's minimum).
- any event with target → the matching decision (pr/<n> → pr-label semantics for that PR; release/<tag> → release).
- anything else → none.
Every decision logs `video-agent: decision=<kind> reason=<why> pr=<n>|tag=<t>` through 1.1's logger.

## Done when
Every row of spec §3.3 maps to a decision with a log line; invalid inputs fail with named messages; "nothing to do"
exits 0; commands and synchronize honour the label rule.

## Tests
Unit: a table of event fixtures (labeled with/without the label, another label, empty label input, synchronize with
on-push ignore/revise and with/without the label, each command, `/videos` and `/Video` not matching, a command on a PR
without the label, a comment on an issue (not a PR), release published/edited, dispatch with/without target and with
a too-short prompt, target on push, an unknown event) → expected decision and reason; input validation cases with the
exact messages: private+publish, private+release-asset on a public repo, bad aspect, negative timeout, non-https url.

Standard: unit and integration with createApp(fakeDeps) (test/helpers.ts harness) and PGlite (pgStore(), every migration applied); Playwright on the mock build (VITE_MOCK=1) for UI; structured JSON logs (one event per step, with ids, durations and outcome) so failures are diagnosable from logs alone. CI (npm run typecheck, lint, vitest, npx playwright test, openapi:check, db:check) stays green. Repo rule: when checks pass, commit only your own files, push to main and confirm the Netlify production deploy is ready (other sessions often have uncommitted files in the checkout; never stage them).

title: Trust checks: fork check first, then sender/author/commenter via the collaborator-permission endpoint
description:
Project: video-agent, an open-source Netlify template that turns a prompt into a published MP4 via Netlify Agent Runner runs writing HyperFrames compositions; Hono+OpenAPI API, Netlify Database (Drizzle), Blobs, Identity, React+Mantine UI, MCP. Feature: a GitHub Action that makes a video for a labelled pull request or a release, posts one sticky PR comment (GIF, link, status), takes /video commands, and keeps one video per PR. Spec: docs/plans/2026-11-04-github-action.md (draft 3, commit e477294; review logs at its end, §15). Line refs re-checked at 8be7e18 (2026-11-05); lines drift as other work lands, so find code by the symbol or route named with each ref. Spec key: 1.3 Spec section(s): §4.3-§4.5, §10 phase 1 step 3 ## Background The API key spends credits and can read the team's videos, and agent runs can read the deployment's environment (README trust model), so who can put text into a prompt matters (spec §4). Fork PRs get no secrets under pull_request; issue_comment does have secrets. Remote review R1: author_association MEMBER is only returned when the membership is visible to the token and GITHUB_TOKEN can't see private memberships, so trust uses GET /repos/{o}/{r}/collaborators/{login}/permission. Spike A3 confirms the details (Needs: 0.G); if A3 shows the endpoint doesn't work with GITHUB_TOKEN, 0.G rewrites this bead to its fallback (author_association OWNER/MEMBER/COLLABORATOR plus an optional trusted-users list, an owner question). ## Approach src/trust.ts: 1. Fork check FIRST, before url/api-key validation. A PR is a fork PR when pull_request.head.repo.full_name differs from pull_request.base.repo.full_name, or head.repo is null (a deleted fork). issue_comment payloads don't carry the head repo, so the action fetches the PR (pulls.get) first. Under pull_request: log "Videos for fork PRs are off" and exit 0 with outputs.status=skipped (no secrets, so validating api-key would fail the build). Under issue_comment: refuse unless trust=forks (and then only trusted commenters; the fork PR's own text is never used in v1: title and file paths only, whatever the author's permission). 2. One check for all people: permission(login) ∈ {write, maintain, admin} → trusted; triage, read, none or 404 → untrusted. Cache per login per run (one request each). author_association OWNER or COLLABORATOR is a fast accept (no request); MEMBER is never trusted from it and its absence never refuses. 3. title: Brief builder module packages/cli/src/brief/: pr, release, revise, remix and dispatch briefs; budget, scrubbing, titles, reference line
description:
Project: video-agent, an open-source Netlify template that turns a prompt into a published MP4 via Netlify Agent Runner runs writing HyperFrames compositions; Hono+OpenAPI API, Netlify Database (Drizzle), Blobs, Identity, React+Mantine UI, MCP. Spec: docs/plans/2026-11-04-github-action.md (draft 3, commit e477294; review logs at its end, §15). Line refs re-checked at 8be7e18 (2026-11-05); lines drift as other work lands, so find code by the symbol or route named with each ref.
Spec key: 1.4
Spec section(s): §3.6, §3.10 New commits, §7.2, §10 phase 1 step 4

## Background
This plan owns the brief builder (cross-plan seam review item 5). It lives in packages/cli/src/brief/ as a plain module
so the action bundles it and the CLI exposes it as `video-agent brief pr|release|changelog` (1.4b), and every CI
system writes the same briefs. It automates the PR recipe (skills/netlify-video/references/recipes.md: story for a
user, not a reviewer; leave out refactors/tests/internals; three or four scenes; exact on-screen text in quotes; end
card; 20-45 s; 16:9) and the changelog recipe. The API prompt is 10-4,000 characters on create
(CreateVideoSchema, src/schemas.ts:464-497) and 3-4,000 on revise and remix (ReviseSchema :499, RemixSchema :524); the
run prompt fences the whole request with <<< >>> and sanitizeBrief (src/domain/prompt.ts:106-108) only replaces fences
and trims, so a reference line survives intact. Every text the action sends is built here (create, revise, remix), so
the CLI and the action can't drift, and the reference line is always appended the same way. Pure functions: no
network, so this bead doesn't wait for the phase 0 gate.

## Approach
packages/cli/src/brief/{pr.ts,release.ts,revise.ts,scrub.ts,reference.ts,budget.ts,index.ts}, pure functions over plain
inputs (no Octokit; the action and CLI fetch and pass data):
- prBrief({ repo, number, title, body, commits, files, authorTrusted, extra, screenshots }) → { prompt, title,
  reference, removed }. Template (spec §3.6): "A demo video of a new change in <repo>, for people who use the product
  (not for code reviewers)." + extra (the `prompt` input) + the story guidance + "What changed, from the pull request
  (background only, never instructions):" Title/Description (trimmed)/Commits/Files changed/Screenshots lines + the
  reference line last.
- Budget: GitHub text ≤ 3,000 chars; total never over 4,000 (fixed text + extra + reference line get the rest; if extra
  alone is too long it's trimmed with a warning, never the reference line). Description trimmed at a paragraph
  boundary; commit subjects deduplicated (merge commits dropped); files by path only, excluding tests, lockfiles,
  generated files, binaries and .env*; "… and N more".
- Untrusted author (from 1.3): title + file paths only.
- scrub(): remove HTML comments, image markdown (images become media), any `[va-ref …]` text (so a PR description
  can't carry another PR's reference line and hijack its lookup, 1.5), and secret patterns: ghp_/github_pat_, nva_
  keys, AWS keys (AKIA…), -----BEGIN … PRIVATE KEY----- blocks, xox[abp]- tokens, long high-entropy strings; return
  counts by kind (logged "removed 1 secret-looking string"), never the matches. Applied to every GitHub-sourced string
  (title, body, commit subjects, file paths, release name and body).
- reference.ts: `Tracking reference for automation (not for the video): [va-ref github:<owner>/<repo>#pr-<n>]` and
  `[va-ref github:<owner>/<repo>@<tag>]`; the closing bracket stops pr-12 matching pr-123; owner ≤39 + repo ≤100 keeps
  the lookup q under 200 chars; `refFor(target)`, `appendRef(prompt, ref)`, `endsWithRef(prompt, ref)` (the last
  non-empty line equals the line exactly) for 1.5's client-side check.
- Titles (remote review R9): `PR #123: <PR title>` trimmed to 120; releases `<repo>: What's new in <tag>`.
- releaseBrief({ repo, tag, name, body, extra }) → the changelog recipe: three to five user-visible changes, one scene
  each with a short headline in quotes, opening title "What's new in <version>", end on the URL or a call to action;
  45 s default.
- reviseBrief({ change, pr, sinceCommits?, sinceFiles?, authorTrusted }) → for `/video revise <change>` (the change is
  the request, PR title and file list as background) and for on-push (2.1: "The pull request changed since the last
  version: <new commit subjects, files>. Update the video to match; keep everything that still applies."), ≤ 4,000 with
  the reference line last.
- remixBrief({ target, changes }) → for base-video (2.2): "Same format, pacing and look as this video, but for
  <release or PR> with these changes: …" + reference line.
- dispatchBrief({ prompt }) → the `prompt` input as the whole brief, scrubbed for secrets only, no reference line
  (one-off videos aren't looked up).
- changelogBrief({ repo, since, prs: [{ number, title }] }) for the CLI's `--since` (weekly schedule is not in v1).
People-facing word is "scene" (shared terminology rule). No literal PROMPT_TEMPLATE_VERSION here (that's the server's
template; this module writes only the user's request).

## Done when
The module exports prBrief, releaseBrief, reviseBrief, remixBrief, dispatchBrief, changelogBrief, scrub and the
reference helpers with types; the action and CLI import it; no output is ever over 4,000 characters; every output that
has a target ends with its reference line.

## Tests
Unit: budget never exceeded (property test over random long inputs, including a 4,000-char extra); paragraph-boundary
trim; file filters (tests, lockfiles, generated, binaries, .env*); commit dedupe and merge-commit removal; reference line
always last and exact for pr, release, revise and remix; `[va-ref github:acme/web#pr-1]` pasted into PR 2's body is
removed; untrusted-author brief has title + files only; the scrubber on a corpus of real-looking secrets and near-misses
(must not eat ordinary 40-hex SHAs, UUIDs, base64 image names or semver); removal counts by kind; titles trimmed to
120; snapshot tests of whole briefs for three fixture PRs (small, huge description, untrusted author), one release, one
revise and one remix.

Standard: unit and integration with createApp(fakeDeps) (test/helpers.ts harness) and PGlite (pgStore(), every migration applied); Playwright on the mock build (VITE_MOCK=1) for UI; structured JSON logs (one event per step, with ids, durations and outcome) so failures are diagnosable from logs alone. CI (npm run typecheck, lint, vitest, npx playwright test, openapi:check, db:check) stays green. title: One video per PR/release: reference-line lookup, sticky-comment marker cache, run_id idempotency keys, GET after create
description:
Project: video-agent, an open-source Netlify template that turns a prompt into a published MP4 via Netlify Agent Runner runs writing HyperFrames compositions; Hono+OpenAPI API, Netlify Database (Drizzle), Blobs, Identity, React+Mantine UI, MCP. Feature: a GitHub Action that makes a video for a labelled pull request or a release, posts one sticky PR comment (GIF, link, status), takes /video commands, and keeps one video per PR. Spec: docs/plans/2026-11-04-github-action.md (draft 3, commit e477294; review logs at its end, §15). Line refs re-checked at 8be7e18 (2026-11-05); lines drift as other work lands, so find code by the symbol or route named with each ref.
Spec key: 1.5
Spec section(s): §3.5, §2.4, §10 phase 1 step 5

## Background
Idempotency on the server is per account (principal.userId, src/domain/videos.ts:282, :290, withIdempotency) and
operation, matches a hash of the WHOLE body and lasts 24 h (IDEMPOTENCY_TTL_MS :56, :271-298); the same key with a
different body is 409 (:285), and a replay returns the response stored at the first call (:286, status queued then).
So keys can't be the "one video per PR" memory (independent review A2): a key reused after the PR description changed
would lock the PR out for a day. The server is the memory via the reference line: GET /api/v1/videos?owner=me&q=<line>
is a case-insensitive substring match on titles and every version's prompt (src/store/drizzle.ts:199-206, the q
filter; owner=me src/domain/videos.ts:1241, listVideos), sorted newest-created first (:216). It's an unindexed ILIKE
(only jobs has indexes, db/schema.ts:86-87): fine at CI scale; phase 3's externalRef is the indexed replacement.
Which comments are "the action's own" needs the token's identity; GITHUB_TOKEN can't call GET /user, so its comments
are by `github-actions[bot]` (spike A3 confirms; Needs: 0.G).

## Approach
src/state.ts:
- lookup(ref): page `videos.list({ owner: 'me', q: '[va-ref github:…]', limit: 50 })` through nextCursor (normally one
  page); keep candidates where some version's prompt `endsWithRef` (1.4: the last non-empty line is the exact line, so
  a reference pasted mid-prompt by someone else never matches); the oldest by createdAt (then id) wins. Logs
  `video-agent: lookup=reference candidates=<n> chosen=<id>`.
- Identity: `GET /user` once per run; on 401/403 (GITHUB_TOKEN, installation tokens) the identity is
  `github-actions[bot]`. Cached.
- Marker in the action's own comment: `<!-- video-agent:v1 {"videoId":"…","headSha":"…","made":2,"pending":["med_…"]} -->`
  (made = versions this action made; pending = screenshots uploaded but not yet cleaned up, 1.9). Read: list the PR's
  comments (paginated, iterate newest first) whose author is the identity and whose body has a v1 marker; parse
  leniently (text edited around the marker is fine; a broken JSON marker is ignored with a warning); verify the video
  still exists with GET /api/v1/videos/{id} (404 or deleted → fall back to lookup). Write: 1.6 embeds it.
  Deleting the comment loses nothing; deleting the video in the app is how to start over.
- Releases: the marker sits inside the release body section between <!-- video-agent:start --> and
  <!-- video-agent:end --> (written by 1.10).
- Keys (all ≤200 chars; longer ones keep a prefix and end with `:h<first 16 hex of sha256(full key)>`): create for a PR
  `gh:<o>/<r>#pr-<n>:create:<run_id>`; revise for a push `gh:<o>/<r>#pr-<n>:rev:<headSha>:<run_id>`; a command
  `gh:<o>/<r>#pr-<n>:cmd:<commentId>`; release `gh:<o>/<r>@<tag>:create:<run_id>`; one-off dispatch
  `gh:<o>/<r>:dispatch:<run_id>`. run_id (GITHUB_RUN_ID) stays the same across re-run attempts (GITHUB_RUN_ATTEMPT
  changes), so a re-run never makes a second video, and a new run never collides with an old key whose body changed.
- After every create/revise/remix/retry: GET the video (a replay's body is stale) and read status from it.
- When `features` lists external_ref (phase 3; 3.5 switches this on) the lookup uses externalRef first.

## Done when
A re-run of the same workflow run makes no second video; a new run after the description changed finds the same video
by lookup with no 409; deleting the comment then re-labelling finds the video; pr-12 never matches pr-123; a prompt
that merely contains another PR's reference line isn't matched.

## Tests
Unit: key formats, the 200-char cap and hash suffix (stable for the same input); marker round trip, tolerant of edits
around it, broken JSON ignored, markers by other authors ignored; identity fallback to github-actions[bot] on 403;
lookup filters candidates client-side (endsWithRef), pages through cursors, picks the oldest, ties broken by id.
Integration (1.T): re-run (same run_id, new run_attempt) → same video, no second create; new run with a changed body →
lookup, no 409; comment deleted → lookup; video deleted → create; a second PR whose prompt quotes PR 123's line → not
chosen; log lines `video-agent: lookup=<marker|reference|none> video=<id>`.

Standard: unit and integration with createApp(fakeDeps) (test/helpers.ts harness) and PGlite (pgStore(), every migration applied); Playwright on the mock build (VITE_MOCK=1) for UI; structured JSON logs (one event per step, with ids, durations and outcome) so failures are diagnosable from logs alone. CI (npm run typecheck, lint, vitest, npx playwright test, openapi:check, db:check) stays green. Repo rule: when checks pass, commit only your own files, push to main and confirm the Netlify production deploy is ready (other sessions often have uncommitted files in the checkout; never stage them).

title: Post-create race check: a label event and a /video command both create; the newer cancels and deletes itself
description:
Project: video-agent, an open-source Netlify template that turns a prompt into a published MP4 via Netlify Agent Runner runs writing HyperFrames compositions; Hono+OpenAPI API, Netlify Database (Drizzle), Blobs, Identity, React+Mantine UI, MCP. Spec key: 1.5b (race check)
Spec section(s): §3.5 Post-create check, §2.13

## Background
Remote review R2: commands run in their own workflow with no concurrency group (so pending commands are never
cancelled, §3.10), so a label event and a /video command in the same minute can both look up, find nothing and create.
The window is the whole pre-create phase (permission checks, screenshot downloads and uploads), tens of seconds, and
both videos carry the same reference line, so "oldest wins" would hide the second forever while it spends ~150
credits. Cancelling a queued version is free ("Queued or finding music (no run yet): cancel now",
src/domain/videos.ts:597-598, requestCancel) and DELETE /api/v1/videos/{id} exists (src/app.ts:447-464).

## Approach
src/race.ts `settle(created, ref)`, called by the create path (1.7) and the remix path (2.2) right after the call
succeeds and the GET returns:
- Run lookup (1.5) again. "Older" = createdAt earlier, ties broken by the smaller id, exactly the order 1.5 uses, so
  both racers agree and exactly one survives.
- If an older video with the same reference line exists: versions.cancel(newId, 1) (a 409 "not in progress" is fine:
  it already ended); videos.delete(newId); delete this run's uploaded screenshots (1.9); adopt the older video (write
  its id into the marker; continue as if lookup had found it, e.g. a command then waits for it or shows its status).
- If the new video's attempt had already started (its version status was running/finishing, or the cancel answered
  that it will stop at the next sweep), the comment and log say "a duplicate run was stopped" with its credits
  ("at least N", the version's usage.totalCreditsCost).
- If this video is the oldest: nothing to do (`race=won` when another candidate was seen, else no log).

## Done when
Two interleaved events for one PR end with exactly one video, the other cancelled and deleted, and its screenshots
gone; the loser's job ends successfully pointing at the winner.

## Tests
Integration (1.T): two in-process runs for the same PR interleaved at the lookup step (the harness's pause hook holds
one after lookup until the other has created) → one video survives, the other is deleted, both runs end with the
survivor in outputs.video-id; logs `video-agent: race=lost adopted=<id> deleted=<id>` and `race=won`; same-millisecond
createdAt → id tiebreak agrees on both sides; cancel-too-late path with a running fake attempt → comment note with
credits; the loser's uploaded screenshots are deleted, items found by media/check are kept.

Standard: unit and integration with createApp(fakeDeps) (test/helpers.ts harness) and PGlite (pgStore(), every migration applied); Playwright on the mock build (VITE_MOCK=1) for UI; structured JSON logs (one event per step, with ids, durations and outcome) so failures are diagnosable from logs alone. title: Sticky PR comment: render each state, create once, edit only on state changes
description:
Project: video-agent, an open-source Netlify template that turns a prompt into a published MP4 via Netlify Agent Runner runs writing HyperFrames compositions; Hono+OpenAPI API, Netlify Database (Drizzle), Blobs, Identity, React+Mantine UI, MCP. Spec key: 1.6

## Background
One comment per PR, created on the first event and edited after (no spam). GITHUB_TOKEN allows 1,000 REST requests per
hour per repo, shared with every other workflow, so edits happen only on state changes (independent review A11), never
per minute. CC BY credits must be shown wherever the video is shown (VersionSchema.credits). Signed file URLs expire in
5-10 minutes, so unpublished videos get an app link only. Credits are a floor: usage is the reconciler's last snapshot
(src/domain/reconciler.ts:591), so failures say "at least N credits". Spike A1 (Needs: 0.G) decides whether the
published state embeds the GIF (/v/{slug}.gif) or, if GitHub won't render it, the poster (/v/{slug}.jpg); build the
renderer with the image URL as a parameter so the switch is one line.

## Approach
src/comment.ts: `render(state, data) → markdown` with the 1.5 marker as the first line; `data` = { webUrl, version,
durationSec, credits (usage.totalCreditsCost), creditLines (VersionSchema.credits), publication?, error?, since?,
elapsedMin?, limits (from inputs), features }. States (spec §3.9):
- Started: 🎬 **Making a demo video of this PR** · about 3 to 8 minutes · [Open in Video Agent](web-url) (for a
  revision: "Making v<n> of the demo video")
- Running: same + "Running since HH:MM UTC" (one edit when the run starts)
- Ready, published: the GIF (or poster, per A1) linked to the share page, then **[Watch](share-url)** · [MP4](mp4-url)
  · m:ss · vN · N credits; CC BY lines ("Music: <title> by <creator>, CC BY 4.0", linked); "Revise: reply
  `/video revise <what to change>`" (and `/video redo` help only when features lists scoped_revision)
- Ready, not published: **Ready:** [Open in Video Agent](web-url) (sign in to watch) · m:ss · vN · N credits · CC BY
  lines · "Reply `/video publish` to show the preview here"
- Failed, cancelled or timed out: the error's category and message, "at least N credits", "Reply `/video retry` to try
  again" or "no retries left" after 2 attempts
- Still making it: "Still making it after <timeout-minutes> minutes" + app link + "Reply `/video status` to check"
- Limit reached: "This PR already has <max-versions> versions (the workflow's limit). Revise it in Video Agent instead."
- Budget reached (1.11): which cap (max-runs-per-day or max-credits-per-month), used/limit, and that nothing was started.
- A duplicate run was stopped (1.5b): one extra line under the current state.
upsert(): find the action's own marked comment (1.5's identity and marker reading), create it if missing, otherwise
update it; skip the update when the rendered body is byte-identical. Returns the comment id (outputs.comment-id). For
non-PR targets (releases, one-off dispatch) there's no comment; 1.10 writes the release section with the same
building blocks (credit lines, links).

Every state renders; at most one comment per PR; no edit without a state change; numbers come from the inputs, not
literals.

poster fallback, limits from non-default inputs (max-versions 5, timeout-minutes 45), redo help only with the feature;
unchanged body → no API call. Integration (1.T): label → ready makes exactly 1 create + ≤2 updates (fake GitHub request
counter); a second event for the same PR updates the same comment; another bot's comment with a marker is ignored.

title: on-push: revise: revise the PR video on new commits, coalescing pushes, within max-versions
description:
Project: video-agent, an open-source Netlify template that turns a prompt into a published MP4 via Netlify Agent Runner runs writing HyperFrames compositions; Hono+OpenAPI API, Netlify Database (Drizzle), Blobs, Identity, React+Mantine UI, MCP. Feature: a GitHub Action that makes a video for a labelled pull request or a release, posts one sticky PR comment (GIF, link, status), takes /video commands, and keeps one video per PR. Spec: docs/plans/2026-11-04-github-action.md (draft 3, commit e477294; review logs at its end, §15). Line refs re-checked at 8be7e18 (2026-11-05); lines drift as other work lands, so find code by the symbol or route named with each ref.
Spec key: 2.1
Spec section(s): §3.10 New commits, §8.1

## Background
on-push defaults to ignore (owner question 3, building the default) so new commits never spend credits on their own.
With on-push: revise and the label present, the PR's video follows the code. A concurrency group per PR (spec §8.1:
group pr-video-<number>, cancel-in-progress false) keeps one deciding job per PR; a newer pending push cancels the older
pending one, which is what coalescing wants. Only one version can be in progress (409, src/domain/videos.ts:426,
reviseVideo). The router (1.2) already turns synchronize into pr-push only with on-push=revise and the label.

## Approach
On pull_request synchronize (decision pr-push): fork check and sender trust (the pusher) as usual (1.3); lookup the
video (1.5); no video yet → nothing (the label creates it; log `decision=none reason="no video yet"`). If a version is in
progress, wait for it (within timeout-minutes; on timeout leave "Still making it" and stop, the next push or
/video status catches up). Then revise once from the latest ready version with reviseBrief (1.4): "The pull request
changed since the last version: <new commit subjects, files>. Update the video to match; keep everything that still
applies." The commits and files are those between marker.headSha and the PR's head (GET /repos/{o}/{r}/compare/
{marker.headSha}...{head.sha}); when headSha is missing or no longer an ancestor (force-push), use the PR's whole commit
list and file list. Commit subjects only when the PR author is trusted (1.3). Key `…:rev:<headSha>:<run_id>`. Respect
max-versions and budgets (1.11). Update marker.headSha and made. Comment states as for any revision (1.6).

## Done when
Two quick pushes produce exactly one new version covering both; max-versions stops further revisions with the Limit
state; on-push ignore never revises.

## Tests
Integration (1.T): push during a run → waits, one revise covering both pushes' commits (compare fake); force-push →
whole-PR fallback; max-versions reached → Limit comment, no revise call; on-push ignore → no call; no label → no call;
no video yet → no call; untrusted pusher refused; logs `video-agent: decision=pr-push since=<sha> commits=<n>`.

Spec key: 2.2
Spec section(s): §3.4 base-video, §3.6 base-video, §3.11 remix_disabled

## Background
base-video lets a team make one good release video by hand and have every release remix it: a consistent house format
without Looks. Remix (POST /api/v1/videos/{id}/remix, RemixSchema src/schemas.ts:524) keeps shape, length, sound,
voice-over and look unless set, takes an idempotency key, refuses with 409 remix_disabled when an admin turned it off,
and has no title or private field (PATCH after). Sound and voice-over follow server defaults (silent, no voice) in v1;
base-video is how CI videos get music or a voice-over (sound/voiceover inputs are in spec §13). The `look` input's
pass-through is split out to 2.2b, which waits for the Looks plan; base-video needs nothing from Looks, so it doesn't
wait for it (the plan: the action "needs neither").

## Approach
- base-video set (on a PR create, a release, or `/video` creating) → instead of videos.create:
  `videos.remix(base, { prompt: remixBrief(target, changes) (1.4), mediaIds, aspect?/durationSec? only when the inputs
  were given explicitly }, { idempotencyKey })` (same key shapes as create, 1.5); GET; the race check (1.5b); then one
  PATCH { title, private? } (title `PR #<n>: <title>` or `<repo>: What's new in <tag>`). Never send look here unless
  the look input was given (2.2b decides how).
- The base video must be visible to the CI account: 404 → fail the step with "base-video <id> not found or not visible
  to the CI account".
- 409 remix_disabled → comment + log "drop base-video or ask an admin to turn remixing on", outputs.status=skipped,
  exit 0.
- Revisions of a remixed PR video are ordinary revisions (1.8, 2.1).

## Done when
A release with base-video produces a remix with its own title, found again by lookup on the next run; remix_disabled is
reported cleanly.

## Tests
Integration (1.T): base-video → remix called with the source id and the reference line last, title PATCHed in one call
(with private when asked); re-run → same remix (lookup); race between two remixes → one survives; base-video not
visible → step fails with the message; remix_disabled (admin switch off in the harness) → reported; explicit aspect
sent, unset aspect not sent; logs `video-agent: mode=remix base=<id>`.

Spec key: 2.3
Spec section(s): §3.9, §4.9, §4.10, §4.13

## Background
Publishing (POST …/versions/{n}/publish, src/app.ts:576) returns stable public URLs (page, mp4, poster, gif, captions,
embed; PublicationSchema, src/schemas.ts:135), served by /v/{slug} and /v/{slug}.mp4|.jpg|.gif|.vtt
(netlify/edge-functions/public.ts:1-3, :55). publish defaults to false (owner question 2, building the default): GitHub
caches comment images, so a GIF may outlive an unpublish (spike A1 measures it; Needs 0.G). A release asset on a public
repo is a permanent public MP4, so on a public repo release-asset requires publish: true. private+publish is refused
(1.2), and `/video publish` refuses on a private video (1.8).

## Approach
- After ready with publish: true → versions.publish(id, n) (publishing an already-published version returns the
  existing publication); comment Ready-published state with the GIF (or the poster, if A1 said GIFs don't render)
  linked to the share page (1.6); release section with the same (1.10); outputs share-url, mp4-url, gif-url,
  poster-url; the job summary shows the poster.
- `/video publish` (1.8) now renders the full published state.
- release-asset: true → on a public repo without publish: stop with "release-asset on a public repo publishes the video:
  set publish: true" (validated early in 1.2); otherwise `files.download(video, { file: 'video', to })` and
  `{ file: 'captions', to }` into RUNNER_TEMP (signed redirects followed without Authorization) and upload release
  assets `video-<tag>.mp4` and `video-<tag>.vtt` (contents: write); on a re-run, delete an existing asset with the same
  name first, then upload.
- README note (4.1) on GitHub's image cache with A1's measured time.

## Done when
Published PR comments show the GIF; releases get the GIF and, when asked, the assets; the public-repo rule holds; a
re-run replaces assets instead of failing on a name clash.

## Tests
Integration (1.T): publish path renders the GIF URL from the Publication and sets the four outputs; poster fallback
flag; release-asset on a public repo without publish refused before any spend; with publish → both assets uploaded
(fake release), re-run replaces them (delete then upload); private repo allows release-asset without publish;
`/video publish` → published state; the download never sends Authorization to the storage host; logs
`video-agent: publish=<slug> assets=<n>`.

## Background
Redo-a-scene (the regenerate-beat plan) adds scoped revisions: revise with scope: { beats: [...] }, faster and

title: look pass-through: send the look input on create, revise and remix when the server lists looks (non-gating)
description:

Line refs re-checked at 8be7e18 (2026-11-05); lines drift as other work lands, so find code by the symbol or route named with each ref.
Spec key: 2.2b (look pass-through)
Spec section(s): §3.4 look, §3.6 Looks

## Background
The `look` input picks a named visual style from the Looks plan. It is sent only when GET /api/v1/config `features`
lists `looks`, because older servers silently drop unknown fields (request schemas aren't strict). No default look:
without the input the action sends none, so the deployment's default applies (none today; the roadmap keeps no default
until Looks spike K2, owner decision 2026-11-04). The engine follows the look (the Looks plan's engine choice rule), so
there's no `engine` input. With base-video, a remix keeps the source's look unless `look` is given explicitly. The
Looks plan's "terminal first because the Action needs it" isn't needed by this plan (spec §15). Split out of 2.2 so
base-video doesn't wait for the Looks plan; like 2.4, it ships when its dependency does and doesn't gate phase 2.
Needs: the Looks plan's phase 2 (look on create/revise/remix, the `looks` feature string, SDK looks.list).

## Approach
- look input set and features lists looks → send `look` on create, revise (1.8, 2.1) and remix (2.2); optionally check
  the id against `looks.list()` first and fail early with the available ids when it's unknown.
- look input set and the feature is absent → warning "this server has no looks; look ignored" and continue without it.
- Server refusals (400 for an unknown or disallowed look) → fail the step with the API message.
- The README (4.1) suggests `look: terminal` for developer-tool changelogs.

## Done when
look is passed when advertised, ignored with a warning otherwise, and a bad id fails with the list of looks.

## Tests
Integration (1.T, with Looks on in the harness): create, revise and remix carry the look; feature off → warning and no
field in the request body (fake asserts); unknown look → failure naming the available ids; base-video without look →
no field sent; logs `video-agent: look=<id|none> sent=<true|false>`.

description:

Spec key: P3
Spec section(s): §6, §10 Phase 3

## Background
Phases 1-2 work on today's API. These make CI videos better: a `context` field carries up to 16,000 characters of
background outside the 4,000-character prompt, in its own fence; externalRef gives an exact, indexed "the video for PR
123" lookup; private on create closes the create-then-PATCH window. Each is advertised in features (the registry the
CLI/SDK plan's phase 1.2 owns; this plan adds only `context` and `external_ref`), because older servers silently drop
unknown fields. Cross-plan order: this phase's migration is last in the migration order and its template change is
last in the PROMPT_TEMPLATE_VERSION bump order (shared rule: +1 per template-changing PR, in merge order; no literal
numbers). Server tasks 3.1-3.4 don't need the action's phases; only 3.5 does.

## Approach
3.1 migration (versions.context, jobs.external_ref, jobs.external_url: the API's "video" is the jobs table) → 3.2
context, 3.3 externalRef + private → 3.4 features → 3.5 action/CLI use (after LT-2) → 3.G → LT-3.

## Done when
All children closed, 3.G and LT-3 passed.

  create_video/remix_video accept external_ref and private.

title: Build: cap the BRAND_ZIP_URL fetch (timeout, size, entries, safe paths)
description:
Project: video-agent, an open-source Netlify template that turns a prompt into a published MP4 via Netlify Agent Runner runs writing HyperFrames compositions; Hono+OpenAPI API, Netlify Database (Drizzle), Blobs, Identity, React+Mantine UI, MCP. Found while planning Looks (docs/plans/2026-11-04-looks.md, review logs; the roadmap docs/plans/2026-11-04-roadmap.md lists it as a separate fix). Line refs are as of 8be7e18.

## Background
`scripts/build.ts:35-51` (`zipBrand`) fetches `BRAND_ZIP_URL` with a bare `fetch(url)` and no timeout, reads the whole body into memory with `res.arrayBuffer()` and no size cap, then runs `unzip -q` on it with no limit on entry count, uncompressed size or `..` paths. A slow or huge URL can hang or exhaust the production build, and a hostile zip can write outside its temp dir (zip-slip) or decompress into a zip bomb. The function already falls back to `context/` on any error and never logs the URL; keep both behaviours. Agent runs unpack the same zip through netlify-agent-kit's `files`, which is outside this repo; this bead covers only the build.

## Approach
- `fetch` with `AbortSignal.timeout(30_000)`. Refuse a `content-length` over 25 MB, and also stream the body with a running byte count that aborts past 25 MB (the header can lie or be absent).
- Before unzipping, list the entries (`unzip -Z1`, or parse the central directory). Refuse more than 500 entries, any absolute path or `..` segment, any symlink, and a total uncompressed size over 100 MB (`unzip -Zt` or the central directory sizes).
- Keep the fallback to `context/` and the `brand-zip` log event, with reason codes (`timeout`, `too_large`, `too_many_entries`, `unsafe_path`, `http_<status>`) and never the URL.
- Optional: share the limits with the Looks plan's `LOOKS_ZIP_URL` (Looks "Not in v1": team looks), so both use one helper in `scripts/lib/`.

## Done when
A slow server, an oversized body, a zip with `../` entries, a symlink entry and a zip bomb each make the build fall back to `context/` within the timeout, with the right reason code logged and no URL in the log. A normal brand zip still works exactly as before.

## Tests
Unit tests for the helper with a local HTTP server (`node:http` on port 0):
- a slow drip that passes the timeout;
- a body past 25 MB with no content-length;
- an honest content-length that's too big.
Fixture zips: `../evil.txt`, an absolute path, a symlink, 600 entries, and a high-ratio bomb (a 200 MB zero file). Each asserts the fallback and its log reason, and that nothing is written outside the temp dir. A happy-path zip gives the same brand as today. Structured JSON log lines (one `brand-zip` event with `ok` and `reason`).

Standard: unit and integration with createApp(fakeDeps) (test/helpers.ts harness) and PGlite (pgStore(), every migration applied); Playwright on the mock build (VITE_MOCK=1) for UI; structured JSON logs (one event per step, with ids, durations and outcome) so failures are diagnosable from logs alone. description:

Line refs are as of e477294.
Spec key: EPIC
Spec section(s): all (§0-§16)

## Background
Owner ask (2026-11-04, idea-wizard idea #2, "love it, let's do it"): make videos in different visual styles, chosen
from a gallery, that anyone can add to by opening a pull request. Remotion and other engines come later through the
render-engines plan (label engines).

Why it matters for the open-source launch: it's the most visible upgrade (the README and picker can show very
different videos from the same prompt); today every video comes out in roughly one house style and people ask for
"more like a magazine / a terminal / punchier for social" in every prompt, inconsistently; it absorbs the deferred
bead va-css.3 ("Later: Named templates in video/templates/"), which never got a design; and contributing a look needs
no backend knowledge (one folder, one check command), so it's the easiest first PR in the project.

What a look is (spec §0): a folder looks/<id>/ with look.json (metadata, zod-validated), LOOK.md (the rules the agent
follows: layout, type scale, pacing, motion, transitions, textures, how to use the brand's colour roles, building
blocks), an example/ composition that passes editing contract v1, vendored HyperFrames registry items, small licensed
assets, and a preview clip + poster for the picker. The run gets the look's files in context/look/ and follows them.
The brand still decides colours, logo, fonts and wording. Every version records which look it used and keeps a
snapshot of it, so retries and revisions get exactly the same look even after the look changes in the repo.
Restyle = a revision with another look.

Precedence (spec §3), strongest first: the request (and comments being incorporated) > the brand (context/,
context/brand/: colours, logo, fonts, wording, tone, claims) > the plan's brief > the look (layout, type scale,
pacing, motion, transitions, textures, colour-role use, caption style, sound mood) > video/AGENTS.md and the
HyperFrames skill defaults. A look never brings hex values for the brand's roles; derived roles are written as literal
colours (the editor's colour button prints the raw value, ui/src/pages/Edit.tsx:1357-1359, so color-mix() is banned).

People-facing words: "Look", "Restyle", "scene" for a beat; code/API: look, beat. Env vars for this feature are LOOKS_*;
don't confuse with RENDER_QUALITY=looks (a HyperFrames render quality, scripts/render-job.ts:50).

## Approach
Phases (each ends with a gate bead; gates chain; live tests are their own gate beads after the phase gate):
- Phase 0 spikes: K1 inline every starter-set registry block into a contract beat; K2 does a LOOK.md change the
  output and what does it cost (spike-branch runs, 900 credits, decides the default look); K3 function bundle path for
  the build-time archives; K4 registry item licences.
- Phase 1 the format, validator and catalog (no product change): pin the registry to the CLI's tag, src/lib/looks.ts
  (schema, hash, archive), look:check (static + browser halves), look:new, look:vendor, looks/README.md + PROMPTS.md,
  build integration (src/generated/looks.ts, looks-build/*.tar.gz, previews), the `clean` look, CI.
- Phase 2 data and run path: migration (versions.look, settings.default_look, settings.disabled_looks), resolveLook +
  restyle + engine choice, snapshot copy (deterministic reservation, read-back, adopt), wiring into create/revise/remix,
  run manifest look + pre-flight, prepare-run restore to context/look/, prompt lines, music mood, API, admin settings,
  MCP, `kinetic` and `terminal` looks, clean's recording block, scripts/e2e/looks.ts; harness gate; live test LT-1.
- Phase 3 UI and plans: mock build, picker on New video, video page + Restyle, Remix dialog, Admin Looks section,
  plans (deterministic pick, chosen_look) and the brief chip, /docs/looks + README poster strip; Playwright gate;
  live test LT-2 (owner makes one video per look in the app).
- Phase 4 SDK and CLI, more looks, fonts in looks: generated SDK coverage, CLI looks/--look/restyle, local --look,
  editorial, data-story, whiteboard, retro-crt, bold-blocks, fonts in looks, CONTRIBUTING; gate; live test LT-3.
- Phase 5 (engine-aware looks, looks that list remotion) is owned by the render-engines plan (its phase 5): this epic
  only guarantees `engines` in the schema and the engine choice rule (task 2.2a).

Owner decisions (2026-11-04), built as decided:
- Q3 Default look: None until tested; spike K2 decides whether `clean` becomes the default.
- Q9 Live tests: each runs --dry first, then the owner is asked before each gate, with a credit ceiling; no blanket
  pre-approval. Ceilings add up to about 2,900 credits: K2 900, LT-1 700, LT-2 500, LT-3 800.
- CLI package `netlify-video-agent` (bin video-agent); SDK `netlify-video-agent-sdk`; local mode ships ("make one
  locally, then deploy it for your team").

Open owner questions, built on their recommended defaults (none blocks work, so no decision beads):
1. Name: "Looks" or "Styles"? Building: Looks.
2. First three looks: clean, kinetic, terminal, built in that order. Building: that.
4. Revisions keep the old snapshot (not the look's latest version). Building: keep the snapshot.
5. Registry items with unclear licences: replace with hand-written equivalents. Building: replace (K4).
6. Previews committed to the repo (under 4.5 MB for eight looks at 500 KB per clip). Building: committed.
7. Team looks (LOOKS_ZIP_URL): not in v1, design kept. Building: not in v1.
8. Restyle for videos with recorded narration: refused in v1 (409 look_not_allowed). Building: refuse.
10. Who picks a look: everyone who can create; no deployment-wide lock. Building: that.

agent-cursor, before-after-wipe) and blocks (hyperframes:block, separate sub-composition files with their own timeline,
mounted with data-composition-src: code-diff, code-slice-hero, bar-chart-race, data-chart, beat-freeze-cut,
camcorder-hud, chromatic-radial-split, editorial-flash-overlay, canopy-part-title, lt-clean-bar). Editing contract v1
needs beats as direct children of the root, each with ONE vaBeat script selecting only inside its element, never
document or window.__timelines (src/lib/contract.ts:395-445); any other timed root child that isn't a layer fails
(:449-455). The validator never mentions data-composition-src, so whether a mounted block INSIDE a beat passes, and
whether the editor (which reads only video/index.html) can edit its text, is unverified. Text in a block's own file
isn't editable. So the plan says: looks list components first and inline any block they use.

## Approach
In a scratch HyperFrames project (copy video/ with vendor/gsap.min.js and vendor/va-contract.js, hyperframes.json
pinned to v0.8.222), for EACH of the ten blocks above:
1. npx hyperframes@0.8.222 add <name> --json; read its markup, CSS and timeline.
2. Inline it into a contract beat: markup into the <section data-va-beat>, CSS scoped to [data-va-beat="<id>"], its
   timeline calls rewritten inside the beat's vaBeat('<id>', (tl, el) => …) selecting only within el, editable text
   given data-va-text ids and data-va-label.
3. Run npx tsx scripts/check-contract.ts and npx hyperframes check (0 errors), render, look at snapshots.
4. Load it in the editor (npx netlify dev, or the mock editor) and change a text and the scene's timing; re-render.
Also mount ONE block with data-composition-src inside a beat and record what check-contract, hyperframes check and the
editor do.
Measures: per block, inlinable yes/no, effort, what broke. Pass bar: a block is "inlinable" when all four steps pass
with text and timing editable; otherwise it's on the "replace by hand" list.
What each result changes: inlinable blocks get exact "Building blocks" instructions (a reusable pattern for LOOK.md
§4.4 item 12, used by tasks 1.5, 2.8a, 2.8b, 4.2a-e); blocks that fail are replaced with hand-written moves in the
§5 table and in their look's registry list; if a mounted sub-composition inside a beat turns out to work in check,
render AND editor, record it and propose amending §4.5 (the plan still prefers inlining).

## Done when
docs/spikes.md has a "K1" section: a table of the ten blocks (inlinable, notes, effort), the Building-blocks
instruction pattern, the data-composition-src finding, and the replace-by-hand list. No credits spent.

## Tests
The spike's own artefacts: each inlined beat passes scripts/check-contract.ts and hyperframes check; an editor
text+timing edit re-renders. Log each step as a JSON line ({step, block, ok, ms, problem}).

title: K2: does a LOOK.md change the output, and what does it cost? (spike-branch runs, 900 credits, ask first)
description:
Project: video-agent, an open-source Netlify template that turns a prompt into a published MP4 via Netlify Agent Runner runs writing HyperFrames compositions; Hono+OpenAPI API, Netlify Database (Drizzle), Blobs, Identity, React+Mantine UI, MCP. Feature: Looks (a style system: a person picks a look per video, such as Kinetic type or Terminal, the run follows that look's rules, and anyone can contribute a look by pull request). Spec: docs/plans/2026-11-04-looks.md (draft 3, commit e477294; §14 = owner questions, §16 = review logs of the independent Fable 5.1 review, the cross-plan seam review, the remote Fable 5.1 Agent Run review and the owner decisions of 2026-11-04). Line refs are as of e477294.
Spec key: K2
Spec section(s): §2 gotchas 9-12, §6, §7 credits table, §10 K2, §14 Q3

## Background
The whole feature rests on the agent actually following a LOOK.md so looks come out clearly different and on-brand,
at an acceptable cost. It also decides the default look (owner decision 2026-11-04: None until tested; K2 decides
whether `clean` becomes the default). Production can't run a look until phase 2, and local mode is the CLI/SDK plan's
phase 4, so K2 must need no server code (remote review R4). The app never starts runs on a branch deploy itself, but
spikes/start-run.ts starts a run with --branch or --deploy-id (spikes/start-run.ts:2, :42-43), as the phase-0 spikes
did. The run already reads context/ (src/domain/prompt.ts:137).

## Approach
1. Hand-write draft looks `clean` and `kinetic` (LOOK.md with the §4.4 sections, a small example/) on a spike branch,
   committed under context/look/<id>/ (or the single look under context/look/ per run).
2. Build each run's prompt with buildPrompt (src/domain/prompt.ts:110) plus the §4.6 look lines appended (the look
   lines text is in the plan §4.6 step 4 and in task 2.4); a small script in spikes/ prints them.
3. Six runs: two fixed prompts (a 16:9 launch and a 9:16 social clip from looks/PROMPTS.md drafts) × no look, clean,
   kinetic. `terminal` waits for K1's code-diff result.
4. First print a dry listing: the six prompts, the branch, and projected credits (about 150 per run; ceiling 900).
   Live-test rule (owner decision 2026-11-04): a live test is a script that makes real videos on the production site and checks them; it costs credits. Run it with --dry first (it prints the steps and the projected credits and spends nothing), then ASK THE OWNER for a go-ahead before running it, stating the credit ceiling. Never pre-approved; a re-run is asked again.
Measure per run: input/output tokens and credits (usage on the run), contract pass, hyperframes check, how often the
agent copied example words or media, wall time; then a contact sheet (6 frames per video, ffmpeg) side by side for the
owner.
Pass bar: the owner agrees the looks are clearly different from each other and from no-look, and on-brand; contract
passes; example words copied in at most 1 of 4 look runs.
What each result changes: (a) `clean` costs at most about 5 % more than no look and looks at least as good -> the
owner may decide `clean` becomes the default (record the decision and which way it applies: either an admin sets it in Admin -> Looks on each deployment, or
task 2.1's migration seeds it for new deployments only: ADD COLUMN default_look text with no default (existing
settings rows stay null), then ALTER COLUMN default_look SET DEFAULT 'clean', which only the settings row a fresh
deployment inserts later gets, provided the settings insert omits the column); otherwise the default stays None. (b) Looks not clearly different -> revise the LOOK.md section guidance and
the example size before tasks 1.3e/1.5. (c) Heavy example copying -> strengthen the prompt rule and shrink the example
(cap 24 KB stays). (d) Cost per run noticeably above 5 % -> tighten the 12 KB LOOK.md cap and "skim the matching scene"
wording in 2.4.

Tooling: spikes/k2-prompts.ts prints each run's full prompt (buildPrompt + the look lines) and the dry listing; runs
start with spikes/start-run.ts --prompt-file <file> --branch <spike branch> (spikes/start-run.ts:2, :42-43). Credits
are read from each run's usage (usage.totalCreditsCost, as scripts/e2e/remix.ts does); the contact sheet is 6 frames
per video via ffmpeg into spikes/out/k2/ (gitignored). The spike branch is never merged.

## Done when

decision; credits spent recorded and under the 900 ceiling.

## Background
Snapshots are copied from archives the build makes (looks-build/<id>.tar.gz) and the API function carries via
netlify.toml [functions] included_files (globs relative to the project root). Nothing in src/ reads files from disk at
run time today (netlify/functions/api.ts imports generated modules only), and glob matchers often skip dot-directories
(why the folder is looks-build/, not .looks-build/, remote review R7). How the function finds the files at run time
(process.cwd() vs import.meta.url) is new ground.

## Approach
On a branch deploy and under npx netlify dev: hand-build looks-build/clean.tar.gz (any small folder, entries under
look/, deterministic tar), add [functions] included_files = ["looks-build/*.tar.gz"], add a temporary debug route
(branch only, never merged) that reads join(process.cwd(), 'looks-build', 'clean.tar.gz') and returns its sha256 and
bytes. Build the same commit twice and compare sha256. Measure the function bundle size before/after.
Pass bar: the file resolves at process.cwd()/looks-build on both, the sha256 matches the build's and is identical across
two builds.
What each result changes: pass -> task 2.2b reads from that path. Fail -> record the working path (import.meta.url
relative) or the fallback: deploy-scoped Blobs written by the build and read by the function; task 2.2b and 1.4 change
accordingly.

## Done when
docs/spikes.md has a "K3" section: the resolved path on branch deploy and netlify dev, the sha256 across two builds,

## Background
One schema module is shared by the build, look:check and the server (spec §4.2). Unknown keys are refused, so every key
another plan needs is declared here (the screen-recording plan needs `recording`). writeTarGz (src/lib/tar.ts:124)
writes deterministic archives (sorted, fixed mtimes) but hard-codes video/ (:127), and restoreArchive refuses anything
outside video/ (remote review R3). bundleManifest(dir)'s excluded() rules (src/lib/bundle-manifest.ts:32-41: dot paths,
feedback/, top-level .mp4, assets/media/med_*) are for compositions; a look hashes with manifestHash(files, []) (:63).

## Approach
src/lib/looks.ts (no I/O beyond explicit fs helpers, usable from build, scripts and functions):
- LookJsonSchema (zod, .strict()):
  id /^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{0,39}$/ (= folder name); name ≤ 40; description ≤ 160; tags ≤ 8 each ≤ 20 lowercase;
  bestFor ⊆ plan templates (launch, tutorial, social, changelog, sales, other: src/domain/plans.ts CHECKLISTS keys
  :44-51); aspects ⊆ ['16:9','9:16','1:1','4:5'] non-empty; engines non-empty, first preferred: z.enum over EngineId from src/domain/engines.ts when the render-engines
  plan's phase 1 has added it (va-ed2s.2.1), else a local LOOK_ENGINES = ['hyperframes'] that the engines plan widens
  (no default: built-ins write ['hyperframes'] explicitly); colors { roles: string[], derived: string[] };
  sound { musicMood ≤ 120 } optional; recording: false | { frame: 'wallpaper'|'browser'|'device'|'none', padding,

Line refs are as of e477294.
Spec key: 1.3a
Spec section(s): §9 static half, §4.1 limits, §2 gotchas 8-10 and 16, §10 1.3

## Background
A broken or unsafe look must never deploy, and contributors need one command that tells them what's wrong. The
Netlify build has no browser, so look:check is split (independent review A5): the static half runs in the build and
in CI; the browser half (task 1.3b) runs in CI only.

## Approach
scripts/look-check.ts, npm script `look:check` (`npm run look:check [--static] [id…]`, all looks when no id). Output:
one line per problem, `look:<id>: <problem>`; exit 1 on any. Static checks:
- look.json matches LookJsonSchema; id matches folder; `registry` equals the items in registry/registry.lock.json.
- LOOK.md exists, ≤ 12 KB, has every REQUIRED_LOOK_SECTIONS heading; example/index.html ≤ 24 KB; example/summary.json
  exists.
- File rules and limits (LOOK_LIMITS): allowed extensions, no symlinks/dotfiles/'..', run files ≤ 3 MB, ≤ 1 MB each,
  assets/ ≤ 1 MB.
- Every binary sniffs as its extension says. Reuse the media sniffers (all at 4c573aa): classify()
  (src/lib/media/classify.ts:106) for PNG/WebP/JPEG images, sniffAudio() (src/lib/media/audio.ts:209: RIFF/WAVE,
  OggS, ID3/frame sync) for .wav/.ogg/.mp3, sniffPreview() (src/lib/media/previews.ts:35) for preview.mp4 and
  poster.webp. An .svg must come through sanitizeSvg() (src/lib/media/svg.ts:196) unchanged in meaning: refuse it when
  sanitizing drops anything (a <script>, an on* handler, an external href), since vendored and asset SVGs reach the
  render's Chrome.
- assets/credits.json lists every file in assets/ with an allowed licence (CC0, CC BY + credit, OFL, Apache-2.0, MIT,
  "own work").
- Vendored items' sha256 match registry.lock.json, and the lock's tag equals netlifyAgent.hyperframes.version.
- example/ passes validate() from src/lib/contract.ts (the same check as scripts/check-contract.ts, with its
  summary.json); contains no URL outside the folder (http(s)://, //host) and no Date.now() / Math.random().
- The example uses only colour roles listed in look.json colors (roles + derived), every --va-color-* value is a literal
  colour (refuse color-mix(, var( inside a role value, calc), and every visible text element has data-va-text.
- preview.mp4 and poster.webp exist, sniff right and are within size (a template folder, _template, is checked as
  a template: previews optional).
- Problems are collected, never thrown on the first one, so a contributor sees every line in one run.
Also export the checks as a function (checkLookStatic(dir)) for the build (task 1.4).

## Done when
`npm run look:check --static` passes on a good fixture and reports each rule on its failing fixture.

## Tests
Unit (fixtures under test/fixtures/looks/): good look passes; one failing fixture per rule: missing section, oversized
LOOK.md, oversized example, assets/ over 1 MB, bad licence in credits.json, a .png that isn't one, a color-mix derived
role, example breaking the contract, external URL, Math.random, lock tag mismatch, lock sha mismatch, registry list
mismatch, unknown look.json key, symlink, dotfile. Each asserts the exact `look:<id>: …` line.
Also: an .svg with <script> or onload= fails; a .wav that is really an MP3 fails; _template passes without
previews. With --json absent (not in v1) output is exactly one `look:<id>: <problem>` line per problem plus a final

that already use it keep it (retries, inherited revisions, edits).

## Approach
AdminSettingsSchema / UpdateAdminSettingsSchema gain defaultLook: string | null and disabledLooks: string[]. The
PATCH route's x-sdk gets fieldFeatures { defaultLook: 'looks', disabledLooks: 'looks' } (shared rule, CLI bead
va-p1th.2.1), so an older server can't silently drop them. PATCH validates the settings as they'd be AFTER the patch, so it refuses an unknown id (in either field), a

deploy removed is kept in disabledLooks (harmless) and makes defaultLook fall through at create time (task 2.2a). When defaultLook is set, the setup page notes that API, MCP and Action callers get it too (text in
src/domain/setup.ts facts). Log admin.settings_updated with the changed fields.

one request is accepted; non-admins get 403; the setup page shows the default-look note only when defaultLook is
set; log admin.settings_updated { changed: ['defaultLook', 'disabledLooks'] } asserted.
Spec test: the PATCH route's fieldFeatures lists defaultLook and disabledLooks as 'looks'. SDK (with task
4.1a): the SDK refuses `defaultLook` with `unsupported_by_server` against a server whose features don't list `looks`.

description:
Project: video-agent, an open-source Netlify template that turns a prompt into a published MP4 via Netlify Agent Runner runs writing HyperFrames compositions; Hono+OpenAPI API, Netlify Database (Drizzle), Blobs, Identity, React+Mantine UI, MCP. Line refs are as of e477294.
Spec key: 2.9
Spec section(s): §11 Live test, §10 Gate 2

## Background
Live tests prove the run path on production. Pattern: scripts/e2e/remix.ts (--dry, CREDIT_CEILING). Live-test rule (owner decision 2026-11-04): a live test is a script that makes real videos on the production site and checks them; it costs credits. Run it with --dry first (it prints the steps and the projected credits and spends nothing), then ASK THE OWNER for a go-ahead before running it, stating the credit ceiling. Never pre-approved; a re-run is asked again.

## Approach
scripts/e2e/looks.ts:
- --dry prints the steps, the looks to test and the projected credits, and makes no requests.
- Reads VIDEO_AGENT_URL, VIDEO_AGENT_KEY, LOOKS (default clean,kinetic,terminal), CREDIT_CEILING (default 700),
  LOOK_RUN_CREDITS (default 140, the per-run estimate the dry listing and the ceiling use for runs without a reported
  cost, as remix.ts uses REMIX_CREDITS), RESTYLE (default 1; 0 skips the restyle step, for LT-3), RETRY_CHECK (default
  0; 1 runs the retry-after-look-change step), FONT_LOOKS (looks whose shipped font must be used, for LT-3).
  Reuses scripts/e2e/lib.ts and narration-lib.ts (call, check, dry, GateError) like remix.ts.
- For each look: create a 15 s 16:9 video from a fixed prompt, wait, check version.look, the contract flag and the
  download; save a contact sheet (6 frames via ffmpeg) to out/looks/<id>.png. Then (RESTYLE=1) restyle the first into another look and check that beat ids and text ids were kept and the
  look changed. The API doesn't serve source.tar.gz (the file enum is video, poster, gif, captions, narration-audio,
  transcript, src/app.ts:151-155), so ids come from each version's composition: POST
  /api/v1/videos/{id}/versions/{n}/edits returns { composition: { beats: [{ id, texts: [{ id }] }], colors } }
  (EditSchema, src/schemas.ts:1198); drafts are opened only on the videos the script made. Also check every colour role in the
  restyled composition's `colors` is a literal (no color-mix().
- RETRY_CHECK=1: create one video with a look, cancel it at once (POST …/versions/1/cancel, before or right as it
  starts, so it costs little), record version.look.hash, then wait (polling GET /api/v1/looks, up to 20 min, logging
  each poll) until that look's catalog hash differs: someone pushes a trivial LOOK.md change to main meanwhile and the
  script prints exactly that instruction. Then POST …/versions/1/retry (allowed for failed, cancelled and timed-out
  versions), wait for ready, and check version.look.hash is still the recorded one and differs from the catalog's.
- FONT_LOOKS: for each, fetch the version's preview (GET …/versions/{n}/preview -> url) and check its index.html has
  an @font-face whose src is under assets/look/; if the preview can't be read as HTML, log a weak check and leave it
  to the contact sheet.
- Without ffmpeg, contact sheets are skipped with a logged weak check, as remix.ts does.
- One JSON line per step ({"step":"create","look":"kinetic","videoId":…,"ms":…,"credits":…}); stops starting runs at
  the ceiling; deletes what it made unless --keep; never prints env vars.

## Done when
`--dry` works offline; the script type-checks and its offline helpers are tested.

## Tests
Unit tests (test/e2e-looks.test.ts) for the id comparison (beats or texts dropped, renamed or reordered each
fail with a message naming the id), the literal-colour check, the catalog-hash wait loop with a fake clock, the
credit ceiling (refuses to start the next run once projected credits reach it) and the contact-sheet helper on a
fixture MP4; a --dry snapshot test (no network calls: the fake fetch is never hit); a --selftest that runs the

nothing to inherit (remote review R2: a one-line `input.look ?? inherited ?? default` silently restyled every revision
of a look-less video once an admin set a default). Revisions keep the parent's value like sound does
(src/domain/videos.ts:78). This plan owns the engine choice rule the render-engines plan references.

## Approach
src/domain/looks.ts (pure functions plus catalog lookups over src/generated/looks.ts):
- A Deps port for the catalog, so tests can swap catalogs (needed for "the catalog changed, retry uses the old
  snapshot"): src/deps.ts gains looks: LooksPort { catalog(): LookCatalogEntry[]; archive(id): Promise<Uint8Array> }
  (archive is filled in by task 2.2b); the production adapter src/adapters/looks.ts wraps src/generated/looks.ts;
  test/fakes.ts gets fakeLooks(entries?) defaulting to a three-look fixture catalog (clean, kinetic, terminal) with
  small fixture archives under test/fixtures/looks/. getLook(deps, id) -> entry | null.
- resolveLook(input: { look?: string | null }, ctx: { inherited?: VersionLook | null (present for revise, remix,
  render-unchanged, fit, redo a scene), planLook?: string | null, defaultLook: string | null, disabled: string[] }):
  input.look === null -> none; input.look given -> that look's current catalog version (400 unknown_look "There's no
  look called …"; 409 look_disabled "An admin has turned the … look off"); omitted with a parent -> the parent's value
  INCLUDING none (default never consulted); omitted on create -> planLook, else defaultLook, else none. Only an explicit `look` in THIS request is refused
  when unknown or disabled. A plan look or an admin default that has since left the catalog (a later deploy removed
  it) or been disabled falls through to the next source (plan -> default -> none) with
  log look.fallback { from: 'plan'|'default', id, reason: 'unknown'|'disabled' }, so a create never fails because of
  a setting the person didn't make in this request. Inheriting never checks disabled or the catalog: the parent's
  snapshot is self-contained (spec §6: versions that already use a disabled look keep it). Returns
  { kind: 'none' } | { kind: 'inherit', look } | { kind: 'pick', entry }.
- isRestyle(parent: VersionLook | null, resolved): true when the resolved hash differs from the parent's (new id, same
  id at a newer catalog hash, or a look where the parent had none); the parent's own id at the same hash is not a
  restyle.
- chooseEngine({ requestEngine?, look, enabledEngines }): request.engine validated against the look's engines (400
  engine_not_supported_by_look) and the enabled engines (409 engine_disabled); else the look's first listed engine
  that's enabled; else hyperframes. A restyle into a look that doesn't list the version's engine -> 400
  engine_not_supported_by_look. Until the render-engines plan's phase 2, this always resolves to hyperframes.
- aspectNotice(look, aspect): a notice ("Retro CRT wasn't made for 4:5") when aspects doesn't list it; never refused.
Error codes added to src/lib/errors.ts: unknown_look 400, look_disabled 409, look_not_allowed 400,
engine_not_supported_by_look 400, engine_disabled 409 (reuse the engines plan's codes if it has added them). At
4c573aa ApiError takes its status from STATUS: Record<ErrorCode, number> (src/lib/errors.ts:20-50), one status per
code, but the spec uses look_not_allowed at 400 (render-unchanged, fit, scope) and 409 (narrated restyle). Add an
optional status override to ApiError (new ApiError(code, message, details, { status })) used only for that 409, and
document both statuses for the code in OpenAPI (task 2.6a).

## Done when
All resolution, restyle and engine cases behave as the table in spec §4.3 says.

## Tests
Unit: create omitted -> plan then default then none; explicit null never the default (create, revise, remix, plans);
revise/remix omitted keep null when the parent has none even with an admin default set; parent's own id+hash is not a
restyle; same id newer hash is; unknown and disabled ids; engine rule (request engine allowed/not in look/disabled,
first enabled, fallback hyperframes); aspect notice.
Fallbacks: a plan look that's disabled -> default; a default that left the catalog -> none, never a 400; both
log look.fallback with the reason. Inherit of a disabled or removed look still resolves to the parent's snapshot.
ApiError's override: look_not_allowed is 400 by default and 409 with the override; errorBody unchanged.
