title: Look snapshot copy: deterministic reservation (insert or re-open), verified copy, adopt in the tx; included_files
description:
Project: video-agent, an open-source Netlify template that turns a prompt into a published MP4 via Netlify Agent Runner runs writing HyperFrames compositions; Hono+OpenAPI API, Netlify Database (Drizzle), Blobs, Identity, React+Mantine UI, MCP. Feature: Looks (a style system: a person picks a look per video, such as Kinetic type or Terminal, the run follows that look's rules, and anyone can contribute a look by pull request). Spec: docs/plans/2026-11-04-looks.md (draft 3, commit e477294; §14 = owner questions, §16 = review logs of the independent Fable 5.1 review, the cross-plan seam review, the remote Fable 5.1 Agent Run review and the owner decisions of 2026-11-04). Line refs are as of e477294.
Spec key: 2.2b
Spec section(s): §4.3 snapshot copy, §2 gotchas 2-5, §1 Data, §10 2.2

## Background
Blob writes aren't transactional. Remix copies outside the transaction under a reservation cleanup row committed
first, writes, reads back and compares the sha256 (src/domain/remix.ts:104-111, :127-130), then the transaction
adopts it (:257-258); an unadopted copy is swept after REMIX_RESERVATION_MS (1 h, :56). Looks reuse that, adjusted:
a revision reuses the video's id, so the same <jobId>/looks/<hash>.tar.gz can be reserved twice, and cleanups has a unique (store, prefix) index (db/schema.ts:691 at e477294, :696 at 4c573aa) -> a second
insert 500s. An unadopted copy also looks present until
swept (remote review R1). Manifest keys must stay under the video's prefix (src/lib/run-manifest.ts:308-309), so the
snapshot is per video. createVideo mints its id inside its transaction today (src/domain/videos.ts:318-321).

## Approach
- netlify.toml: [functions] included_files = ["looks-build/*.tar.gz"] (path confirmed or replaced by K3).
- readBundledLookArchive(id): reads join(process.cwd(), 'looks-build', `${id}.tar.gz`) (or K3's path), checks sha256
  against the catalog; a mismatch is a server error (bundle corrupt), never a silent fallback. Behind a Deps port
  (e.g. deps.looks.archive(id)) so tests use fixtures.
- deps.looks.archive(id) (the LooksPort from task 2.2a) is the production reader above; fakes return fixture
  archives, and a fake can return wrong bytes to test the corrupt-bundle error.
- Two sources for a snapshot: { from: 'bundle', entry } (a pick: the bundled archive of the current catalog version)
  and { from: 'blob', look: VersionLook } (a REMIX inheriting its source's look: copy the source video's own snapshot
  blob at look.key, checking look.sha256, because the catalog may hold a newer hash for that id, or none). If the
  source's blob is gone, use the bundled archive only when the catalog still has that id at the same hash; otherwise
  409 conflict "The source video's look snapshot is missing; pick a look for the remix". A revision that inherits
  needs no copy at all (same video, same key).
- snapshotLook(deps, jobId, source) -> VersionLook, called BEFORE the transaction:
  1. If a committed version of this video already references key `${jobId}/looks/${hash}.tar.gz`, skip the copy
     (re-checked inside the tx). The blob merely existing is never the signal.
  2. Insert the reservation cleanup row { id: `look-${jobId}-${hash}`, kind: 'delete_prefix', store: 'sources',
     prefix: key, nextActionAt: now + 1 h, doneAt: null }, or if it exists re-open it with updateCleanup(id, { doneAt:
     null, nextActionAt: now + 1 h }) (src/store/types.ts:332). Then write the archive to the sources store
     (overwriting an unadopted copy is harmless: same bytes), read it back, compare sha256.
- adoptLookSnapshot(repo, jobId, look): inside the version-inserting tx, mark the reservation done; if another
  committed version already references the key, mark it done too.
- createVideo: when the resolved look needs a copy, mint the job id before the transaction (as remixVideo does) and
  pass it in.
- Logs: look.snapshot { jobId, id, hash, copied: bool, ms }, look.snapshot_adopted, look.snapshot_unadopted (replay).

## Done when
Snapshots are copied once per video and hash, adopted by the creating transaction, swept when unadopted, and never collide on the unique index.

## Tests
Integration (memory + PGlite): reservation committed before the copy; read-back mismatch fails the request; an
idempotent replay leaves the copy unadopted and the sweep deletes it; a successful create marks the reservation done;
a second revision picking a look whose first attempt failed re-opens the row (no unique-index error); an existing but
unadopted blob is copied again, never trusted; a version never references a key no committed version adopted; two
versions of one video picking the same look share one blob and one reservation row (marked done once); deleting the
video removes the snapshot with its prefix. Logs asserted: look.snapshot with copied true/false.
Remix inherit: the copy comes from the source's blob (a fake catalog with a newer hash for that id doesn't change
the remix's hash); source blob gone + same hash in the catalog -> bundled copy; gone + different hash -> 409 with the
message; a corrupt bundled archive (fake returns other bytes) -> 500 internal and log look.archive_corrupt { id }.

Standard: unit and integration with createApp(fakeDeps) (test/helpers.ts harness) and PGlite (pgStore(), every migration applied); Playwright on the mock build (VITE_MOCK=1) for UI; structured JSON logs (one event per step, with ids, durations and outcome) so failures are diagnosable from logs alone. CI (npm run typecheck, lint, vitest, npx playwright test, openapi:check, db:check) stays green. title: Wire looks into createVideo, reviseVideo, remixVideo, edit renders and fit; refusals and logs

Line refs are as of e477294.
Spec key: 2.2c
Spec section(s): §4.3 inheritance table, §4.9 errors, §10 2.2

## Background
The inheritance table (spec §4.3) is the contract every entry point follows. Recorded narration locks length and beat
sum (src/domain/prompt.ts:116, lockedNarrationLines :485, checkNarrationModified src/lib/narration-modified.ts:155,
:306-309), so a restyle of a narrated version is refused in v1 (owner Q8 default). Redo a scene (regenerate-beat plan)
refuses a new look.

## Approach
- CreateVideoInput, ReviseInput, RemixInput gain look?: string | null (src/domain/videos.ts:56-82 at e477294,
  :66-92 at 4c573aa; src/domain/remix.ts:35-49).
- createVideo (src/domain/videos.ts:308 at 4c573aa): resolveLook with planLook (task 3.5a adds it, reading the plan
  BEFORE the transaction; until then null) and the admin default; when a copy is needed, mint the job id before the
  transaction (today it's minted inside, :331 at 4c573aa), snapshot, then adopt inside the tx; versions.look set with
  restyle false.
- Aspect notice: the version DTO (versionDto, src/domain/videos.ts:903 at 4c573aa) adds aspectNotice(entry, aspect) to
  its notices list (today only the output's notices, :973) when the catalog entry for version.look.id doesn't list
  the video's aspect. Computed on read, nothing stored; built-ins cover all four shapes, so in v1 only a fixture
  catalog triggers it.
- reviseVideo (:407 at 4c573aa): inherited = parent's look (no copy, same key); look: null on a parent with a look ->
  version.look null and no look lines (the agent keeps whatever the composition has); a restyle sets
  version.look.restyle = true and copies the new snapshot; a restyle of a parent with recorded narration (version.narration set) ->
  409 look_not_allowed "Restyle isn't available for videos with recorded narration yet" (the parent's own look at the
  same hash is accepted); `scope` present (regenerate-beat) with look -> 400 look_not_allowed: `scope` doesn't exist yet when this lands
  (migration order: looks 2.1 before regenerate-beat 2), so export assertLookAllowed({ scope, look }) from
  src/domain/looks.ts and let the regenerate-beat bead that adds scope (va-8cy4.3.5, "look refused") call it and own
  that test.
- remixVideo (src/domain/remix.ts:149): inherited = the source version's look (none if none), re-snapshotted
  under the remix's own prefix FROM THE SOURCE'S BLOB (task 2.2b's { from: 'blob' }), restyle false; a new look =
  restyle as a new video, restyle true (remix drops recorded narration today, so allowed). The remix already mints
  newJobId before its transaction, so the look copy sits next to the source copy and uses the same failure path.
- Edit -> Render and Fit to my narration are both created by renderEdit (src/domain/edits.ts:671; the version's
  mode is set at :779, 'author' for a fit, 'render_unchanged' otherwise) from POST /api/v1/edits/{id}/render
  (RenderEditSchema, src/schemas.ts:1238), not by reviseVideo. Both copy look from the draft's base version
  (restyle false): display only for render_unchanged; the fit's manifest and prompt use it (task 2.3a). zod strips
  unknown keys, so to refuse rather than silently ignore, RenderEditSchema gains look: z.unknown().optional()
  documented "Not accepted: an edit render keeps the edited version's look", and renderEdit throws 400
  look_not_allowed when it's present.
- Engine: chooseEngine for new videos (records versions.engine when the render-engines plan has added it).
- Debug logs: add look to video.create_requested / video.revise_requested / remix events.

## Done when
Every row of the §4.3 table holds in the harness.

## Tests
Integration (createApp(fakeDeps), memory + PGlite): create with look / omitted (default; none by default) / null /
unknown (400) / disabled (409); revise inherits the parent's snapshot (same key and hash, no new blob); revise with a
new look restyles (new snapshot); restyle of a narrated version is 409; revise with scope + look is 400;
render-unchanged copies look and refuses look in the request; fit inherits and refuses look; remix keeps the source's
look under its own prefix; remix with another look; delete a video: its looks/ snapshot is in the cleanup prefix.
Also: revise with look: null on a looked parent -> look null, no new blob, prompt without look lines; a revision
inheriting a look that's since disabled still works; remix inherit copies from the source's blob; restyle flag true
only for restyles; POST /edits/{id}/render with look -> 400 look_not_allowed and without it the new version's look
equals the base's; the aspect notice appears in the DTO for a fixture look without 4:5. Log lines asserted:
video.create_requested { look }, video.revise_requested { look, restyle }, video.remixed { look, restyle }.

title: Run manifest look field + reconciler (fit and author/revision manifests) + snapshot pre-flight
description:

Spec key: 2.3a

## Background
Inputs a run restores come from a server-written manifest whose sha256 is in the prompt. There are three putManifest
calls: render-unchanged (src/domain/reconciler.ts:208), author-from-frozen (:232) and author/revision (:317, written
only when `revision || media`, :316). verifyRunManifest accepts only v: 1, checks fields it knows and ignores unknown
ones (src/lib/run-manifest.ts:295-320); the cross-plan rule keeps v: 1 with an optional field and its own shape check.
A version whose snapshot is gone would burn credits on every retry, failing inside the runner; the reconciler
already pre-flights remix copies (:258-260, SourceUnavailable).

## Approach
- src/lib/run-manifest.ts: RunManifest.look?: { id, key, sha256, hash }; verifyRunManifest shape check: key inside
  the job prefix (the existing own() rule), sha256 and hash hex, id matches the look slug rule.
- reconciler: render-unchanged manifest gets NO look; author-from-frozen (fit) manifest gets look; author/revision
  manifest gets look and its condition becomes `if (revision || media || version.look)`.
- Pre-flight before starting an attempt whose version has a look: deps.blobs.list('sources', key) includes key, else
  fail the attempt (SourceUnavailable-style) with "This video's look snapshot is missing; restyle it to pick the look
  again". No run starts, no credits.
- Pass look { id, name } and restyle (version.look.restyle, decided at creation, task 2.1) into buildPrompt /
  buildFitPrompt (task 2.4). The reconciler never re-reads the parent or the remix source to decide it, so every
  retry gets the same prompt.
- The render-engines plan adds an optional `engine` field to the same manifest (va-ed2s.2.5): whichever lands second
  rebases; each field keeps its own shape check.
- Logs: run.manifest { attemptId, kind, look: id|null }, look.preflight_failed { jobId, key }.

## Done when
Manifests carry look exactly where the spec says; a missing snapshot fails before any run starts.

## Tests
Unit: verifyRunManifest accepts a good look entry and refuses a key outside the prefix, non-hex hashes, a bad id.
Integration: the fake runner receives a manifest with look for create/revise/fit and none for render-unchanged; a
retry after the catalog changed still points at the original snapshot; pre-flight failure leaves the attempt failed
with the message and the fake runner never called.
A remix whose source video was deleted after creation still starts (look from its own copy) and gets the
restyle lines when it was created as a restyle; pre-flight runs for remix and fit attempts too; logs
run.manifest { attemptId, kind, look } and look.preflight_failed { jobId, key } asserted.

title: Prompt: look lines, restyle lines, fit-prompt look lines; template constant +1; golden prompt untouched
description:
Project: video-agent, an open-source Netlify template that turns a prompt into a published MP4 via Netlify Agent Runner runs writing HyperFrames compositions; Hono+OpenAPI API, Netlify Database (Drizzle), Blobs, Identity, React+Mantine UI, MCP. Feature: Looks (a style system: a person picks a look per video, such as Kinetic type or Terminal, the run follows that look's rules, and anyone can contribute a look by pull request). Spec: docs/plans/2026-11-04-looks.md (draft 3, commit e477294; §14 = owner questions, §16 = review logs of the independent Fable 5.1 review, the cross-plan seam review, the remote Fable 5.1 Agent Run review and the owner decisions of 2026-11-04). Line refs are as of e477294.
Spec key: 2.4
Spec section(s): §4.6 steps 4-5, §2 gotchas 9-12, §1 prompt facts, §10 2.4

## Background
Optional features keep the prompt byte-identical when off (src/domain/prompt.ts:38-41); the golden fixture
test/fixtures/prompt-silent.txt is compared byte for byte (src/domain/prompt.test.ts:76-79). Shared rule: each PR that
changes the template sets PROMPT_TEMPLATE_VERSION (src/domain/prompt.ts:8) to current+1 in merge order (looks is
first), and the first PR to touch test/remix-run.test.ts:176 makes it import the constant. Untrusted names go in fences
via sanitizeBrief (:106).

## Approach
- PromptInput.look?: { id, name } | null and restyle?: boolean; buildFitPrompt gets look too.
- When look is set, right after the "Read context/ first …" line (src/domain/prompt.ts:137), add (exact wording from spec §4.6 step 4): "The look for this video is in
  context/look/ (prepare-run puts it there). Read context/look/LOOK.md before you design anything.
  context/look/example/ shows how its rules become a composition: skim the scene that matches the one you're writing,
  and reuse its structure and building blocks, never its words or media. The look governs layout, type scale, pacing,
  motion, transitions, textures and how colour roles are used. The brand in context/ still decides colours, logo,
  fonts and wording; where they disagree, the brand wins, and the request wins over both. Write any colour role you
  derive as a literal colour. Copy any look asset you use (textures, effects) into video/assets/look/, and add a
  credits line for any that needs one. Its name, as JSON:" then a fenced sanitised {"id","name"}.
- When restyle (version.look.restyle, task 2.1; revisions AND remixes into another look): "This is a restyle into
  that look. Apart from what the request asks to change, keep the story: the scenes in order, their beat ids, the on-screen
  words (and their data-va-text ids), the media and any voice-over. Rebuild how it looks and moves to follow the look.
  A scene's length may change by up to a quarter where the look's pacing needs it, never shorter than its voice-over
  (run npx tsx scripts/voice.ts sync after any timing change); the total stays within the target."
  The opening clause "Apart from what the request asks to change," is the only change from the spec's §4.6 wording
  (polish 2026-11-05): a remix into another look is a restyle too, and a new-topic remix ("same format, about
  webhooks", README "Remix a video") must rewrite the words the plain wording says to keep. It follows the precedence
  rule (§3: the request wins over everything).
- buildFitPrompt: the look lines, never the restyle lines. buildRenderUnchangedPrompt: never mentions a look.
- PROMPT_TEMPLATE_VERSION = current + 1; test/remix-run.test.ts imports the constant instead of the literal 16.
- Do NOT regenerate test/fixtures/prompt-silent.txt.

## Done when
Prompts match the spec; the golden fixture still passes unchanged.

## Tests
Unit: no look -> byte-identical golden; look lines appear once, the name fenced and sanitised (a name containing >>>
can't close the fence); restyle adds the restyle lines; fit prompt gets look lines but not restyle lines;
render-unchanged prompt never mentions a look; snapshot tests for a look and a restyle prompt.
Also: a remix prompt with restyle true has the remix lines and the restyle lines in that order; a revision with

description:

Line refs are as of e477294.
Spec key: 2.6a
Spec section(s): §4.9, §4.13, §10 2.6

## Background
The REST API is the source of truth for the web app, SDK and MCP. Cross-plan rules: every route carries an operationId
and an explicit x-sdk name ({ resource, method }) so the SDK is generated (CLI/SDK plan draft 3); the version DTO grows
additively (editable stays); webhooks embed the DTO (src/domain/webhooks.ts:56-57), so look reaches them for free;
the features list in GET /api/v1/config is owned by the CLI/SDK plan's phase 1.2 and each plan adds its own string.
Needs: CLI/SDK plan phase 1 (operationId + x-sdk on every route, the features list).

## Approach
- x-sdk feature gating (shared rule from CLI bead va-p1th.2.1: x-sdk is { resource, method, feature?,
  fieldFeatures? }; zod drops unknown body fields, so an older server would silently ignore `look` and still answer
  202; the generated SDK refuses with unsupported_by_server when GET /config's features lacks the string). Set in
  this PR:
  - listLooks: x-sdk { resource: 'looks', method: 'list', feature: 'looks' } (the route only exists with looks);
  - createVideo, reviseVideo, remixVideo: add fieldFeatures { look: 'looks' }, merged with any entries other plans
    set on the same route (createVideo also carries engine: 'engines' from the render-engines plan);
  - the admin settings PATCH route (task 2.6b's fields): fieldFeatures { defaultLook: 'looks', disabledLooks:
    'looks' }, set by task 2.6b;
  - createPlan's look: fieldFeatures { look: 'looks' }, set by task 3.5a.
- GET /api/v1/looks, operationId listLooks, x-sdk as above, any signed-in role:
  { looks: [{ id, name, description, tags, bestFor, aspects, engines, recording, hash, enabled, preview: { mp4,
  poster } }], default: string | null }. Every catalog look is listed with enabled (no look is secret; names and descriptions are
  visible to every signed-in role).
- look?: string | null (z.string().regex(slug).nullable().optional()) on POST /api/v1/videos, /videos/{id}/revise,
  /videos/{id}/remix (src/schemas.ts create/revise/remix bodies), described per §4.3.
- Version DTO: look: { id, name, hash } | null. `hash` is additive to spec §4.9's { id, name } (polish
  2026-11-05): the live test proves a retry kept the old snapshot by comparing it with GET /looks' hash after a
  deploy changed the look (the API exposes no manifest or source.tar.gz: the file enum is video, poster, gif,
  captions, narration-audio, transcript, src/app.ts:151-155), the Restyle picker uses it to tell "same look" from
  "updated look", and §12's "updated since" needs it later. Key, sha256 and bytes stay server-side.
- Errors: 400 unknown_look; 409 look_disabled; 400 look_not_allowed (render-unchanged, fit, scope); 409
  look_not_allowed (narrated restyle, through ApiError's status override, task 2.2a); 400
  engine_not_supported_by_look; 409 engine_disabled; the aspect notice in the version's notices. Each route's
  OpenAPI error list names the codes it can return.
- POST /api/v1/edits/{id}/render: RenderEditSchema's refused `look` field (task 2.2c) appears in the spec as "not
  accepted".
- features: add 'looks'.
- npm run openapi:gen (ui/src/api/openapi.json + UI types); openapi:check green.

## Done when
The endpoints and fields are live in the harness and the OpenAPI spec; the SDK coverage test (once it exists) sees listLooks.

## Tests
Integration: GET /looks for each role; create/revise/remix with look through the HTTP layer; DTO and webhook payload
carry look; each error code and HTTP status; openapi:check; operationId/x-sdk uniqueness test passes.
Also: GET /looks returns hash for every entry and the DTO's look.hash equals the snapshot's; GET /config
features includes 'looks'; a narrated restyle returns HTTP 409 with code look_not_allowed and a render with look
returns 400 with the same code; a Viewer can GET /looks but gets 403 on create with look (role rules unchanged).
x-sdk: the OpenAPI spec has feature 'looks' on listLooks and fieldFeatures.look = 'looks' on createVideo,
reviseVideo and remixVideo (a spec test). Once the generated SDK exists (CLI/SDK phase 2; task 4.1a runs it): the
SDK refuses `look` with `unsupported_by_server` against a server whose features don't list `looks`, and refuses
looks.list() the same way.

## Background
The planner's router returns a template (launch, tutorial, social, changelog, sales, other; src/domain/plans.ts:358-364).
The model choosing a look is not in v1 (independent review A4): the server picks deterministically, so the same plan
always gets the same look and there's no extra model output to validate. Choices reach the model as labelled data
blocks (chosen_shape, chosen_sound, :517-520).

## Approach
- POST /api/v1/plans accepts look?: string | null (schemas + OpenAPI regen); createPlan's x-sdk gets
  fieldFeatures { look: 'looks' } (shared rule, CLI bead va-p1th.2.1), merged with any other plan's entries.
- If the person chose one: the questions and brief steps get a chosen_look data block (name and one-liner) and never
  ask about style (add the rule line next to the sound rule at plans.ts:506-508).
- If not: pick the first enabled look in catalog order whose bestFor lists the router's template, else the admin
  default, else none; pass it as chosen_look.
- Explicit null stays none (resolveLook).
- The frozen plan stores look (FrozenPlan.look: string | null, the id; resolved against the catalog at create);
  createVideo uses it as planLook (task 2.2c) before the default. The snapshot copy must happen before createVideo's
  transaction, but consumePlan runs inside it (consumePlan, src/domain/videos.ts:102, called at :333 at 4c573aa), so createVideo

title: CLI, SDK and player: make videos from a terminal, from code, and on your own machine
description:
Project: video-agent, an open-source Netlify template that turns a prompt into a published MP4 via Netlify Agent Runner runs writing HyperFrames compositions; Hono+OpenAPI API, Netlify Database (Drizzle), Blobs, Identity, React+Mantine UI, MCP. Feature: CLI, SDK and player (netlify-video-agent with bin video-agent, netlify-video-agent-sdk, netlify-video-agent-player): make videos from a terminal, from code, and on your own machine with your own coding agent (local mode). Spec: docs/plans/2026-11-04-cli-and-sdk.md (draft 3, commit e477294; review logs at its end, §16). Line refs are as of e477294.
Spec key: EPIC
Spec section(s): all (§0-§16)

## Background
Owner ask (2026-11-04): "We need a CLI for this" (idea #1: run the video loop locally with your own agent) and "we want
proper CLI that uses proper SDK and we can add to docs section" (idea #14, which includes the player). One plan for all
of it: the CLI's remote commands are built only on the SDK, and local mode is a CLI command.

What ships (§0): three public npm packages, one private workspace package, a few server changes.
- netlify-video-agent-sdk: typed client for a deployment's REST API. Resource methods GENERATED from the OpenAPI spec
  using an explicit x-sdk name per route (va.videos.create, va.versions.publish…), plus hand-written helpers for
  multi-request jobs (wait, download, upload, music jobs, webhooks, feature checks).
- netlify-video-agent (bin video-agent): remote commands over the SDK, with --json and stable exit codes for agents;
  and `video-agent local …`, which makes a video ON YOUR MACHINE with Claude Code, Codex or Gemini CLI inside that
  agent's OS sandbox, with no Netlify account.
- netlify-video-agent-player: <video-agent-player>, a small web component for published videos (later phase, in scope).
- packages/action: private workspace package owned by the github-action plan; never published to npm.
Plus /docs/cli and /docs/sdk under a docs navigation that scales; `video-agent login` (approve in the browser, get an
API key); operationIds + x-sdk on every route; version + features in GET /api/v1/config; /v/{slug}.json.

Positioning (owner decision 2026-11-04): "make one locally, then deploy it for your team". Local mode is the front
door; review, editor, publishing, API/MCP, queue, planning and the shared library stay hosted (§6.7). Every local run
ends with one line pointing at the Deploy to Netlify button.

This plan is the HUB for the five other 2026-11-04 plans (§12): it owns the features registry, operationIds/x-sdk and
the coverage test, the SDK, the CLI catalog and exit-code rule, packages/ workspaces + Changesets + trusted publishing,
local mode's runtime bundle (prepare-run --inputs), and the docs navigation. Other plans add their own routes, SDK
helpers (redoScenes, uploadRecording), CLI commands (scenes/redo, looks/restyle, --engine, demo, record, brief) and
docs pages on top of this groundwork, in their own beads.

Reviews: independent Fable 5.1, cross-plan seam review, remote Fable 5.1 high in a Netlify Agent Run (all "sound with
changes"; logs in §16). Key changes they forced: names (video-agent and @video-agent are taken), OS sandbox as the
boundary (tool allowlists aren't), keys can't create keys (device flow mints at claim), file: callback instead of a
loopback server, local mode decoupled from render-engines, nothing on npmjs before the repo is public.

Owner questions (§13):
- Q1 DECIDED (2026-11-04): unscoped names netlify-video-agent (CLI, bin video-agent), netlify-video-agent-sdk,
  netlify-video-agent-player; no npm org (the @video-agent scope is someone else's).
- Q2 DECIDED (2026-11-04): ship local mode, framed "make one locally, then deploy it for your team".
- Q3 open: CLI login on every deployment by default? BUILDING: yes, with the cliLoginEnabled admin switch.
- Q4 open: where keys live? BUILDING: a 0600 config file; CI uses VIDEO_AGENT_KEY or --key - --no-save.
- Q5 open: local push to the team app? BUILDING: not in v1 (design in Considerations).
- Q6 open: publishing before the repo is public? BUILDING: npm pack tarballs internally; first npmjs publish from the
  public repo with provenance.
- Q7 open: /player.js served by every deployment? BUILDING: yes.
- Q8 open: an agent that can't finish inside its sandbox in C2? BUILDING: leave it out of v1 (Gemini is the likely one).
- Q9 open: server-side wait (rest_wait)? BUILDING: not in v1; If-None-Match polling.
Other owner decisions applied: live tests run --dry then ask the owner before each gate (no blanket approval).

## Approach
Phases (§11), each ending in a gate bead; gates chain where the plan says so:
0 spikes C1-C4 (bundled runtime, sandboxed agents, Kokoro venv, npm placeholders); 1 API groundwork (operationIds +
x-sdk, version + features, request ids, oasdiff warning job, workspaces, /v/{slug}.json); 2 the SDK; 3 the CLI's remote
commands + device login; 4 local mode; 5 the player; 6 docs, nav and README; 7 release.
Parallelism: phases 0 and 1 together; then 2, 4 (needs C1-C3 and 3.1 only) and 5 together; the rest of 3 after 2.
Live tests (LT-1 SDK, LT-2 CLI, LT-3 local with real agents) are their own gate beads and block the release gate.

## Done when
Every phase epic closed; LT-1..LT-3 passed with owner approval; CI green; the fresh-machine check (7.3) passes; the plan
gets an as-built note (deviations, credits spent).

## Tests
Per bead. Live tests: scripts/e2e/sdk.ts, scripts/e2e/cli.ts (production, owner-approved, credit ceilings), and a manual
local-mode run per shipped agent (tester's own subscriptions). CI: a fixture-agent local-mode job (4.8).

Standard: unit and integration with createApp(fakeDeps) (test/helpers.ts harness) and PGlite (pgStore(), every migration applied); Playwright on the mock build (VITE_MOCK=1) for UI; structured JSON logs (one event per step, with ids, durations and outcome) so failures are diagnosable from logs alone. CI (npm run typecheck, lint, vitest, npx playwright test, openapi:check, db:check) stays green. Repo rule: when checks pass, commit only your own files, push to main and confirm the Netlify production deploy is ready (other sessions often have uncommitted files in the checkout; never stage them).

## Considerations
Not in v1, designed (§14), so nothing is lost:
- local preview <dir> (unpack source, npx hyperframes preview --background = HyperFrames Studio); local render <dir>
  (render-unchanged run without an agent, render-job only); local init (writes ./context/ BRAND.md template, brand.json,
  assets/, and video-agent.json defaults: agent, aspect, sound, output folder); local list (videos under ./videos/).
- Named profiles: profiles list|use|remove, --profile, VIDEO_AGENT_PROFILE, config { current, profiles: { <name>: {
  url, apiKey, keyId } } }.
- CLI `webhooks verify --secret <s> [--signature <h>] < body` (exit 0/1) and `music search|import` commands (the SDK
  methods ship in v1).
- Runtime matrix beyond Node 22/24: Deno, Bun, a Vite-bundled browser smoke test.
- local push: import API taking a local source.tar.gz + outputs, verified server-side with a render-unchanged run (Q5).
- LocalRunnerPort for netlify dev: RUNNER=local only with ALLOW_NON_PRODUCTION=true; start spawns the local executor
  with the server's own prompt, snapshot reads the child, stop uses proc-tree. The file half (prepare-run --inputs)
  ships in v1; the other half needs render-job's already-typed `signed` upload mode (prompt.ts:22, :112, not
  implemented in render-job) plus dev-only upload/fetch endpoints, because netlify blobs:get/set hit the linked
  project's real stores, not netlify dev's emulated ones.
- Native Windows (WSL works; config would live under %APPDATA%).
- rest_wait: ?wait=<0-10> on GET /api/v1/videos/{id}, reusing the MCP loop (src/mcp.ts:541-545), honouring
  If-None-Match; 60 s sync function limit makes 10 s safe; billed function time, so measure against If-None-Match
  polling (requests and GB-s per finished video) and ship only on a clear win; advertised as rest_wait (reserved string).
- Interactive terminal planning (arrow-key choices, write-ins, skip, accept the brief); v1 prints questions and takes
  --answers.
- local --engine remotion (after render-engines phase 2 and its licence decision): refuses without
  --accept-remotion-license, prints that plan's notice once; runtime bundle carries engines/remotion/template/ (lockfile
  only; npm ci at run time with registry.npmjs.org added to the sandbox network allowlist).
- --pass-env NAME for ELEVENLABS_API_KEY / OPENVERSE_CLIENT_*: passes one variable and adds its host to the allowlist;
  out of v1 because it puts a secret where an injected instruction could read it.
- Player extras: hover-preview (muted hover clip from /v/{slug}.json `hover`), theming (::part(video), ::part(credits),
  --va-player-radius, --va-player-background).
- CLI variants of every skill recipe (changelog, social cut, localise, review).
- Plan-with-questions locally; the browser editor locally; Python/Go SDKs; a React wrapper for the player; admin
  commands beyond `api`; OAuth for REST; the OS keychain; telemetry of any kind.
Risks (§15): agent CLI flags drift (live test checks --help); sandboxes differ by OS (C2 on macOS and Linux; doctor
explains); local failures runners don't have (doctor, --keep, agent.log, run.jsonl); bundle drift (fixture CI job runs
the bundle); prompt injection via inputs (fences + sandbox + deny lists + env scrub + network allowlist); device-flow
phishing and lockout; settings that quietly reopen the host (allowLocalBinding, broad Seatbelt profiles: never set);
no spend cap for Codex/Gemini subscriptions (max-turns, timeouts); monorepo install time (hoisted devDeps, measured);
support load (stated matrix); Netlify positioning (decided: ship).

title: C1: spike the bundled run-script runtime with pinned tools and prepare-run --inputs
description:
Project: video-agent, an open-source Netlify template that turns a prompt into a published MP4 via Netlify Agent Runner runs writing HyperFrames compositions; Hono+OpenAPI API, Netlify Database (Drizzle), Blobs, Identity, React+Mantine UI, MCP. Spec key: C1
Spec section(s): §11 Phase 0 C1; §6.3; §6.4

## Background
Local mode can't use the repo checkout: it ships bundled copies of the run scripts. Today every script finds video/,
.render/ and context/ from repoRoot = the script's own location (scripts/lib/run-tools.ts:12); render-job runs an
UNPINNED `npx -y hyperframes render` (scripts/render-job.ts:202), which off the runner would fetch hyperframes@latest
and tsx on every run using the person's ~/.npmrc credentials; prepare-run fetches inputs only with netlify blobs:get
(scripts/prepare-run.ts:53-55); netlify-agent-kit install skips off the runner unless --force, and with --force writes
~/.cache/netlify-agent-kit and links into ~/.local/bin (agent-kit README "What it changes").

## Approach
Prototype (throwaway branch or scratch dir; nothing merged):
1. esbuild-bundle prepare-run, render-job, checkpoint, check-contract, voice, openverse, narration (and engine.ts /
   recording.ts if they exist) to ESM .mjs.
2. Build a workspace: video/ template copy, context/ default, root AGENTS.md, scripts/<name>.ts one-line shims
   (`import '<runtime>/render-job.mjs'`), VA_REPO_ROOT=<ws>.
3. Pinned runtime at ~/.cache/video-agent/runtime/<ver>/: npm ci of exact hyperframes (0.8.222), tsx, netlify-agent-kit
   from a lockfile; node_modules symlinks in <ws> and <ws>/video; its .bin first on PATH; empty npm_config_userconfig.
4. Run `netlify-agent-kit install --force` in the workspace with HOME=~/.cache/video-agent/agent-kit-home; add that
   home's .local/bin to PATH.
5. Write a v1 run manifest pointing at <ws>/.va-inputs/<store>/<key>; run prepare-run with a prototype --inputs mode;
   then render-job with a prototype --upload local and a file:// callback on a fixture composition.
Matrix: macOS (Apple silicon) and Linux (Ubuntu), Node 22 and 24. Second run with npm_config_offline=true.

## Done when
Pass: an MP4 with the same hashes as the repo's own render of the fixture; no network fetch of tools on the second run;
nothing written to the real ~/.local/bin or ~/.cache/netlify-agent-kit; runtime size and first-install time measured.

4.3a installs skills/Chrome/ffmpeg itself (copy dist/skills from the pinned hyperframes package, npx hyperframes browser);

title: C2: spike each agent CLI headless inside its OS sandbox (Claude Code, Codex, Gemini)
description:
Project: video-agent, an open-source Netlify template that turns a prompt into a published MP4 via Netlify Agent Runner runs writing HyperFrames compositions; Hono+OpenAPI API, Netlify Database (Drizzle), Blobs, Identity, React+Mantine UI, MCP. Feature: CLI, SDK and player (netlify-video-agent with bin video-agent, netlify-video-agent-sdk, netlify-video-agent-player): make videos from a terminal, from code, and on your own machine with your own coding agent (local mode). Spec: docs/plans/2026-11-04-cli-and-sdk.md (draft 3, commit e477294; review logs at its end, §16). Line refs are as of e477294.
Spec key: C2
Spec section(s): §11 Phase 0 C2; §6.5; §1 Agent CLIs; §2 gotchas 10-11

## Background
The reviews established that a tool allowlist is not a boundary (Write + Bash(npx tsx scripts/*) is arbitrary code;
Read/cat reach ~/.ssh, ~/.aws, ~/.netlify and the CLI's own config holding an nva_ key) and that the person's own agent
config (hooks, MCP servers/connectors, plugins, memory files) loads into a run unless suppressed. The OS sandbox is the
boundary. Claude Code's sandbox wraps Bash only; Read/Write/Edit/Glob/Grep run in-process under permission rules. On
Linux a sandboxed command's localhost is private; macOS Seatbelt allows only the sandbox proxy; allowLocalBinding
(macOS only) reopens every localhost service and is never set. Gemini headless auto_edit denies every shell command,
workspace policy files don't apply, and its default macOS profile permissive-open allows broad reads and all network.
Codex workspace-write blocks network by default. `-p --output-format stream-json` requires --verbose in Claude Code.
Flags seen on the author's machine (2026-11-04): claude 2.1.280 (--verbose, --permission-mode dontAsk, --settings,
--setting-sources, --strict-mcp-config, --max-turns, --max-budget-usd), codex-cli 0.157.1 (exec, -s, -C,
--skip-git-repo-check, --json, -o, -c, --dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox), gemini (-p, --approval-mode,
-s/--sandbox, -o stream-json, undocumented --policy).

## Approach
Order: needs C1's workspace (bundle, shims, pinned runtime) and C3's model-download hosts for the network
allowlist, so it starts once both are done (dependency edges on C1 and C3). With the C1 workspace and the real
buildPrompt output, run each agent twice: a silent 15 s video, then a narrated one
with music, using the §6.5 settings:
- Claude Code: claude -p <prompt> --verbose --output-format stream-json --permission-mode dontAsk --setting-sources ""
  --strict-mcp-config --max-turns <n> --settings <ws>/.va/claude.json (sandbox.enabled, failIfUnavailable,
  allowUnsandboxedCommands false, autoAllowBashIfSandboxed, sandbox.network.allowedDomains, sandbox.filesystem.denyRead,
  plus permissions.deny for the same paths and for Read/Glob/Grep outside the workspace; allow Bash, Read, Write, Edit,
  Glob, Grep; deny WebFetch, WebSearch). Linux needs bubblewrap + socat.
- Codex: codex exec -C <ws> --skip-git-repo-check --ephemeral --sandbox workspace-write
  -c sandbox_workspace_write.network_access=true -c 'shell_environment_policy.inherit="none"'
  -c 'shell_environment_policy.set={…}' --json -o <ws>/.render/last.txt, deny-read permissions, no user MCP config.
- Gemini: gemini -p <prompt> --sandbox --approval-mode yolo -o stream-json, custom Seatbelt profile on macOS, Docker or
  Podman on Linux with only the workspace mounted, a workspace-only settings home; never write ~/.gemini/policies.
Deny-read list: ~/.ssh ~/.aws ~/.config/gcloud ~/.azure ~/.netlify ~/.npmrc ~/.config/video-agent ~/.codex ~/.gemini
~/.claude (except what the agent needs to authenticate before the sandboxed shell starts) ~/.docker ~/.kube ~/.gnupg.
Network allowlist: api.openverse.org + Openverse audio hosts (Jamendo, Freesound, Wikimedia Commons), the HyperFrames
model hosts (from C3), the agent's own API host.
Canaries: a file in a deny-read folder (try `cat` AND the agent's own Read tool), a canary env var, a canary HTTP
server on the host's 127.0.0.1, and a canary in the person's OWN agent config (on a throwaway test account: a user-level
hook and an MCP server entry in ~/.claude/settings.json, ~/.codex/config.toml and ~/.gemini/settings.json, plus a

title: operationId + x-sdk on every route, with a coverage test
description:
Project: video-agent, an open-source Netlify template that turns a prompt into a published MP4 via Netlify Agent Runner runs writing HyperFrames compositions; Hono+OpenAPI API, Netlify Database (Drizzle), Blobs, Identity, React+Mantine UI, MCP. Feature: CLI, SDK and player (netlify-video-agent with bin video-agent, netlify-video-agent-sdk, netlify-video-agent-player): make videos from a terminal, from code, and on your own machine with your own coding agent (local mode). Spec: docs/plans/2026-11-04-cli-and-sdk.md (draft 3, commit e477294; review logs at its end, §16). Line refs are as of e477294.
Spec key: 1.1
Spec section(s): §4.1 (How generated names are chosen), §4.4, §5.1 item 1, §2 gotcha 2

## Background
The spec has no operationIds (grep -c operationId ui/src/api/openapi.json = 0). Routes use createRoute({ method, path,
summary, description, tags, … }) (e.g. src/app.ts:464-467, tag versions); every route already has a tag. 67 paths (66
under /api/v1) and 91 operations on 2026-11-04 (other sessions add routes). The SDK's resource layer is generated from
an explicit per-route SDK name (review A3, owner constraint: generated names must read well), never derived from paths
or operationIds, so naming is a decision a reviewer sees in the route's diff.

## Approach
- Add to every createRoute an operationId (unique, camelCase, verb first) and an `x-sdk` vendor extension. Check how
  @hono/zod-openapi 1.6.3 passes `x-` keys from createRoute into the operation object (OpenAPI allows spec extensions
  on operations); if it drops them, set them through the route's `openapi` metadata and assert they reach app.spec().
- x-sdk shape (src/lib/sdk-meta.ts exports the type, so routes and scripts/gen-sdk.ts share it):
  `false` (no SDK method; still reachable through va.raw) or
  `{ resource: string, method: string, feature?: string, fieldFeatures?: Record<string, string> }`.
  `feature`: the features string the whole operation needs (e.g. listLooks → 'looks'). `fieldFeatures`: input fields
  that a feature added to an older route (e.g. createVideo { look: 'looks', engine: 'engines' }, reviseVideo
  { scope: 'scoped_revision' }). Zod strips unknown body fields, so an older server would silently ignore `look`;
  the generated SDK method checks these before sending (2.1/2.2) and throws unsupported_by_server instead. Each later
  plan sets fieldFeatures on the routes it extends, in the same PR.
- Proposed names for today's routes (re-check against HEAD; any route added since gets a name in the same style):
  system: GET /api/health getHealth false; GET /api/v1/config getConfig config.get (the cached helper replaces it).
  videos: POST /videos createVideo videos.create; GET /videos listVideos videos.list; PUT|DELETE
  /videos/{id}/favorite favoriteVideo videos.favorite, unfavoriteVideo videos.unfavorite; GET|PATCH|DELETE
  /videos/{id} getVideo videos.get, updateVideo videos.update, deleteVideo videos.delete; POST /videos/{id}/versions
  reviseVideo videos.revise; POST /videos/{id}/remix remixVideo videos.remix; GET /videos/{id}/progress
  getVideoProgress videos.progress (draft 3 said versions.progress, but the route is per video and takes no n).
  versions (/videos/{id}/versions/{n}/…): GET media listVersionMedia versions.media; POST retry retryVersion
  versions.retry; POST cancel cancelVersion versions.cancel; POST|DELETE publish publishVersion versions.publish,
  unpublishVersion versions.unpublish; PUT verdict setVerdict versions.setVerdict; POST captions correctCaptions
  versions.captions; PUT|DELETE poster setPoster versions.setPoster, resetPoster versions.resetPoster; GET preview
  getVersionPreview versions.preview; GET {file} getVersionFile false (302; the files.url/files.download helpers wrap
  it); PUT previews/{name} addPreviewVariant false (admin backfill).
  keys and me: GET /keys listKeys keys.list; POST /keys createKey false (web session only, keys.ts:17-20); DELETE
  /keys/{id} revokeKey keys.revoke; GET /oauth/grants listGrants grants.list; DELETE /oauth/grants/{id} revokeGrant
  grants.revoke; GET /me getMe me.get; GET /me/usage getUsage me.usage; GET|PUT|DELETE /me/webhook getWebhook
  webhooks.get, setWebhook webhooks.set, deleteWebhook webhooks.delete; POST /me/webhook/test testWebhook webhooks.test.
  planning: POST /plans createPlan plans.create; GET /plans/{id} getPlan plans.get; POST /plans/{id}/questions
  askPlanQuestions plans.questions; POST /plans/{id}/brief writePlanBrief plans.brief; PATCH /plans/{id} updatePlan
  plans.update.
  notifications: GET /notifications listNotifications notifications.list; POST /notifications/read
  markNotificationsRead notifications.markRead.
  media: POST /media uploadMedia false (binary body; media.upload helper); GET /media listMedia media.list; POST
  /media/check checkMedia media.check; GET /media/{id} getMedia media.get; PATCH updateMedia media.update; DELETE
  deleteMedia media.delete; GET /videos/{id}/recordings listRecordings media.recordings (no cursor, not pageable);
  POST /media/recordings/delete-unused deleteUnusedRecordings media.deleteUnusedRecordings; upload sessions POST
  /media/uploads createUpload uploads.create, GET /media/uploads/{id} getUpload uploads.get, PUT parts/{index}
  uploadPart false (binary), POST complete completeUpload uploads.complete, DELETE abortUpload uploads.abort;
  peaks and speech (PUT|GET /media/{id}/peaks, /speech) false (editor internals).
  music (/media/openverse/…): GET search searchMusic music.search; GET library searchLibraryMusic music.library; GET
  common listCommonMusic music.common; POST import importMusic music.import; GET jobs/{id} getMusicJob music.job.
  comments: GET|POST /videos/{id}/comments listComments comments.list, addComment comments.add; POST batch
  addComments comments.addBatch; POST read markCommentsRead comments.markRead; PATCH|DELETE /comments/{id}
  updateComment comments.update, deleteComment comments.delete.
  false (web app or admin; raw only): every /edits/… and /versions/{n}/edits route and the narration-lock routes
  (createEdit, getEdit, saveEdit, discardEdit, renderEdit, rebaseEditNarration, getEditPreview, getNarrationLock,
  takeNarrationLock, releaseNarrationLock, takeOverNarrationLock); /users (listUsers, updateUser); /admin/*
  (getTeamWebhook, setTeamWebhook, deleteTeamWebhook, testTeamWebhook, getSettings, updateSettings, resolveAttempt,
  resumeQueue); POST /transfers transferVideos; GET /stats getStats; /api/internal/runs/{id}/done and /checkpoint
  (runDone, runCheckpoint).
- Names other plans rely on must be reachable once their routes exist: videos.create/get/list/revise/remix/favorite,
  versions.retry/cancel/publish/unpublish/setVerdict/captions, videos.progress, versions.beats (regenerate-beat:
  GET /api/v1/videos/{id}/versions/{n}/beats, operationId getVersionBeats; videos.redoScenes is its hand-written sugar), plans.create/questions/brief,
  comments.list/add/addBatch, media.check/list/get/delete/setTrace/getTrace (screen plan), music.search/import,
  looks.list (looks plan), engines.list (engines plan), keys.list/revoke, me.get/usage.
- Test (test/openapi-ids.test.ts): every operation has a tag, a unique camelCase verb-first operationId (/^[a-z]+[A-Z][A-Za-z0-9]*$/,
  the leading word a verb), and an x-sdk value of the right shape (resource and method camelCase identifiers); no two
  operations share { resource, method }. Regenerate openapi.json (npm run openapi:gen).
- Rule for every later PR in any plan: new routes carry both, or this test fails.

## Done when
Every route has both; the test passes; openapi.json regenerated; the REST reference (Scalar) shows operationIds.

## Tests
Unit test over app.spec() (via createApp(makeDeps()), as scripts/gen-openapi.ts builds it), failing with the method and
path of each offender: missing operationId, duplicate operationId, missing or malformed x-sdk, duplicate
{ resource, method }. A committed snapshot (test/__snapshots__ or a JSON file) of the full
{ method path → operationId, x-sdk } table so every rename shows in review. A small fixture route with an x-sdk
extension proves the extension survives into the generated spec.

description:

## Background
Forks deploy whenever they like, so SDK releases meet older servers. GET /api/v1/config is public (auth skipped,
src/app.ts:238) and returns PublicConfigSchema (src/schemas.ts:1496: admission, siteUrl, planningAvailable, mcpOAuth,
authProvider, requiredTeams, remixEnabled, narrationEnabled…) but no version and no feature list. The root package.json
version is 0.0.0, private and never bumped, so it can't identify a deployment (review A10). This plan OWNS the features
registry; every other plan adds only its own string in its own PR.

## Approach
- PublicConfigSchema gains version: { commit: string | null (Netlify's COMMIT_REF at build time), promptTemplate:
  number (PROMPT_TEMPLATE_VERSION, src/domain/prompt.ts:8), release: string | null (a template release tag when the
  build has one) } and features: string[].
- Registry (snake_case), documented in src/domain/features.ts with one line each: remix, narration, planning, rest_wait
  (RESERVED, not emitted in v1), cli_login, looks, engines, scoped_revision, screen_recording, context, external_ref.
  A string appears only when the deployment has the feature AND it's switched on (remix only when remixEnabled, etc.).
- Phase 1 emits remix (settings remixEnabled), narration (narrationEnabled), planning (planningAvailable: AI Gateway
  present); cli_login is added by 3.3a (cliLoginEnabled). Export FEATURES (the registry, as a readonly tuple) and
  `type Feature` from src/domain/features.ts; the SDK coverage test (2.5) checks x-sdk feature strings against it.
- Build info: scripts/build.ts writes src/generated/build-info.ts (committed with nulls, overwritten at build like
  src/generated/context.ts) with commit = process.env.COMMIT_REF (Netlify build variable) ?? null and release = the tag
  from `git describe --tags --exact-match HEAD` when it matches ^v\d (our template releases), else null. The function
  reads it at runtime; build-time vars like COMMIT_REF aren't reliably present in function env. OpenAPI regenerated.

## Done when
Config returns version and features; switches reflected; OpenAPI and UI types regenerated; docs comment lists the registry.

Integration via createApp(fakeDeps) (test/helpers.ts harness(), GET /api/v1/config without auth): features follow
admin switches (PATCH /api/v1/admin/settings remixEnabled false → no remix; narration off → no narration; planning only
with the Gateway fake); version.promptTemplate equals PROMPT_TEMPLATE_VERSION (imported, never a literal);
version.commit/release null with the committed build-info; a test that every emitted string is in FEATURES and that

title: Surface Netlify's x-nf-request-id in API errors for the SDK and CLI
description:

Feature: CLI, SDK and player (netlify-video-agent with bin video-agent, netlify-video-agent-sdk, netlify-video-agent-player): make videos from a terminal, from code, and on your own machine with your own coding agent (local mode). Spec: docs/plans/2026-11-04-cli-and-sdk.md (draft 3, commit e477294; review logs at its end, §16). Line refs are as of e477294.
Spec key: 1.5
Spec section(s): §4.4 Breaking-change check; §5.1 item 5

## Background
The API is additive within /api/v1; that's the policy the SDK relies on. oasdiff (github.com/oasdiff/oasdiff) detects
breaking changes between two OpenAPI files. Reviews: keep it a warning job in v1; blocking from the SDK's 1.0.

## Approach
New job in .github/workflows/ci.yml: check out main's ui/src/api/openapi.json, run a pinned oasdiff `breaking` (release
binary or npx with an exact version) against the PR's file, post the result as a job summary/annotation, never fail in
v1. Document the 1.0 rule (blocking unless label api-breaking + a major SDK changeset) in the workflow comment and
CONTRIBUTING notes.

## Done when
The job runs on PRs, reports breaking changes as warnings, and passes.

## Tests
Verify on a throwaway branch that removing a field produces a warning; the job logs the oasdiff command and version.

Standard: unit and integration with createApp(fakeDeps) (test/helpers.ts harness) and PGlite (pgStore(), every migration applied); Playwright on the mock build (VITE_MOCK=1) for UI; structured JSON logs (one event per step, with ids, durations and outcome) so failures are diagnosable from logs alone. ## Background
One repo keeps route, SDK method, CLI command and docs in one commit and one CI run. Runners run npm install at the
root (agent-kit README), which installs every workspace's deps, so packages must add almost nothing (review A11). No
packages/ folder and no workspaces exist yet. Local npm 10 strips libc fields from the lockfile; use npx npm@11 install
(memory: lockfile-npm-11).

## Approach
- Root package.json: "workspaces": ["packages/*"]; root stays the private Node-24 app.
- packages/sdk (netlify-video-agent-sdk), packages/cli (netlify-video-agent, bin video-agent), packages/player
  (netlify-video-agent-player), packages/action (private: true, owned by the github-action plan; never published,
  excluded from Changesets). Each: package.json (ESM, exports, files, engines node >=22 for sdk/cli), tsconfig,
  src/index.ts stub, test/ stub. No devDependencies in packages; everything (esbuild, TypeScript, Vitest, Playwright,
  Changesets) hoisted to the root. SDK and player: no runtime dependencies.

  tsc -b packages/*/tsconfig.json; ESLint and vitest cover packages/ (including packages/action).
- Lockfile regenerated with npx npm@11 install.
- Measure the runner's install time without spending extra credits: compare the setup step's duration of the first
  ordinary production runs after this merges (Agent Runs data) with the previous week's median. If a dedicated run is
  needed after all, it is a live action: print what it does and its projected credits, and ASK THE OWNER first.
- Also time `npm ci` at the root locally and in CI before and after (no credits), so a regression shows before merge.

Workspaces install, build, typecheck, lint and test in CI; packages are empty stubs; setup time within 5% of before.

title: /v/{slug}.json: serve the oEmbed JSON the share page already advertises, plus player metadata and the video id
description:
Project: video-agent, an open-source Netlify template that turns a prompt into a published MP4 via Netlify Agent Runner runs writing HyperFrames compositions; Hono+OpenAPI API, Netlify Database (Drizzle), Blobs, Identity, React+Mantine UI, MCP. Feature: CLI, SDK and player (netlify-video-agent with bin video-agent, netlify-video-agent-sdk, netlify-video-agent-player): make videos from a terminal, from code, and on your own machine with your own coding agent (local mode). Spec: docs/plans/2026-11-04-cli-and-sdk.md (draft 3, commit e477294; review logs at its end, §16). Line refs are as of e477294.
Spec key: 1.7
Spec section(s): §5.3; §2 gotcha 13; §1 Files

## Background
The share page advertises <link rel="alternate" type="application/json+oembed" href="/v/{slug}.json">
(netlify/edge-functions/public.ts:106) but the handler's regex serves only mp4|jpg|gif|vtt|webp|mp3|txt (public.ts:53),
so it's a 404 today. The player (phase 5) needs exactly this metadata, and the CLI/SDK resolve share URLs to a video
through it (videos.resolve, 2.3a). Public files are served with access-control-allow-origin: * (public.ts:87). The
edge function reads the publication mirror pub/{slug}.json from the internal store (Mirror: slug, jobId, versionN,
title, width, height, durationSec, keys, credits?, showTranscript?; public.ts:10-30). The share page already exposes
the video id in its "Remix in Video Agent" link (/videos/{jobId}?remix={n}, public.ts:113), so returning it here
reveals nothing new. Small, so it lands early.

## Approach
Extend the regex to json. Response (application/json+oembed; charset=utf-8): oEmbed 1.0 (type "video", version "1.0",
title, provider_name (the site name or "Video Agent"), provider_url, width, height, thumbnail_url, thumbnail_width,
thumbnail_height, html = the embed snippet from embedHtml, src/domain/videos.ts:869 at e477294, used for the
publication DTO's embed at :862) plus video_agent: { videoId, versionN, mp4, poster, posterWebp, captions, durationSec,
credits, lqip, hover }. Mirror fields that exist today come straight from it (durationSec, credits, keys); lqip and the
hover clip key are added to the mirror at publish time, and older mirrors answer null for them (no backfill job).
CORS *, cache-control public, max-age=60. Unpublished or unknown slugs 404 like the page (plain JSON
{ error: "not_found" }). Every request re-reads the mirror, so unpublishing takes effect at once.

## Done when
GET /v/{slug}.json returns valid oEmbed + video_agent (with videoId and versionN) for a published version; 404 when
unpublished; CC BY credits included; lqip/hover null on old mirrors.

## Tests
Edge-function tests (test/edge.ts harness): published (every field, types), unpublished → 404, unknown slug → 404,
CC BY credits present, mirror without lqip/hover → nulls, posterWebp absent → null, CORS * and cache headers, HEAD;
the oEmbed required fields validated against the oEmbed 1.0 field list; the html field equals embedHtml's output for
the same version. Structured log line per request (slug, status, ms).

title: Generate SDK types and resource methods from the spec (gen-sdk.ts); UI re-exports the types
description:
Project: video-agent, an open-source Netlify template that turns a prompt into a published MP4 via Netlify Agent Runner runs writing HyperFrames compositions; Hono+OpenAPI API, Netlify Database (Drizzle), Blobs, Identity, React+Mantine UI, MCP. Feature: CLI, SDK and player (netlify-video-agent with bin video-agent, netlify-video-agent-sdk, netlify-video-agent-player): make videos from a terminal, from code, and on your own machine with your own coding agent (local mode). Spec: docs/plans/2026-11-04-cli-and-sdk.md (draft 3, commit e477294; review logs at its end, §16). Line refs are as of e477294.
Spec key: 2.1
Spec section(s): §4.1 layers 1-2, Generated signature rule; §4.3

## Background
Today openapi:gen writes ui/src/api/openapi.json then runs openapi-typescript@7.13.0 into ui/src/api/schema.d.ts
(package.json scripts). Generation wins for coverage and drift: a new route is in the SDK the day it merges, typed
(review A3). One generated schema shared with the UI so they can't disagree.

## Approach
- openapi:gen: openapi-typescript once into packages/sdk/src/generated/schema.d.ts; ui/src/api/schema.d.ts becomes a
  one-line re-export of it; then scripts/gen-sdk.ts writes packages/sdk/src/generated/resources.ts. openapi:check checks
  both generated files.
- gen-sdk.ts reads each operation's x-sdk { resource, method } and emits one namespace per resource, one thin typed
  method per operation. Signature rule: path params positionally in path order, then one `input` object (body fields
  and query fields merged; generation FAILS if a body field and a query field share a name), then opts
  ({ idempotencyKey?, signal?, headers? }). Input field names are the API's own (no renaming), so examples
  are va.versions.publish(id, n, { transcript: true }), va.videos.list({ owner: 'me', q: 'webhooks' }) (the list
  query is status, owner, published, favorite, q, cursor, limit), va.versions.retry(id, n), va.videos.progress(id). Binary-body routes (small media upload)
  are skipped (hand-written). x-sdk: false routes are skipped (reachable via raw).
- Feature gates: for an x-sdk with `feature`, the generated method calls the core's requireFeatures([feature]) (2.2)
  before the request; for each `fieldFeatures` entry it adds that feature when input[field] !== undefined. So
  va.videos.create({ look: 'clean' }) against a server without `looks` throws unsupported_by_server instead of the
  server silently dropping the field. Methods without either make no config request.
- Each generated method carries a JSDoc line from the route's summary and its operationId (so editors show it).
- Pageable marker: an operation is pageable only when its 200 response has items + nextCursor (RecordingListSchema,
  src/schemas.ts:911, has none), recorded for listAll's types (2.3a).
- Exported convenience types: Video, Version, Media, Plan, Comment, WebhookEvent derived from paths as
  ui/src/api/client.ts derives Video/Version.

## Done when
Generated files committed and checked in CI; UI typechecks against the re-export; generator deterministic.

## Tests
Generator unit tests on a small fixture spec (scripts/gen-sdk.test.ts): positional path params in path order, merged
body+query input, a body/query name clash fails with both names in the message, x-sdk false skipped, binary body
skipped, pageable detection (items + nextCursor only), feature and fieldFeatures emitted as requireFeatures calls (and
absent otherwise); determinism (two runs byte-equal); openapi:check fails on stale generated files; the UI typechecks
against the re-exported schema.d.ts.

Standard: unit and integration with createApp(fakeDeps) (test/helpers.ts harness) and PGlite (pgStore(), every migration applied); Playwright on the mock build (VITE_MOCK=1) for UI; structured JSON logs (one event per step, with ids, durations and outcome) so failures are diagnosable from logs alone. title: SDK core: VideoAgent client, auth, raw, redirects, errors, retries, idempotency, logger, User-Agent
description:
Project: video-agent, an open-source Netlify template that turns a prompt into a published MP4 via Netlify Agent Runner runs writing HyperFrames compositions; Hono+OpenAPI API, Netlify Database (Drizzle), Blobs, Identity, React+Mantine UI, MCP. Feature: CLI, SDK and player (netlify-video-agent with bin video-agent, netlify-video-agent-sdk, netlify-video-agent-player): make videos from a terminal, from code, and on your own machine with your own coding agent (local mode). Spec: docs/plans/2026-11-04-cli-and-sdk.md (draft 3, commit e477294; review logs at its end, §16). Line refs are as of e477294.
Spec key: 2.2
Spec section(s): §4.2; §2 gotchas 17, 17a

## Background
Behaviour every method shares. Facts: keys start nva_ (src/domain/auth.ts:88); errors are { error: { code, message } }
(ui/src/api/client.ts ApiErrorBody); rate limits answer rate_limited with Retry-After: 60 (src/app.ts:180);
Idempotency-Key accepted on create/revise/remix (src/app.ts:139, :334, :471, :498, :1233); the server hashes
JSON.stringify(body) and answers 409 conflict when a key returns with a different hash (src/domain/videos.ts:280-284),
TTL 24 h per user and operation (:54); file routes 302 to signed storage URLs valid 5-10 minutes (src/app.ts:676-707).

## Approach
- new VideoAgent({ url (or VIDEO_AGENT_URL), apiKey (or VIDEO_AGENT_KEY when process exists), userAgent?, fetch?,
  retries = 3, logger? }). User-Agent: netlify-video-agent-sdk/<version> (+<userAgent>) (draft 3 wrote
  video-agent-sdk/; the package name is clearer in a deployment's logs). apiKey is optional: without one the client
  sends no Authorization and can still call the unauthenticated routes (config, the CLI login create/claim routes,
  public /v/{slug}.json); a keyed route then fails with the server's 401 (exit 3 in the CLI).
- Feature gate (used by generated methods, 2.1): the client fetches GET /api/v1/config once (lazily, on the first
  gated call; one in-flight promise shared by concurrent calls) and caches { version, features }. requireFeatures(list)
  throws VideoAgentError { code: 'unsupported_by_server', status: 0, message: "This server (<commit or 'unknown'>)
  doesn't support <feature>. Update the deployment." }. A server older than phase 1 has no `features`: treat it as [].
  2.3c exposes config.get()/config.supports() over the same cache.
- raw: openapi-fetch (MIT, bundled into dist; no runtime deps) typed by generated paths, with auth, base URL, retries,
  errors.
- Redirects: authenticated requests use redirect: 'manual' and never follow with the key (file routes handled by 2.3b).
- Idempotency: create/revise/remix (and later redoScenes) send Idempotency-Key (opts.idempotencyKey or a UUID). The body
  is serialized ONCE and the same string is sent on every retry; a 409 on a retry is reported, never retried.
- Retries: GETs and keyed POSTs on network errors, 429 (Retry-After capped at 60 s) and 5xx, jittered backoff; other
  POSTs never retry.
- Errors: VideoAgentError { status, code, message, retryAfterSec?, requestId? (x-nf-request-id) }; isVideoAgentError(e,
  code).
- Logger: (event, fields) => void with request events (method, path, status, ms, attempt, requestId); never headers or
  bodies.
- No Node-only imports in the main entry.

## Done when
Client constructs from options or env; raw and generated methods authenticate, retry, map errors and log as specified.

## Tests
Unit (fetch stub, fake timers): retries/backoff and jitter bounds, Retry-After honoured and capped at 60 s, key reuse
and identical bytes across retries (assert body string equality on every attempt), 409-on-retry reported not retried,
unkeyed POST never retried, error mapping incl. requestId from x-nf-request-id and a non-JSON error body, redirect:
'manual' on every authenticated request (no Authorization ever sent to a redirect target), logger receives
{ method, path, status, ms, attempt, requestId } and never headers or bodies (serialize every logged event and grep
for nva_), config fetched once for many gated calls, unsupported_by_server for a missing feature and for a server
without `features`, no-key client calls config without Authorization. Integration: harness() from test/helpers.ts and
fetch: (req) => h.app.fetch(req), with a key from apiKey(h, h.member); create a video with an Idempotency-Key twice →
the same video (replayed).

Standard: unit and integration with createApp(fakeDeps) (test/helpers.ts harness) and PGlite (pgStore(), every migration applied); Playwright on the mock build (VITE_MOCK=1) for UI; structured JSON logs (one event per step, with ids, durations and outcome) so failures are diagnosable from logs alone. Feature: CLI, SDK and player (netlify-video-agent with bin video-agent, netlify-video-agent-sdk, netlify-video-agent-player): make videos from a terminal, from code, and on your own machine with your own coding agent (local mode). Spec: docs/plans/2026-11-04-cli-and-sdk.md (draft 3, commit e477294; review logs at its end, §16). Line refs are as of e477294.
Spec key: 2.3a
Spec section(s): §4.2 Waiting; §4.1 videos row; §1 ETags

## Background
GET /api/v1/videos/{id} sets an etag including the signed URLs' expiry and answers 304 to a matching If-None-Match
(src/app.ts:410-424). Statuses: queued, running, finishing, ready, failed, cancelled, timed_out (src/schemas.ts:62).
Review R6: no default timeout, because a run may use the runner's full 25 minutes, retries re-queue, and with
MAX_ACTIVE_RUNS 3 a queued video can wait longer than any fixed default; a default that gave up fails healthy CI. There
is no queue-position field in the API. rest_wait (server-side wait) is not in v1.

## Approach
- videos.wait(id, { version?, timeoutMs?, intervalMs?, onProgress?, signal? }): poll GET /api/v1/videos/{id} with
  If-None-Match (304 = no change), every 3 s for the first minute then 8 s (intervalMs overrides). Which version:
  `version` if given, else the latest version at the first poll. onProgress({ version, status, stage, step }) is
  called whenever any of those four changes. The video's etag ("<job id>-<job.version>…", src/domain/videos.ts:1122 at
  e477294) changes with status, not with the agent's live step, so while the version is running or finishing each
  tick also reads GET /api/v1/videos/{id}/progress (videos.progress: stage, step, steps, credits) and compares; while
  queued only the cheap If-None-Match poll runs (status includes queued). Deviation from draft 3's "when the etag
  changes" wording, recorded for draft 4: otherwise CLI and Action progress would freeze during the whole run. Resolves with the Video DTO on ready; throws VideoAgentError code video_failed (with status and the
  version's error) on failed, cancelled, timed_out. timeoutMs throws code wait_timeout (CLI --timeout → exit 6);
  signal aborts with the signal's reason. No default timeout.
- listAll(method, input): async iterator over nextCursor, typed so it only accepts pageable operations (2.1 marker).
- videos.resolve(ref): turns what a person pastes into { id, versionN? }: a vid_… id as is; a web URL
  (<site>/videos/{id}, or /videos/{id}/edit/{n} → versionN = n; ui/src/App.tsx routes) parsed locally; a share URL (<any host>/v/{slug}) by fetching <that origin>/v/{slug}.json
  without Authorization (1.7) and reading video_agent.videoId and versionN. Anything else throws code invalid_ref. The
  CLI's <video> arguments use it (3.4a-c).

## Done when
wait handles 304s, every terminal status, progress callbacks, signal and timeout; listAll iterates pages and is a type
error on non-pageable lists; resolve handles ids, web URLs and share URLs.

## Tests
In-process integration (harness() + fetch: (req) => h.app.fetch(req)): move the fake attempt through queued → running
→ ready, and to failed and timed_out (h.drive()); assert the 304 path (a counter on the stub fetch); onProgress called
once per change with { version, status, stage, step }, including a step change while the etag stays the same (the
fake runner's latestStep moves) and no /progress request while queued; fake timers for the 3 s/8 s cadence; timeoutMs → wait_timeout;
abort via signal. listAll over a 3-page fixture; a type test (expect-type) that listAll(media.recordings) doesn't
compile. resolve: id, web URL (/videos/{id} and /videos/{id}/edit/{n}), share URL via a stub /v/{slug}.json (and its 404 → not_found),
garbage → invalid_ref; the share fetch carries no Authorization.

Standard: unit and integration with createApp(fakeDeps) (test/helpers.ts harness) and PGlite (pgStore(), every migration applied); Playwright on the mock build (VITE_MOCK=1) for UI; structured JSON logs (one event per step, with ids, durations and outcome) so failures are diagnosable from logs alone. CI (npm run typecheck, lint, vitest, npx playwright test, openapi:check, db:check) stays green. Repo rule: when checks pass, commit only your own files, push to main and confirm the Netlify production deploy is ready (other sessions often have uncommitted files in the checkout; never stage them).

title: SDK helpers: files.url and files.download (DTO-signed vs 302, no Authorization on storage fetch)

## Background
The version DTO already carries signed poster, gif, poster variants and hover clip with one expiry
(src/domain/videos.ts:955, :962-990); video, captions, narration audio and transcript are unsigned API links that 302
(:942-946) to storage URLs valid 5-10 minutes (src/app.ts:680). The edge function accepts signed URLs up to an hour

## Approach

split; fetch the storage URL immediately WITHOUT Authorization; in Node with `to`, stream to disk via dynamic node:fs
import (temp file + rename); elsewhere return the Response. Files: video, poster, gif, captions, narration, transcript,
previews.

## Done when
Both helpers work for every file kind; the key never reaches the storage host; downloads are atomic on disk.

## Tests
Unit: redirect handling asserts no Authorization header on the second fetch; DTO-signed files make zero requests; partial download leaves no file. Integration against the in-process app plus a stub storage fetch.

title: SDK helpers: media.upload (sessions, resume, wait for ready), music.importAndWait, config.get/supports
description:

Spec: docs/plans/2026-11-04-cli-and-sdk.md (draft 3, commit e477294; review logs at its end, §16). Line refs are as of e477294.
Spec key: 2.3c
Spec section(s): §4.1 media/music/config rows; §2 gotchas 12, 16

## Background
POST /api/v1/media?filename=&caption= takes up to 4 MB; bigger files use upload sessions with parts of at most 4 MB,
each with its own sha256, then complete (src/domain/media-uploads.ts:2, :22 PART_SIZE, :148-149;
skills/netlify-video/references/connect.md:67-81); an item must reach status ready (or rejected with rejectReason).
Openverse imports may answer 202 with a job to poll. Screen recordings are the big-upload case (screen plan adds
media.uploadRecording on top of this).

## Approach
- media.upload(file | path | Blob, { caption?, role?, onProgress?, signal? }): ≤4 MB → single POST; else create a
  session, slice 4 MB parts, sha256 each (WebCrypto), PUT parts with retries, resume by listing received parts after a
  failure, complete, then poll GET /api/v1/media/{id} until ready (or throw VideoAgentError code media_rejected with
  rejectReason). Uses media.check first (POST /api/v1/media/check takes { files: [{ filename, sha256 }] } and
  answers per file sameFile/sameName, src/schemas.ts MediaCheckSchema): a sameFile hit returns that item without
  uploading (opt out with { dedupe: false }).
- music.importAndWait(openverseId): follows the 202 job until done/failed.
- config.get() (the core's cached GET /api/v1/config, 2.2) and config.supports(feature) → boolean; hand-written
  helpers for newer features (e.g. other plans' redoScenes, uploadRecording) call the same requireFeatures.

## Done when
Uploads of any size succeed, resume after a forced failure, and wait for ready; music jobs complete; feature checks work.

## Tests
Unit: part slicing at exactly 4 MB, 4 MB + 1 and 9 MB, each part's sha256 and the whole-file sha256 against
media-uploads.ts's rules; resume after a dropped part (GET /api/v1/media/uploads/{id} lists received parts; only the
missing part is re-sent); a rejected item → media_rejected with rejectReason; check-first dedupe (no upload when
sameFile); onProgress byte counts monotonic; signal aborts and the session is aborted (DELETE). Integration with
harness() and the fakes' media assembly: a 9 MB fixture uploads in 3 parts and reaches ready; music.importAndWait
follows a 202 job to done and to failed; unsupported_by_server when the fake config lacks a feature. JSON log events
per part (index, bytes, ms, attempt).

title: SDK webhooks: verifyWebhook and parseWebhook (WebCrypto, raw body, delivery headers)
description:

Spec key: 2.4
Spec section(s): §4.1 top-level row; §4.2 Webhooks

## Background
Signatures are t=<unix>,v1=<hex>, hex = HMAC-SHA256 of "<t>.<raw body>" (src/lib/crypto.ts:44-46). Deliveries also
carry x-video-agent-event and x-video-agent-delivery (src/domain/webhooks.ts:189-191); receivers dedupe on eventId.

## Approach
verifyWebhook({ secret, body (raw string), signature, toleranceSec = 300 }): parse, constant-time compare via
crypto.subtle, reject timestamps outside tolerance, malformed headers. parseWebhook({ secret, body, headers }):
verify then return the typed event with eventId, event type and delivery id. Runs on Node, Deno, Bun, Workers, Netlify
Edge (WebCrypto only).

## Done when
Both functions exported and documented; work on Node 22/24.

## Tests

title: CLI catalog, router, help, --json, exit codes, logging and config file
description:
Project: video-agent, an open-source Netlify template that turns a prompt into a published MP4 via Netlify Agent Runner runs writing HyperFrames compositions; Hono+OpenAPI API, Netlify Database (Drizzle), Blobs, Identity, React+Mantine UI, MCP. Feature: CLI, SDK and player (netlify-video-agent with bin video-agent, netlify-video-agent-sdk, netlify-video-agent-player): make videos from a terminal, from code, and on your own machine with your own coding agent (local mode). Spec: docs/plans/2026-11-04-cli-and-sdk.md (draft 3, commit e477294; review logs at its end, §16). Line refs are as of e477294.
Spec key: 3.1
Spec section(s): §6.1; §6.2 Config, Exit codes, Logging

## Background
Single source of truth for commands, like src/mcp-catalog.ts for MCP tools. No framework: node:util parseArgs plus a
catalog router, bundled into one file (record's Playwright is the one exception, owned by screen-recording). Needed by
local mode (phase 4) as well as remote commands.

## Approach
- packages/cli/src/catalog.ts: per command name, summary, args, flags (types, defaults), examples, SDK methods used,
  required features string (hidden when the server doesn't list it), needsHostedApp. Router, --help, help --json from it.
- Output: --json prints exactly one JSON object on stdout; progress and prompts on stderr. Errors with --json:
  { error: { code, message, requestId? } } on stdout too.
- Exit codes, mapped by HTTP status first, then specific codes override: 0 ok; 1 error (5xx, network, unmapped); 2 usage
  or invalid request (bad flags, code invalid_ref; 400: invalid_request, unknown_look, look_not_allowed…); 3 401; 4
  403/404; 5 code video_failed; 6 code wait_timeout (wait/--wait hit --timeout); 7 409 (conflict, not_editable, remix_disabled, look_disabled, engine_disabled,
  engine_unsupported, cli_login_disabled, narration lock); 8 429; 9 unsupported_by_server. A new server code needs no
  CLI change unless it should override its status's exit code (shared rule).
- Config: one profile in v1, ~/.config/video-agent/config.json ($XDG_CONFIG_HOME honoured), mode 0600,
  { url, apiKey, keyId, webhookSecret? }. Precedence: flags > VIDEO_AGENT_URL/VIDEO_AGENT_KEY > file.
- Logging: --verbose or VIDEO_AGENT_DEBUG=1 → JSON lines on stderr (method, path, status, ms, retry, request id, steps);
  never keys.
- Words: people see scene, Look, Restyle, Redo this scene; flags --scene, --look, --engine; API stays beat/scope/look/engine.
- `<video>` args accept an id (vid_…), a web URL or a share URL. The catalog marks such args as type `video`; commands
  resolve them with the SDK's videos.resolve (2.3a), so this task only declares the type (it has no SDK dependency, so
  local mode can start early).
- Feature-gated commands (catalog `feature`): hidden from --help and help --json when the server's config lacks the
  string; when the server can't be reached, help shows them marked "(needs a server with <feature>)". Invoking one
  anyway prints "This server doesn't support <feature> yet (server <commit>)." and exits 9 (unsupported_by_server).
  Commands with needsHostedApp say so in help, and `local` commands are always listed.
- Test seam: main(argv, io) where io = { stdout, stderr, stdin, env, fetch, now, openBrowser, configDir }, so every
  command test runs in-process without touching the real home, network or browser.

## Done when
Router, help (human and --json), exit-code mapping, config read/write and logging work with stub commands; catalog test in CI.

## Tests
In-process tests calling main(argv, io): help snapshots (human and --json), --json prints exactly one parseable JSON
object on stdout (and nothing else) for success and for errors, each exit-code mapping row (a table-driven test from
status/code to exit), config precedence (flag > env > file), the file written 0600 under $XDG_CONFIG_HOME, a
feature-gated stub command hidden without the feature and exiting 9 when invoked, unknown command/flag → exit 2 with a
suggestion; a test greps every stdout/stderr byte of the suite for nva_. --verbose emits JSON lines with method, path,
status, ms, retry, requestId.
