## Background
OAuth tokens are bound to /mcp (src/auth/oauth.ts:33, :254-256, :463-465, :568), so the REST API doesn't accept them;
keys can't create keys (src/domain/keys.ts:17-20). The CLI gets an ordinary API key through the device flow (3.3a-c).

## Approach
- login [--url] [--key nva_…|-] [--no-browser] [--no-save]: device flow through the SDK's generated
  cliLogins.create/claim (no key needed; 3.3b) with label = "video-agent on <host>", host = os.hostname() capped at 64
  printable ASCII; print "Open <verificationUrl> and enter ABCD-EFGH"; open the
  browser unless --no-browser; poll the token endpoint every intervalSec, honouring slow_down; save url, apiKey, keyId,
  webhookSecret to the 0600 file). --key reads a key (stdin with -), checks it with me.get before saving, and never echoes it; --no-save
  keeps it out of the file (CI). Ctrl-C while polling stops cleanly (exit 1, nothing saved). The login expiring prints
  "The code expired. Run video-agent login again." (exit 3); denied → "The login was denied in the browser." (exit 3).
  Before starting, config.supports('cli_login'); false (switched off, or a server older than 3.3), or a 409
  cli_login_disabled → message "CLI sign-in isn't available on this server. Create a key on <site>/keys and run
  video-agent login --key -" (exit 7).
- logout [--revoke]: forget the key, and with --revoke call keys.revoke on it first.
- whoami: me.get + server version and features.
- doctor (remote part): Node ≥22, config present, server reachable, version + features listed. (4.7 adds local checks;
  whichever lands first creates the command.)

## Done when
Login works headless and with a browser; logout revokes; whoami and doctor report correctly.

session path (h.call with h.member's cookie and same origin) → claim saves url/apiKey/keyId/webhookSecret 0600;
slow_down honoured with fake timers (interval grows by 5 s); denied and expired paths and their exit codes;
--no-browser prints URL and code only; --key - from stdin; --key with a revoked key → exit 3 and nothing saved;
--no-save writes nothing; cli_login_disabled → the API-keys-page message, exit 7; logout --revoke revokes the key
(next call 401); whoami prints email, role, server version and features; doctor's remote checks with a stubbed
unreachable server. No nva_ in any output.

title: Device login domain: cli_logins table, create/approve/claim with createKeyForUser and owner checks, limits, switch
description:
Project: video-agent, an open-source Netlify template that turns a prompt into a published MP4 via Netlify Agent Runner runs writing HyperFrames compositions; Hono+OpenAPI API, Netlify Database (Drizzle), Blobs, Identity, React+Mantine UI, MCP. Feature: CLI, SDK and player (netlify-video-agent with bin video-agent, netlify-video-agent-sdk, netlify-video-agent-player): make videos from a terminal, from code, and on your own machine with your own coding agent (local mode). Spec: docs/plans/2026-11-04-cli-and-sdk.md (draft 3, commit e477294; review logs at its end, §16). Line refs are as of e477294.
Spec key: 3.3a
Spec section(s): §5.2 (all bullets)

## Background
A device-style flow (RFC 8628 model) that ends in an ordinary API key: no OAuth config needed, works with Identity and
Sign in with Netlify, and the key appears (and can be revoked) on the API keys page. Facts: createKey refuses non-session
principals (src/domain/keys.ts:17-20) and returns key AND webhookSecret once (:35); using a key re-checks the owner
(disabled, domain no longer allowed: src/domain/auth.ts:100-108; Identity user gone/unconfirmed: :134-139); keys are
compared with safeEqual on sha256 (auth.ts:129). Reviews: mint at claim (no key at rest), owner checks at claim, return
webhookSecret, typed code (RFC 8628 §5.4), caps against lockout. Nothing in the app limits by IP yet (new work).
Migration order (roadmap): after redo-a-scene's phase-2 migration, before screen-recording's.

## Approach
- Migration (one PR, OpenAPI regenerated): cli_logins (id, device_code_hash, user_code: 8 characters from the
  consonant alphabet BCDFGHJKLMNPQRSTVWXZ (RFC 8628 §6.1), stored without the dash, shown ABCD-EFGH; label ≤64
  printable ASCII; host ≤64; client_ip; status pending|approved|denied|claimed|expired; user_id; api_key_id;
  failed_attempts (wrong device codes on this login; 5 → expired); created_at; expires_at = +10 min) and
  cli_login_failures (user_id, created_at) for wrong typed codes; settings.cliLoginEnabled (default true) in the admin
  settings schemas next to remixEnabled (src/schemas.ts AdminSettingsSchema and UpdateAdminSettingsSchema). Drizzle schema + db:generate; memory store +
  PGlite store.
- src/domain/cli-login.ts:
  createLogin({ label, host, clientIp }) → { loginId, deviceCode (32 random bytes, base64url; only its sha256 stored),
  userCode, verificationUrl = <siteUrl>/cli/approve (no code in it), expiresAt, intervalSec: 5 }.
  lookupLogin(user principal, userCode) → { loginId, label, host, clientIp, createdAt, expiresAt, role (the approver's)
  } for a pending, unexpired login; a wrong code records a failure and answers 404 not_found; 5 failures in 15 minutes
  → 429 rate_limited "Too many wrong codes. Try again in 15 minutes." (applies to lookup and decide).
  decideLogin(user principal, userCode, 'approve' | 'deny'): approve records user_id and status approved (≤10 approvals
  per person per hour → 429), deny sets denied.
  claimLogin(loginId, deviceCode): safeEqual on sha256 (a wrong code counts failed_attempts and answers 404);
  answers { status: 'pending' } | { status: 'slow_down' } (polled faster than intervalSec; the client adds 5 s) |
  { status: 'denied' } | { status: 'expired' } (also for a second claim: the code works once) | on approved: re-run
  the key-owner checks with the same helpers principalFromRequest uses for a key's owner (disabled; domain no longer
  allowed, auth.ts:100-108; Identity user gone or unconfirmed, :134-139) → { status: 'denied' } if any fail; else
  mint via createKeyForUser(deps, userId, "CLI · <host> · <yyyy-mm-dd>") (the part of createKey after the session
  check, keys.ts:21-35; createKey calls it) and return { status: 'claimed', apiKey, keyId, webhookSecret, user:
  { id, email, role } } once; status claimed, api_key_id set.
- Limits on createLogin: ≤10 pending per client IP (x-nf-client-connection-ip; count pending rows) and ≤500 pending
  overall → 429 rate_limited with distinct messages.
- Admin switch off → every function throws 409 cli_login_disabled. Feature string cli_login emitted in
  /api/v1/config features when on (1.2 registry).
- Sweep (the existing scheduled sweep): mark pending rows past expires_at expired; delete rows an hour after expiry and
  failures older than a day.
- Logs: cli_login.created (loginId, clientIp), .lookup_failed (userId), .approved/.denied (loginId, userId),
  .claimed (loginId, keyId), .claim_refused (loginId, reason). Never the codes or the key.

## Done when
Domain functions and migration done; all limits and checks enforced; no key ever stored.

## Tests
Integration on memory and PGlite (pgStore(), every migration applied), with deps.clock: happy path create → lookup →
approve → claim (key works on GET /api/v1/me; webhookSecret returned; name "CLI · host · date"); deny → denied; wrong
typed code ×5 → locked for 15 minutes (and unlocked after); 11th approval in an hour → 429; 11th pending login from one
IP → 429 while another IP still works; global cap; slow_down when polled early; expiry at 10 minutes; second claim →
expired; wrong device code ×5 → login expired; approve-then-disable → denied; approve-then-domain-removed → denied;
Identity user deleted → denied; switch off → cli_login_disabled everywhere; sweep marks and deletes; no row ever holds
a key or a raw code (scan the stored rows). JSON step logs asserted for each event.

Standard: unit and integration with createApp(fakeDeps) (test/helpers.ts harness) and PGlite (pgStore(), every migration applied); Playwright on the mock build (VITE_MOCK=1) for UI; structured JSON logs (one event per step, with ids, durations and outcome) so failures are diagnosable from logs alone. CI (npm run typecheck, lint, vitest, npx playwright test, openapi:check, db:check) stays green. Repo rule: when checks pass, commit only your own files, push to main and confirm the Netlify production deploy is ready (other sessions often have uncommitted files in the checkout; never stage them).

Spec key: 3.3b
Spec section(s): §5.2 Routes and middleware

## Background
Only /api/v1/config (and OPTIONS) skips the auth middleware (src/app.ts:238); cookie-session writes go through
assertSameOrigin (src/domain/auth.ts:165).

## Approach
Four routes (tag cli; OpenAPI regenerated; each with operationId and x-sdk):
- POST /api/v1/cli/logins { label, host } → 201 createLogin's result. Unauthenticated. operationId createCliLogin,
  x-sdk { resource: 'cliLogins', method: 'create' } (no `feature` key: the CLI checks
  config.supports('cli_login') itself so "switched off" and "old server" both get the --key hint).
- POST /api/v1/cli/logins/{id}/token { deviceCode } → 200 claimLogin's result. Unauthenticated. claimCliLogin,
  { cliLogins, claim }.
- POST /api/v1/cli/logins/lookup { userCode } → 200 { loginId, label, host, clientIp, createdAt, expiresAt, role }.
  Web session only (a `user` principal: API keys and OAuth tokens get 403), assertSameOrigin. lookupCliLogin,
  x-sdk false. A POST so the typed code never lands in a URL or access log.
- POST /api/v1/cli/logins/approve { userCode, decision: 'approve' | 'deny' } → 200 { status }. Web session only,
  assertSameOrigin. decideCliLogin, x-sdk false.
Add exactly the two unauthenticated paths (/api/v1/cli/logins and /api/v1/cli/logins/{id}/token, POST only) to the
requireAuth exemption beside /api/v1/config (src/app.ts:238 at e477294). Read the client IP from
x-nf-client-connection-ip (fall back to 'unknown', which shares one bucket). Zod schemas with the caps (label/host
≤64 printable ASCII, userCode 8-9 chars with optional dash, deviceCode ≤64). Errors documented per route
(404 not_found, 409 cli_login_disabled, 429 rate_limited).

## Done when
Routes live behind the switch; exemptions minimal; spec regenerated with operationIds.

## Tests
Integration via harness(): unauthenticated access only to the two POST routes (GET on them and every other new path
→ 401); lookup and approve refuse an API key (403) and a cross-origin cookie request; schema caps (65-char label,
non-ASCII host, bad code shapes → 400); the exemption list unchanged otherwise (a test that /api/v1/cli/logins/lookup
without a session is 401); openapi:check; the coverage test sees the four operationIds.

title: CLI create, revise, remix (prompt files, media upload first, --plan/--answers, idempotency, --wait, --out)
description:
Project: video-agent, an open-source Netlify template that turns a prompt into a published MP4 via Netlify Agent Runner runs writing HyperFrames compositions; Hono+OpenAPI API, Netlify Database (Drizzle), Blobs, Identity, React+Mantine UI, MCP. Feature: CLI, SDK and player (netlify-video-agent with bin video-agent, netlify-video-agent-sdk, netlify-video-agent-player): make videos from a terminal, from code, and on your own machine with your own coding agent (local mode). Spec: docs/plans/2026-11-04-cli-and-sdk.md (draft 3, commit e477294; review logs at its end, §16). Line refs are as of e477294.
Spec key: 3.4a
Spec section(s): §6.2 create/revise/remix rows

## Background
The core making commands. Other plans add flags in their own beads: --look (looks), --engine (render-engines),
--recording (screen-recording), --scene (regenerate-beat), and create --context-file /
--external-ref (github-action phase 3, gated on the context and external_ref features; that plan's bead registers them
in this catalog). Interactive terminal planning is Not in v1.

## Approach
Flags map to the API's own fields (src/schemas.ts CreateVideoSchema, ReviseSchema, RemixSchema):
- create "<prompt>" | --prompt-file <f|-> → prompt; --aspect 16:9|9:16|1:1|4:5 → aspect; --duration <sec> → durationSec;
  --sound silent|music|music_sfx → sound; --voice <voice id> → voiceover { enabled: true, voice }, --voice off →
  { enabled: false }; --media <id|path> (repeatable, ≤12) → mediaIds, where a path uploads first with media.upload
  (dedupe on) and a ./file:"caption" suffix sets the caption; --title → title; --webhook-url → webhookUrl;
  --idempotency-key → opts.idempotencyKey (else the SDK's UUID); --wait follows with videos.wait and the progress
  line; --out <dir> (implies --wait) downloads video, poster and captions with files.download.
- Planning (feature planning; hidden without it): --plan → plans.create({ prompt, aspect, durationSec, mediaIds, sound,
  voiceover }) then plans.questions(planId); prints the plan id and questions (with --json as data: { planId,
  questions: [{ id, text, choices }] }) and exits 0. --plan-id <id> --answers <file|-> → plans.brief(planId,
  { answers }) then videos.create({ planId, … }); --answers takes the PlanAnswers shape. (Interactive terminal Q&A is
  Not in v1.)
- revise <video> "<change>" [--from-version n] [--comments <id,…>] → commentIds [--media …] [--duration] [--sound]
  [--voice] [--idempotency-key] [--wait] [--out]: videos.resolve the arg, then videos.revise.
- remix <video> "<change>" [--from-version] [--aspect] [--duration] [--language] [--sound] [--voice] [--media …]
  [--idempotency-key] [--wait] [--out]: videos.remix (remix_disabled → exit 7).
- --json output: the Video DTO (and with --wait the final DTO; with --out also { files: [paths] }).

## Done when
Commands work against the in-process app with every flag; idempotency keys passed; --wait/--out paths covered.

## Tests
In-process CLI tests (main(argv, io) with the SDK pointed at harness()'s app): each flag reaches the request body with
the API's field name (assert on the stored job), prompt from stdin, a --media path uploaded first (and deduped on a
second run), media ./x.png:"caption", plan print and plan answer → create with planId, --plan without planning → exit 9,

## Background
repoRoot comes from the script location (scripts/lib/run-tools.ts:11, `export const repoRoot = resolve(...)`). render-job always uploads with netlify blobs:set
(scripts/render-job.ts:358-381), then POSTs the manifest to --callback (:419-434), and derives the checkpoint URL as
/done → /checkpoint (:196); it writes .render/<attempt>/manifest.json first (:416). checkpoint.ts is best effort
(scripts/checkpoint.ts:1-5, bundle cap 2 MB :12). PromptInput.upload is { mode: 'blobs' } | { mode: 'signed'; url }
(src/domain/prompt.ts:22), and PromptInput has its own checkpointUrl (:20) used in the checkpoint.ts line (:246).
Three builders write the --upload arg the same way: buildPrompt (:112), buildRenderUnchangedPrompt (:388) and
buildFitPrompt (:554); the service always passes blobs
(reconciler.ts:225, :252, :343). The template version is recorded on the attempt (reconciler.ts:457), not in the prompt
text. A host loopback server is unreachable from the sandboxes (review R1), so files carry results back.

## Approach
1. run-tools.ts:12 → repoRoot = process.env.VA_REPO_ROOT ?? <today's value>.
2. render-job: --upload local skips Blobs uploads and uploadReferences. A --callback file://<ws>/.render/<attempt>/done
   writes done.json (the manifest) at that path instead of POSTing (410 branch n/a). postCheckpoint with a file: URL
   writes <seq>.json (message, renderPercent, optional bundle ≤2 MB) into the derived checkpoint folder. https: callbacks
   unchanged.
3. PromptInput.upload (and the two other builders' input types) gains { mode: 'local' }; one shared uploadArg(upload)
   helper in prompt.ts writes --upload blobs | --upload local | --upload <url> for all three builders.
4. Prompt tests, for each of the three builders: for the same input, blobs and local prompts differ only in the
   --upload argument (and the callback/checkpoint URLs the caller passes); a fixture blobs input produces exactly
   today's text (feature-off byte-identical rule; snapshot taken before the change).
5. Bump PROMPT_TEMPLATE_VERSION by 1 in merge order (shared rule 3). test/remix-run.test.ts:176 asserts the literal
   `toBe(16)`; replace that assertion (the rule forbids literal template numbers in tests) unless another plan's bump
   already did.

## Done when
Runner path byte-identical; local modes work; tests pass.

## Tests
Unit (scripts/render-job and checkpoint tests, temp dirs): a file: callback writes done.json atomically (temp + rename)
with the same JSON the https path would POST; postCheckpoint with a file: URL writes 1.json, 2.json… using the existing
.render/checkpoint-seq-<attempt> counter, with the bundle when asked and without it over 2 MB; a file: URL outside
<repoRoot>/.render/ is refused; --upload local makes no netlify call (netlifyCli stubbed to throw); VA_REPO_ROOT moves
every path (video/, .render/, context/); the three builders' prompt diff tests; existing render-job and prompt tests

## Background

## Approach

shape). Everything after the fetch (manifest verification, hashes, restore, media, feedback stills, and the other
plans' steps in render-engines' order) is unchanged. The local layout is <dir>/<store>/<key>, the same store names and
keys the server's run manifest uses (src/lib/run-manifest.ts), so 4.3b writes inputs with the server's own key
builders.

Revisions, media and feedback stills prepare from a folder exactly as from Blobs.

manifest with a parent source.tar.gz, two media items and a feedback still prepares identically in both modes (hash of
every file under video/ compared; the blobs mode with netlify blobs:get stubbed to copy from the same folder). JSON
log per fetched key (store, key, bytes, ms, mode).

## Background
The OS sandbox is the boundary, not a tool allowlist. Killing a process group isn't enough (spike S11: npm exec and a
worker survived a group SIGTERM); scripts/lib/proc-tree.ts runs detached, samples the tree, SIGTERMs then SIGKILLs every
pid seen (proc-tree.ts:1-6).

## Approach
Adapter interface { name, detect(), signedIn(), command(ws, prompt, opts), parseEvents(stream), sandboxCheck() }.
Shared:
- Child env allowlist: PATH (runtime first), HOME, USER, LANG, TERM, TMPDIR, VA_*, RENDER_QUALITY, empty
  npm_config_userconfig, the agent's own auth vars when set. Never VIDEO_AGENT_*, NETLIFY_*, cloud credentials, any
  other secret (no --pass-env in v1).
- Deny-read list and network allowlist constants (from C2), rendered into each agent's settings.
- 30-minute default timeout (--timeout); Ctrl-C and timeout stop the tree with proc-tree.ts, never by name or group alone.
- --no-sandbox escape hatch: warns once, still scrubs env.
- Logs: agent events to agent.log, a one-line terminal status, run.jsonl steps. /docs/cli warns that agent.log, run.jsonl
  and prompt.txt hold the full prompt (brand text, captions).
- No telemetry: nothing is sent to us.

## Done when
Framework in place with a test adapter; env and stop behaviour proven.

title: Remix a video: a new video from another video's composition plus a change request
description:
Project: video-agent, an open-source Netlify template that turns a prompt into a published MP4 via Netlify Agent Runner runs writing HyperFrames compositions; Hono+OpenAPI API, Netlify Database (Drizzle), Blobs, Identity, React+Mantine UI, MCP. Feature: remix a video (a new video that starts from another video's finished composition plus a change request). Spec: docs/plans/2026-11-03-remix.md (draft 3, commit 73bea33; §0 = owner decisions from the 2026-11-03 interview, §10 = review log of the Fable 5.1 + Codex gpt-6.1-sol reviews). Line refs are as of 73bea33.
Spec key: RM
Spec section(s): all (§0-§9)

## Background
Owner ask (2026-11-03): from a video, press Remix, say what should change, and get a NEW video that starts from the
original's finished composition, prompts and settings rather than from scratch: a clone plus a revision. People will use
it every way, from "exactly this, swap the brand names" to "a video like this about a totally different topic".

What already exists (spec §1): every finished version keeps its whole composition as sources/{jobId}/v{n}.tar.gz
(index.html, summary.json, agent-made assets, AI voice clips, music credits; <=10 MiB tar limit; hash in
outputs.sha256, finalize.ts:217), library media as version_media snapshots (key + hash), and its settings on the
versions row. Revisions already restore a parent archive into video/ and ask the agent to change it
(reviseVideo videos.ts:369-464, reconciler.ts:252-277, prepare-run.ts:376-395). A remix is that run with three
differences: the parent is in another video, the result is a new video owned by the remixer, and some state is dropped
(recorded narration, edit state, captions).

Owner decisions (§0): no fidelity toggle (the agent infers how much to change); entry points on the video page, a Library
tile menu, the public share page (signed-in Creators only) and New video ("Start from an existing video" search picker);
optional Plan first like revisions; immediate-source lineage only; apply today's brand; source media as removable
chips; source length prefilled; language inherited (transcription only); no owner opt-out; admin kill switch
remixEnabled (on by default); empty "What would you change?" box; source comments not carried; "Remix" in the Library
meta line, no filter; no owner notification; aspect change allowed with a warning; recorded narration dropped
deterministically; no remix counts on the original.

## Approach
Phases: 1 data + run path; 2 remixVideo domain (copy, clean, adopt, create) + plans; 3 API, MCP, config, OpenAPI, mock;
4 UI (dialog, four entry points, admin toggle); 5 production e2e + docs. Each phase ends with a gate bead; gates chain.

Architecture (spec §3): at creation, copy the source archive to sources/{newJobId}/remix-source.tar.gz under a narrow
reservation cleanup row (+1 h) that the creating transaction adopts (marks done); clean recorded narration out of the
copy with applyNarration(…, null); snapshot everything a run needs in versions.remix so retries never read the
original. Runs reuse the existing `revision` kind: the reconciler builds manifest.source from versions.remix
(parentN null, no references). Provenance on jobs.remix_of_job_id/_n (immediate source).

## Done when
Every phase epic closed; the phase 5 live gate passed on production; CI green; the spec gets a short as-built note
(deviations, credits spent).

## Tests
Each phase has a gate bead; unit/integration/UI tests are listed per bead.

Standard: unit and integration with createApp(fakeDeps) (test/helpers.ts harness) and PGlite (pgStore(), every migration applied); Playwright on the mock build (VITE_MOCK=1) for UI; structured JSON logs (one event per step, with ids, durations and outcome) so failures are diagnosable from logs alone. CI (npm run typecheck, lint, vitest, npx playwright test, openapi:check, db:check) stays green. Repo rule: when checks pass, commit only your own files, push to main and confirm the Netlify production deploy is ready (other sessions often have uncommitted files in the checkout; never stage them).

## Considerations
Not in v1 (spec §8): remix counts/reverse links on the original, a Remixes filter, stored lineage chains, owner
notifications, owner opt-out, keeping recorded narration, translation semantics for the language field, picking source
comments, multi-source remixes, streaming blob copies. A separate follow-up (dismissible comments in Incorporate
feedback, spec §9) is NOT part of this epic. Production e2e spends credits (budget ~600 for phase 5).

## Background

snapshot on its v1 so a run or a Try again never re-reads the original (Codex review: retries must not touch the
source, which may be deleted, videos.ts:640-649); plans that can target a remix (plans are otherwise either jobless or
the job's own, videos.ts:112-115, plans.ts:281-307); and an admin kill switch (§0).

## Approach
db/schema.ts:
- jobs: remix_of_job_id text NULL, remix_of_n integer NULL.
- versions: remix jsonb NULL. Shape (export a `VersionRemix` type from src/domain/types.ts):
  { sourceKey: string; sourceSha256: string; fromJobId: string; fromN: number; fromTitle: string;
    fromOwnerName: string | null; history: string[] (oldest first, <=8 entries, <=4000 chars total);
    fromSummary: string (<=1000 chars); narrationDropped: boolean; sourceSound: 'silent'|'music'|'music_sfx' }
  (sourceSound lets needsMusicPick decide without reading the original, bead 1.3.)
- plans: remix_from_job_id text NULL, remix_from_n integer NULL.
- settings: remix_enabled boolean NOT NULL DEFAULT true.
Generate with `npx drizzle-kit generate --name remix`; never hand-edit snapshot.json.
Map the new columns in src/store/drizzle.ts and src/store/memory.ts (insert/get/update paths for jobs, versions,
plans, settings) and in the row types (JobRow, VersionRow, PlanRow, settings row in src/domain/types.ts).

## Background
Every run-side check assumes one job: verifyRunManifest requires source keys under `${jobId}/` (run-manifest.ts:308-310),
prepare-run rejects another job's manifest (prepare-run.ts:478), and the reconciler finds the parent by version.parentN
in the same job (reconciler.ts:252-255). Because bead 2.2 copies the source into the NEW job's prefix, those checks can
stay as they are; only the reconciler needs to know where a remix's source is. Both reviews agreed a new run kind buys
nothing: prepare-run and render-job are already driven by manifest.source.

## Approach
- src/domain/reconciler.ts: in startRequest, before the `if (version.parentN !== null)` branch (:252), add: when
  version.remix is set, build the revision input from it: { parentN: null, sourceKey: remix.sourceKey,
  sourceSha256: remix.sourceSha256, references: [], narrationSamples: null }. Never call getOutput for it. Missing
  copy blob at start -> the existing SourceUnavailable path (:431-443) with "The remix's copied source is missing.".
- Widen the reconciler's local `revision` type (:152) and the manifest type (run-manifest.ts RunManifest.source.parentN,
  :30-40) to `number | null`.
- Manifest: kind stays 'revision'. OMIT `references` when empty: an empty array is rejected (run-manifest.ts:314-322).
- parentSourceSha256 on the attempt (reconciler.ts:356, :450) = the copy's sha256.
- Pass a `remix` input to buildPrompt (bead 1.4 consumes it).

## Done when
A version with versions.remix set produces a valid 'revision' manifest pointing at {jobId}/remix-source.tar.gz with parentN null and no references; versions without remix behave exactly as before.

- verifyRunManifest accepts parentN null + no references; still rejects keys outside the job prefix and `references: []`.
- Reconciler unit/integration: remix version -> manifest.source.key/sha from versions.remix, attempt.parentSourceSha256 set.
- Retry: a second attempt for the same remix version builds an identical manifest (except attempt ids).
- Missing copy -> attempt fails with category source_unavailable and a clear message.
- Regression: an ordinary revision's manifest is byte-identical to before (snapshot or deep-equal).

title: Remix source copy: reservation cleanup row, verified copy, adoption in the creating transaction
description:
Project: video-agent, an open-source Netlify template that turns a prompt into a published MP4 via Netlify Agent Runner runs writing HyperFrames compositions; Hono+OpenAPI API, Netlify Database (Drizzle), Blobs, Identity, React+Mantine UI, MCP. Feature: remix a video (a new video that starts from another video's finished composition plus a change request). Spec: docs/plans/2026-11-03-remix.md (draft 3, commit 73bea33; §0 = owner decisions from the 2026-11-03 interview, §10 = review log of the Fable 5.1 + Codex gpt-6.1-sol reviews). Line refs are as of 73bea33.
Spec key: 2.2
Spec section(s): §2 gotchas 2 and 7, §3.1 steps 2-6

## Background
The remix must own a copy of its source so it survives the original's deletion (deleteVideo queues delete_prefix for
{jobId}/ in videos, sources, bundles, videos.ts:640-649) and so run checks stay per-job. Two traps (verified): the
sweep deletes ANY due row's prefix with no existence check (cleanup.ts:29-32), and insertCleanup is onConflictDoNothing
on unique (store, prefix) (drizzle.ts:1192), so a row for {newJobId}/ would either delete a successful remix or later
swallow deleteVideo's own row and leak the remix's files. BlobsPort has only buffered get/set (deps.ts:142-152).

## Approach
src/domain/remix-copy.ts (used by remixVideo, bead 2.3):
1. reserve(repo, newJobId): insertCleanup({ kind: 'delete_prefix', store: 'sources', prefix: `${newJobId}/remix-source`,
   nextActionAt: now + 1 h }) -> returns the row id. The narrow prefix never collides with deleteVideo's `${newJobId}/`.
2. copy(deps, source output, cleaned bytes): blobs.set('sources', `${newJobId}/remix-source.tar.gz`, bytes); read back
   and verify sha256 (strong consistency store).
3. adopt(repo, reservationId) inside the creating transaction: updateCleanup(id, { doneAt: now }). listDueCleanup only
   takes doneAt null rows (drizzle.ts:1198), so an adopted copy is never swept.
Failure anywhere after reserve (exception, tx rollback, lost idempotency race, crash) leaves the row open; the sweep
deletes the orphan copy within the hour.

## Done when
The three helpers exist, are used by remixVideo, and the lifecycle is covered by tests (most in 2.5).

## Tests
- Unit: reserve row shape; copy verifies hash (a fake blobs store that corrupts on read fails the copy); adopt sets doneAt.
- deleteVideo on an adopted remix still inserts and runs its own {jobId}/ cleanup (no conflict with the reservation row)
  and the copy is gone afterwards.

durationSec?, sound?, voiceover?, mediaIds?, planId?, webhookUrl? }, idempotencyKey?)
Order (each step matters):

   (409 not_ready otherwise). Visibility BEFORE the idempotency lookup, like reviseVideo (videos.ts:391-392), so a key

   ApiError invalid_request "This version is too large or damaged to remix."); copy (2.2).

   still equal to deriveTitle(v1.prompt), finalize.ts:483), aspect (input ?? source), language (input ?? source),
   private: source.private, remixOfJobId, remixOfN, owner = principal }; access mirror for private videos like
   updateVideo (videos.ts:605-613, files.ts:88); v1 { prompt, authorId/apiKeyId = principal, mode 'author', parentN null,

   versions' prompts up to fromN, oldest first, PREFIXED with the source v1's own remix.history when the source is itself
   a remix, then capped to the newest 8 entries / 4000 chars; fromSummary = output.agentSummary capped

## Background
The UI shows "Remix of Title v3" and the Library meta line shows "Remix". buildVideoDto (videos.ts ~964-1050) builds the

title: Screen recording demos: turn a raw screen recording into a polished, editable product demo
description:
Project: video-agent, an open-source Netlify template that turns a prompt into a published MP4 via Netlify Agent Runner runs writing HyperFrames compositions; Hono+OpenAPI API, Netlify Database (Drizzle), Blobs, Identity, React+Mantine UI, MCP. Feature: screen recording -> polished demo (a raw screen recording becomes a finished, editable product demo: auto zoom that follows the action, a smooth cursor and click ripples where there's a pointer trace, dead time cut or sped up, a callout per step, hidden areas over private things, an intro and outro in the brand or a Look, captions and optional voice-over). Spec: docs/plans/2026-11-04-screen-recording-demo.md (draft 3, commit e477294; review logs at its end: §16 draft 1->2 and draft 2->3). Line refs are as of e477294.
Spec key: SR
Spec section(s): all (§0-§16)

## Background
Owner ask (2026-11-04, idea #11): "screen recording -> polished demo: I love it, how would it work?"
A person hands Video Agent a raw screen recording and gets back a finished product demo: the camera zooms in on what
they click and follows the action, the cursor is smooth and visible, clicks ripple, dead time is cut or sped up, each
step gets a short label, and the whole thing opens and closes in the brand (or a Look), with captions and optional
voice-over. It must stay editable in the browser editor like every other video.

How it works (spec §0). Two halves.
1) Getting the recording in, three paths shipped in order C, B, A:
   C. Upload a file (QuickTime, Loom, OBS): pixels only, converted in the browser with Mediabunny (WebCodecs).
   B. Record in the app (getDisplayMedia): pixels only, encoded LIVE with Mediabunny MediaStreamVideoTrackSource.
   A. `video-agent record <url>` in the CLI (Playwright Chromium): pixels plus a POINTER TRACE (every move, click,
      scroll, key count, and the role and accessible name of what was clicked).
   Every file arrives as H.264 MP4, a keyframe a second, fast start, constant size and frame rate; the server never
   transcodes. It becomes a library `video` item with role `screen-recording` (+ trace.json when there is one).
2) Turning it into a video: ONE ordinary `author` run on the runner (never in a Function): prepare-run hydrates the
   recording; scripts/recording.ts analyze finds idle spans (ffmpeg freezedetect), page changes (scdet), activity
   (frame differencing), the cursor (trace or a small moving blob) and speech (hyperframes transcribe); plan makes steps,
   in/out/speed, auto-zoom camera keys, cursor path, ripples, keyframed redaction boxes, plus contact sheets and one
   focus crop per step for the agent; the agent names steps from the focus crops and writes callouts and voice lines;
   emit prints each recording scene's markup; check verifies; voice.ts and render-job run as today.

Why it can look good: it copies how Screen Studio/Screenize/Reframed work (recording + cursor log -> zoom keyframes from
click clusters and dwell). Path A has the exact log plus clicked-element names; paths B/C infer from pixels.
Why it stays editable: a recording scene is the ORIGINAL library file plus data (data-va-in/out, camera keys, clicks,
redact entries, a cursor-path script file), turned into seek-safe GSAP tweens by a new vendor/va-recording.js. The
editor changes the data and re-renders without the agent (~34 credits). Nothing is re-encoded; no derived clips.

Reviews that shaped it (spec §16): draft 1 independent Fable 5.1 review + cross-plan seam review; draft 2 remote
Fable 5.1 high review in a Netlify Agent Run at 19740d8. Key fixes they forced: tweens in AUTHORED beat time (vaBeat
already time-scales), role-aware probeClip, 150 MB cap (assembly holds ~3 copies in a 1024 MB background function),
contact sheets in context/ (runs can't read .va-run/), cursor path out of index.html, a role table instead of
isTakeRole branches, stss/stts parsing, a no-agent compose path, keyframed redaction boxes, server-side name scrubbing,
focus crops so the agent can read UI text, holds for long voice lines, live encoding for path B, an analysis cache, a
run time budget.

## Approach
Phases (spec §10), each ending in a gate; gates chain:
- Phase 0: spikes D1-D6 (D1, D3 use one runner run each; the rest are local; D6 needs compose from phase 2).
- Phase 1: recordings in the library (role table, limits, stss/stts, assembly memory, visibility, retention, pointer
  trace schema and routes, bundles by key, OpenAPI/SDK).
- Phase 2: the run (recording.ts analyze/plan/emit/compose/check, va-recording.js, contract additions, manifest,
  prepare-run, prompt, AGENTS.md, finalize guards, create/remix API, Quick demo API). Local gate, then live test LT-1.
- Phase 3: the web app (upload + setup, video page Hidden list, editor panels, look picker filter, record in the app).
  Playwright gate, then live test LT-2.
- Phase 4: the CLI recorder (record, trace, media upload --role, demo, local demo, docs). Local gate, then LT-3.
- Phase 5: polish and extras from spec §13, created DEFERRED so no designed feature is lost.

Owner decisions (decided 2026-11-04, roadmap): packages netlify-video-agent (CLI, bin video-agent; run with
`npx -y netlify-video-agent@1 …`) and netlify-video-agent-sdk; local mode ships ("make one locally, then deploy it
for your team"); every live test runs --dry first and asks the owner before each run, with a credit ceiling; no default
look until the Looks plan's spike K2 (so demos default to the wallpaper frame).

Open owner questions (spec §14), built on their recommended defaults:
1. Path order C (upload), then B (record in app), then A (CLI)? Building: yes; docs lead with the CLI once it exists.
2. Limits 5 min / 150 MB per recording, 2 GiB stored per person? Building: yes, revisited after D5.
3. Recordings private to the uploader until a video uses them? Building: yes.
4. Solid hiding boxes (not blur)? Building: yes; blurred copy later.
5. Hiding is cosmetic (viewers of the video can watch the full recording). Building: the setup note + demos with
   anything hidden START PRIVATE (note shown again on Make public and Publish); burn-in deferred to phase 5.
6. Recording audio dropped from the video but transcribed on device to help name steps? Building: yes to both.
7. Padded wallpaper frame by default? Building: yes.
8. A separate "From a screen recording" card on New video? Building: yes.
9. Agent-hidden areas: a "Looks right" button in the Hidden list + one line in the existing Publish dialog? Building:
   yes.
10. Default length min(90, max(20, 40% of recording)) set by the server, agent prefers the planner's estimate when it
    differs >30%? Building: yes.
11. Quick demo with no agent (compose only, ~34 credits + analysis)? Building: API only in v1
    (POST /videos {recording, agent:false}); UI only after D6.
12. Scripted tours when? Building: after the CLI recorder (phase 5); trace schema reserves source.kind "script".
None of these blocks work, so there are no decision beads.

Cross-plan dependencies (the orchestrator adds the edges; each affected bead names them):
- Phase 1 needs CLI phase 1 (operationIds, features registry, packages/); its migration comes after CLI 3.3's in the
  roadmap order; 1.5c (SDK methods) needs CLI phase 2.
- Phase 2 needs render-engines phase 1 (Engine interface, src/lib/contract-core.ts, prepare-run step order,
  EngineCapabilities). The prompt bump lands after redo-a-scene phase 2 and before Action phase 3 (roadmap rule 3).
- Phase 3 needs Looks phase 1 (look.json schema with the `recording` block, the `clean` look); 3.4 needs Looks phase 3.
- Phase 4 needs CLI phase 3 (remote CLI); 4.2b local demo needs CLI phase 4; 4.3 docs needs CLI phase 6 (docs nav).
- Redo-a-scene's derived-file list must include assets/recording/<step>.cursor.js and <step>.hold.jpg (it lists only
  plan.json today); the GitHub Action's "refresh on release" builds on remix {recording} (2.6) and scripted tours.

## Done when
Every phase epic 0-4 closed; LT-1, LT-2 and LT-3 passed on production with the owner's go-ahead; CI green; the
spec gets a short as-built note (deviations, credits spent, D1-D6 results). Phase 5 beads stay deferred until picked.

## Tests
Each phase has a gate bead; unit, integration, run-script, Playwright and live tests are listed per bead.
Budget for the whole build: about 1,000 credits (D1 ~150, D3 ~150, LT-1 <=500, LT-2 ~34, LT-3 ~210).

## Considerations
Not in v1 (spec §13, created as deferred phase 5 beads): scripted tours; refresh on release (Action
plan); burn-in of hidden areas; OpenCV cursor detection; IndexedDB recovery for path B; the full Look recording block
(cursor shape/scale/colour, ripple and callout styles, browser frame with address bar, device frame); replaceable traces
after use (version_media trace columns); follow-cam and polished vertical cut; callouts that follow the camera; small
extras (click SFX, 60 fps, surfaceSwitching, Hidden thumbnails, ripples toggle, steps count on the DTO,

title: D1: HyperFrames renders data-media-start + data-playback-rate frame-accurately in a later scene; media-start basis; native hold; render speed
description:
Project: video-agent, an open-source Netlify template that turns a prompt into a published MP4 via Netlify Agent Runner runs writing HyperFrames compositions; Hono+OpenAPI API, Netlify Database (Drizzle), Blobs, Identity, React+Mantine UI, MCP. Feature: screen recording -> polished demo (a raw screen recording becomes a finished, editable product demo: auto zoom that follows the action, a smooth cursor and click ripples where there's a pointer trace, dead time cut or sped up, a callout per step, hidden areas over private things, an intro and outro in the brand or a Look, captions and optional voice-over). Spec: docs/plans/2026-11-04-screen-recording-demo.md (draft 3, commit e477294; review logs at its end: §16 draft 1->2 and draft 2->3). Line refs are as of e477294.
Spec key: D1
Spec section(s): §1 HyperFrames, §5.3, §10 Phase 0, gotchas 7-9, 20-21

## Background
Recording scenes play the ORIGINAL library file with data-media-start (the offset = step's in) and
data-playback-rate (speed = (out-in)/slot duration), inside a .va-stage that GSAP scales and translates. data-playback-rate
is parsed and clamped 0.1-10 by the HyperFrames 0.8.222 runtime but isn't in `npx hyperframes docs data-attributes`
(checked). data-playback-start takes precedence over data-media-start (runtime reads playback-start ?? media-start ?? 0).
data-hf-media-start-basis changes the meaning: local (default) = hostStart + authoredStart, global = authoredStart
(seen in node_modules/hyperframes/dist/hyperframe.runtime.iife.js). A recording scene usually starts after an intro, so
the basis decides whether the offset is absolute. Holds (a scene longer than its step at 0.5x) currently plan a still
image of the out frame because a <video> is only visible for its own data-duration; if HyperFrames can hold a clip's
frame natively, the still goes away. The run deadline is 22 min (src/deps.ts:92), so render speed bounds demo length.

## Approach
Make a fixture recording with ffmpeg: 1440p H.264, 1 s GOP (-g 30), 30 fps, a burned-in frame counter
(drawtext with the frame number) and a moving square. Build a composition: an intro beat 0-4 s, then a recording beat at
4 s with data-va-in=12.4, data-va-out=21.8, a slot duration of 7.5 s (rate 1.2533), a scaled/translated .va-stage, then
a held beat (rate 0.5 then still). Try both data-hf-media-start-basis values. Render locally (npx hyperframes render) and
once on the runner (a test run; --dry first, ask the owner). Read frames back with ffmpeg and OCR/compare the counter
to the expected source frame for every output frame. Also time render per output second on the runner. Check whether a
<video> whose data-duration exceeds the remaining media holds its last frame (the lint message about "final-frame
hold" suggests a native hold exists).

## Done when
Pass: every output frame shows the expected source frame (+-0) with the chosen basis; the hold shows the out
frame; under 4 s of render per second of output on the runner. Results change: which basis value the contract pins on
recording slots (§5.3 contract rules); whether holds need <step>.hold.jpg (§5.3 Holds, emit, render-job allowance); the
time budget (§10) and max demo length. If rate isn't frame-accurate, fall back to one beat per speed segment.

## Tests
The comparison script logs per-frame expected vs actual counters (JSON lines) and a summary; kept as a regression render test for later HyperFrames upgrades (package.json:71 pins 0.8.222).

## Background
Path B encodes while recording: the display track drawn to a canvas at the FIRST frame's size (window
captures resize; avc1 streams with resolution changes don't play reliably), canvas.captureStream(30) fed to Mediabunny's
MediaStreamVideoTrackSource -> WebCodecs H.264 -> Mp4OutputFormat({fastStart:'in-memory'}) with keyFrameInterval:1 at
3-4 Mbps for 1440p (~0.03-0.04 bpp). The file is ready at stop: no second pass, no MediaRecorder fragmented MP4 (which
§4.2 refuses). Fallback: MediaRecorder (video/mp4;codecs=avc1 where supported, else WebM VP9) + post-hoc conversion.
Path C converts uploads with the same settings. Mediabunny is MPL-2.0 (unmodified use has no copyleft obligation);
keyFrameInterval (default 5) and fastStart are documented; Worker support is unverified; BufferTarget suits <~100 MB.

## Approach
A test page: getDisplayMedia -> canvas -> live encode for 5 min at 1440p; count dropped frames (compare
encoded frame count to 30 fps x duration); resize the captured window mid-recording; check VideoEncoder.isConfigSupported
for avc1 and the fallback path. Separately, convert 5-min 1440p MOV/WebM files in the page and in a Worker. Run every
output through the §4.2 checks (the new mp4.ts stss/stts parsing, or ffprobe for the spike).

## Done when
Pass: live encode under 2% dropped frames on a 2023 laptop and the file passes §4.2; conversion under 1.5x real
time and passes §4.2 in all three browsers. Results change: Worker vs main thread; whether Firefox gets the fallback;
bitrate; whether path B must keep the canvas step.

title: Role table: replace every isTakeRole branch in media-uploads.ts with ROLES[role] lookups (takes unchanged)
description:
Project: video-agent, an open-source Netlify template that turns a prompt into a published MP4 via Netlify Agent Runner runs writing HyperFrames compositions; Hono+OpenAPI API, Netlify Database (Drizzle), Blobs, Identity, React+Mantine UI, MCP. Feature: screen recording -> polished demo (a raw screen recording becomes a finished, editable product demo: auto zoom that follows the action, a smooth cursor and click ripples where there's a pointer trace, dead time cut or sped up, a callout per step, hidden areas over private things, an intro and outro in the brand or a Look, captions and optional voice-over). Spec: docs/plans/2026-11-04-screen-recording-demo.md (draft 3, commit e477294; review logs at its end: §16 draft 1->2 and draft 2->3). Line refs are as of e477294.
Spec key: 1.1
Spec section(s): §1 Media and uploads, §4.2 The role table

## Background
Every narration-take rule in src/domain/media-uploads.ts keys off isTakeRole (:50): the unknown-role
refusal "role must be narration-take or narration-upload" (:119-120), the scopeJobId pair of checks (:121-124),
assertNarrationEnabled (:125), the 30-an-hour assertTakeRate (:86-95, called at :137), quotaForTakes (:138, :258),
checkWholeHash (:245), "A recording must be an audio file" (:357) and takeSamples (:367). Adding screen-recording to
isTakeRole would fire all of them wrongly (review A6). The remote review (draft 2->3) asked not to promise knobs nobody
uses; every remaining field differs between the two roles, only wholeHashAtComplete (true for both) is dropped.

Found in the polish round (not in the spec): outside media-uploads.ts the code treats ANY non-null role as a take.
src/domain/takes.ts:27 is `isTake = (m) => m.role !== null`, used at 14 call sites (edits.ts:360 library picks,
media.ts:203/:246/:417, plans.ts:226/:238, remix.ts:143, take-extras.ts:61/:69, takes.ts:40 canReadTake, :124
retention, :242 GC), and the Postgres library queries leave out every row with a role (`takeVisible`,
src/store/drizzle.ts:127-130 `isNull(t.media.role)`; the provenance join at drizzle.ts:116 too), while the memory
store's isTake (src/store/memory.ts:1080) checks the two take roles explicitly. A 'screen-recording' row would be
hidden from the library on Postgres, shown on the memory store, and handled as a take by retention, GC and
visibility. The codebase also says "recording" for narration takes (MediaDto.recording = recordingDto,
media.ts:246; "Delete unused recordings"; take_deleted's message), so new code must say "screen recording".

## Approach
1. New src/domain/media-roles.ts: `export const TAKE_ROLES = ['narration-take', 'narration-upload'] as const`,
   `isTakeRole(role)` (moved from media-uploads.ts:50, re-exported there for existing imports), and
   `ROLES: Record<MediaRole, RolePolicy>` with RolePolicy = { audioOnly: boolean; needsScope: boolean;
   quotaSetting: 'takeQuotaBytes' | 'recordingQuotaBytes'; perHour: number; gatedBy: 'narration' | null;
   samples: boolean }. Rows: narration-take and narration-upload = { audioOnly: true, needsScope: true,
   quotaSetting: 'takeQuotaBytes', perHour: TAKE_UPLOADS_PER_HOUR (30), gatedBy: 'narration', samples: true }.
   The screen-recording row ({ false, false, 'recordingQuotaBytes', 10, null, false }) is added by 1.3a with the
   MediaRole value. A field is added only when a third role needs one; the whole-file hash at completion stays a
   plain rule for every role.
2. Replace the checks at :119-124 (unknown role -> 400 listing UPLOAD_ROLES; `needsScope` true -> scopeJobId
   required; false -> scopeJobId refused), :125 (gatedBy), :137 (perHour, via a generalized
   `repo.countRoleUploads(uploaderId, roles, since)` that replaces countNarrationTakes in both stores,
   src/store/types.ts:397), :138/:258 (quota by quotaSetting), :245 (checkWholeHash for every role), :357 (audioOnly)
   and :367 (samples) with ROLES lookups. `UPLOAD_ROLES` (the roles createUploadSession accepts) starts as
   TAKE_ROLES; 1.2b adds 'screen-recording'.
3. Narrow takes.ts:27 to `isTake = (m) => isTakeRole(m.role)`, make memory.ts:1080 import the same helper, and
   change drizzle's takeVisible and the provenance filter from `isNull(role)` to `role is null or role not in
   TAKE_ROLES` (an `inArray`/`notInArray` on TAKE_ROLES). Audit all 14 isTake call sites and leave a one-line comment
   at each that says why takes (and only takes) are excluded. With only take roles in the union, behaviour is
   byte-for-byte unchanged.

## Done when
Takes behave exactly as before (every existing take test passes untouched); the table is the only place role rules
live; `isTake` means "narration take or upload" in both stores and every query; no code path tests `role !== null` or
`isNull(role)` to mean "take".

## Tests
New test/media-roles.test.ts pins every take rule on memory and PGlite through createApp(fakeDeps): unknown role 400
(message lists the accepted roles), take without scopeJobId 400, library upload with scopeJobId 400, narration disabled
409, 31st take in an hour rate_limited, quota exceeded 413 with bytes left, whole-hash mismatch 400 at complete,
audio-only refusal, samples computed. A store-parity test inserts a media row with a made-up non-take role directly
through the repo and asserts both stores list it in the library and isTake() is false (guards the drizzle/memory
divergence). Existing test/media-uploads.test.ts and voice-over tests unchanged and green. Each test logs
{ test, role, step, outcome } JSON lines.

Standard: unit and integration with createApp(fakeDeps) (test/helpers.ts harness) and PGlite (pgStore(), every migration applied); Playwright on the mock build (VITE_MOCK=1) for UI; structured JSON logs (one event per step, with ids, durations and outcome) so failures are diagnosable from logs alone. CI (npm run typecheck, lint, vitest, npx playwright test, openapi:check, db:check) stays green. Repo rule: when checks pass, commit only your own files, push to main and confirm the Netlify production deploy is ready (other sessions often have uncommitted files in the checkout; never stage them).

title: OpenAPI, the screen_recording feature string, list_media role/trace flags, MCP list_media
description:
Project: video-agent, an open-source Netlify template that turns a prompt into a published MP4 via Netlify Agent Runner runs writing HyperFrames compositions; Hono+OpenAPI API, Netlify Database (Drizzle), Blobs, Identity, React+Mantine UI, MCP. Spec: docs/plans/2026-11-04-screen-recording-demo.md (draft 3, commit e477294; review logs at its end: §16 draft 1->2 and draft 2->3). Line refs are as of e477294.
Spec key: 1.5b (plan task 1.5)
Spec section(s): §6 intro, §6.2 MCP, roadmap rules 1-2

## Background
Clients discover features from GET /api/v1/config `features` (roadmap rule 1; the CLI plan owns the array and adds it
in its phase 1.2). Agents and the UI need to know which library items are screen recordings and which have a pointer
trace. Naming: the media DTO already has a `recording` field, the narration take's facts (recordingDto,
src/domain/media.ts:246, takes.ts:64), so the new facts must not reuse that name.

## Approach
- Add 'screen_recording' to the features registry in this PR (rule 1: each feature adds its own string). It means:
  the screen-recording role on upload sessions, the trace routes, and (from 2.6) `recording` on create and remix.
  Until 2.6 ships, `features` lists it only when the server accepts all of those, so add the string in this PR but
  behind `SCREEN_RECORDING_API_READY` (a constant flipped to true by 2.6) so clients never see a half feature.
- Media DTO (media.ts:217-247): add top-level `role: 'narration-take' | 'narration-upload' | 'screen-recording' |
  null` and `hasTrace: boolean` (true when traceKey is set); the take-only `recording` field is unchanged.
- MCP list_media (src/mcp.ts:961) shows role and has_trace per item and accepts a `role` filter
  ('screen-recording'); its description says screen recordings are private to the uploader until a video uses them.
- Regenerate ui/src/api/openapi.json and ui/src/api/schema.d.ts (`npm run openapi:gen`); the mcp-catalog test stays in
  step.

## Done when
openapi:check green; features lists screen_recording once the API is complete; the media DTO and list_media show role
and hasTrace.

## Tests
Integration (createApp(fakeDeps)): GET /api/v1/config lists screen_recording only with the flag on; media DTO fields
for a plain clip (role null, hasTrace false), a take (role narration-take, recording unchanged) and a recording with a
trace; MCP list_media output and its role filter; test/mcp-catalog.test.ts. JSON log per assertion group.

Standard: unit and integration with createApp(fakeDeps) (test/helpers.ts harness) and PGlite (pgStore(), every migration applied); Playwright on the mock build (VITE_MOCK=1) for UI; structured JSON logs (one event per step, with ids, durations and outcome) so failures are diagnosable from logs alone. Spec key: 1.G
Spec section(s): §10 Gate 1

## Background
Proves the library half before any run uses it. No credits. Freezing a trace needs create with `recording` (2.6,
phase 2), so this gate checks set/replace/read on the deploy preview and leaves the freeze to the integration tests
(1.4b inserts the version_media row directly) and to the phase 2 gate.

## Approach
All phase 1 unit and integration tests green on memory and PGlite. Then a new script scripts/e2e/recording-library.ts
(header lists every variable and check, like scripts/e2e/remix.ts; helpers from scripts/e2e/lib.ts and
narration-lib.ts), run on a deploy preview with ALLOW_NON_PRODUCTION=true (no credits; still `--dry` first, which
prints the steps and touches nothing):
1. Make a normalized 140 MB fixture locally (ffmpeg testsrc2 1440p, -g 30, +faststart; cached under .render/) and a
   matching trace.json; upload both through the SDK's media.uploadRecording (1.5c) as Creator A.
2. Check the item: ready, role screen-recording, hasTrace, meta.mp4 facts; the assembly function's memory log lines
   (media.assembly_memory, from 1.2c) peak under 700 MB.
3. Visibility: Creator B gets 404 for get, file and trace; an admin can read it; A can GET the trace and it's scrubbed.
4. Replace the trace (PUT again), then a bad trace (wrong frame size) gets 400.
5. A refused file: a 3 s clip with a 10 s GOP gets the keyframe message.
6. Preview by key: the ensureBundle integration test (1.5a) covers version bundles; here, request the item's signed
   file URL with a Range header (206 and the right bytes), proving the media store serves a 140 MB item in ranges.
   A full version preview of a recording is checked in the phase 2 gate.
7. Cleanup (delete the uploads) at the end, even on failure; --keep skips it.
Logs one JSON line per step { step, ok, ms, details }.

## Done when
All of the above pass on the deploy preview; results logged; the plan's as-built note lists the peak memory measured.

## Tests
The script above (with --dry and --keep) plus the phase 1 CI suite.

title: mp4.ts: parse stss and stts (track timescale) to measure the longest keyframe gap; detect fragmented MP4
description:
Project: video-agent, an open-source Netlify template that turns a prompt into a published MP4 via Netlify Agent Runner runs writing HyperFrames compositions; Hono+OpenAPI API, Netlify Database (Drizzle), Blobs, Identity, React+Mantine UI, MCP. Feature: screen recording -> polished demo (a raw screen recording becomes a finished, editable product demo: auto zoom that follows the action, a smooth cursor and click ripples where there's a pointer trace, dead time cut or sped up, a callout per step, hidden areas over private things, an intro and outro in the brand or a Look, captions and optional voice-over). Spec: docs/plans/2026-11-04-screen-recording-demo.md (draft 3, commit e477294; review logs at its end: §16 draft 1->2 and draft 2->3). Line refs are as of e477294.
Spec key: 1.2a (plan task 1.2)
Spec section(s): §1 (mp4.ts), §4.2 Checks and limits table, gotchas 4-5, review R2

## Background
src/lib/media/mp4.ts reads box headers and moov metadata only (:1) and computes fastStart (moov before
mdat, :94); it parses no stss (sync samples) or stts (sample timing), so the keyframe gap can't be measured. Long GOPs
make HyperFrames' per-frame seeks slow (gotcha 4). ISO/IEC 14496-12 §8.6.2: when stss is absent, EVERY sample is a sync
sample, so an all-intra file is the best case and must be accepted (review R2 corrected draft 2's "refuse no stss").
The §4.2 limits table also needs a constant 24-30 fps and one picture size for the whole file (gotcha 5: window
captures resize; avc1 streams with resolution changes don't play reliably), so this task reports those facts too.
inspectMp4 (mp4.ts:82) is called by classify (classify.ts:138) with { audioOnly: true }; Mp4Info is at mp4.ts:3-11.

## Approach
Extend Mp4Info with a `video` timing block, filled only for the first video track:
{ timescale: number (mdhd), sampleCount: number, fps: number (sampleCount / media duration),
  cfr: boolean (every stts delta equal within 1 tick; a single-entry stts is CFR),
  maxKeyframeGapSec: number (no stss -> one frame), syncSamples: number,
  sampleEntries: number (stsd entry_count; > 1 means the picture size or codec changes mid-file),
  sizeChanges: boolean (sampleEntries > 1, or an avc1/avc3 entry whose width/height differ from tkhd's) }
and top-level `fragmented: boolean` (a top-level moof, or moov/mvex present). Walk moov/trak(video)/mdia/mdhd and
mdia/minf/stbl/{stts,stss,stsd} inside the existing bounded parser limits (maxBoxes 20,000, maxDepth 12,
maxMoovBytes 64 MiB, mp4.ts:15); stts/stss entry counts are checked against the box size before reading (a count
past the end throws Mp4Error). Gap = the largest time between consecutive sync samples, and from the last one to the
end, computed from cumulative stts deltas in the track timescale. Pure, no Node built-ins beyond what mp4.ts already
uses (it runs in Functions and the browser). Existing callers keep working: the new fields are additive, and a file
without a video track has `video: null`.

## Done when
Mp4Info reports gap, fps, cfr, size changes, fragmented and fast start for every fixture; existing callers and tests
unaffected.

## Tests
src/lib/media/mp4.test.ts with small generated fixtures committed under test/fixtures/mp4/ (each 1-3 s at 320x180,
made by a documented script test/fixtures/mp4/make.sh using ffmpeg, with expected values in expected.json): -g 30
(gap 1.0 s), -g 300 on a 3 s clip (gap = duration), all-intra -g 1 written without stss (gap one frame, accepted),
fragmented (-movflags frag_keyframe+empty_moov), non-fast-start, VFR (a concat of 30 fps and 15 fps parts, cfr false),
a two-sample-entry file (resolution change, sizeChanges true), audio-only M4A (video null). Malformed stss/stts
(counts past the box end) throw Mp4Error; limits respected. Each case logs { fixture, expected, actual } as JSON.

Standard: unit and integration with createApp(fakeDeps) (test/helpers.ts harness) and PGlite (pgStore(), every migration applied); Playwright on the mock build (VITE_MOCK=1) for UI; structured JSON logs (one event per step, with ids, durations and outcome) so failures are diagnosable from logs alone. CI (npm run typecheck, lint, vitest, npx playwright test, openapi:check, db:check) stays green. Repo rule: when checks pass, commit only your own files, push to main and confirm the Netlify production deploy is ready (other sessions often have uncommitted files in the checkout; never stage them).

title: classify + upload sessions: the screen-recording role and its limits (5 min, 150 MB, keyframe gap <=2 s, fast start, not fragmented)
description:
Project: video-agent, an open-source Netlify template that turns a prompt into a published MP4 via Netlify Agent Runner runs writing HyperFrames compositions; Hono+OpenAPI API, Netlify Database (Drizzle), Blobs, Identity, React+Mantine UI, MCP. Feature: screen recording -> polished demo (a raw screen recording becomes a finished, editable product demo: auto zoom that follows the action, a smooth cursor and click ripples where there's a pointer trace, dead time cut or sped up, a callout per step, hidden areas over private things, an intro and outro in the brand or a Look, captions and optional voice-over). Spec: docs/plans/2026-11-04-screen-recording-demo.md (draft 3, commit e477294; review logs at its end: §16 draft 1->2 and draft 2->3). Line refs are as of e477294.
Spec key: 1.2b (plan task 1.2)
Spec section(s): §4.2, §1 Media and uploads, §6.1 (any H.264 clip can be a recording)

## Background
Today a clip is H.264 (avc1/avc3, classify.ts:151) with AAC or no audio, <=100 MB (:133), <=2 min (:155),
<=4096 px (:157; LIMITS at classify.ts:36-46; MP4 path :132-167; WebM is audio-only :168-178). Upload sessions cap at
100 MB (media-uploads.ts:114-115) and the in-flight reservation is 1 GiB (UPLOAD_QUOTA_BYTES, :23; checked at
:129-135 with "You have too many uploads in progress. Finish or wait for them first."). A raw demo runs long, so
recordings get their own limits; ordinary clips keep theirs. Using a role on `video` items (not a new kind) keeps
every kind==='video' path working (pickers, previews, version_media, slots). Limits are built on §14 Q2's default and
D5's result (100 MB if D5 fails). 1.3a has already added 'screen-recording' to MediaRole and ROLES and made the
role private-until-used; this task opens uploads for it.

## Approach
- `classify(bytes, { head?, role? })` (classify.ts:106). For role 'screen-recording' the MP4 path applies
  RECORDING_LIMITS (exported from classify.ts, imported by every consumer so values never drift: bytes 150 MB,
  seconds 300, maxSide 4096, fps 24-30, maxKeyframeGapSec 2): H.264 (avc1|avc3); AAC audio or none (kept, unused);
  <=5 min; <=150 MB; <=4096 px; `video.cfr` and fps within 24-30; `video.sizeChanges` false;
  maxKeyframeGapSec <= 2; fastStart true; fragmented false (all from 1.2a). The 100 MB check at :133 becomes
  role-aware. Every refusal says what to do, e.g. "This recording needs a keyframe every second. The app converts
  recordings for you; if you uploaded from a script, run: ffmpeg -i in.mov -vf scale=trunc(iw/2)*2:trunc(ih/2)*2
  -c:v libx264 -g 30 -keyint_min 30 -r 30 -crf 20 -movflags +faststart -an out.mp4" (one message per rule: codec,
  length, size, frame rate, size change, keyframes, fragmented, fast start). Export the command as
  RECORDING_FFMPEG_HINT for the UI, CLI and docs.
- Assembly (media-uploads.ts:352) passes `{ role: u.role }` to classify; the `audioOnly` rule from ROLES still
  refuses a non-audio take.
- createUploadSession: add 'screen-recording' to UPLOAD_ROLES (1.1); no scopeJobId (needsScope false); the size cap
  at :114 uses RECORDING_LIMITS.bytes for the role ("Screen recordings must be 150 MB or smaller."); perHour 10
  through ROLES; quota through recordingQuotaBytes (enforced by 1.3b). Recordings always use a session, even under
  4 MB (the single-request upload path, media.ts:174, never takes a role).
- x-sdk (CLI plan va-p1th.2.1): createUploadSession's `role` field already exists for takes, so it can't be gated as
  a whole with fieldFeatures; instead the SDK's media.uploadRecording and media.upload({ role: 'screen-recording' })
  (1.5c) check features for 'screen_recording' and refuse with unsupported_by_server. Note the value in the route's
  x-sdk description so the generator's docs say it.
- In-flight reservation: when reserved + size > UPLOAD_QUOTA_BYTES, the error says how many sessions are open:
  "You have 3 uploads in progress. Finish or cancel one to start another." (a new repo.countOpenUploads(uploaderId)
  in both stores, next to reservedUploadBytes, src/store/types.ts:191). Code stays rate_limited.
- Every ready video item (any role) records its MP4 timing facts in meta.json via mergeMediaMeta (media.ts:35):
  `mp4: { fps, cfr, maxKeyframeGapSec, sizeChanges, fastStart }`. 2.6 reads them to decide whether an ordinary clip
  can be used as a recording without failing later in the run.

## Done when
A normalized 4-min 1440p recording uploads through a session with the role and becomes a ready item; every bad file
is refused with its own message; ordinary clips keep the 2 min / 100 MB rules and the single-request path; the
in-flight message names the open sessions.

## Tests
Unit (src/lib/media/classify.test.ts): classify with and without the role over the 1.2a fixtures plus a 3-min
synthetic one (length, size via a stubbed byteLength, codec, gap, fps 15 and 60 refused, VFR refused, resolution
change refused, fast start, fragmented, all-intra accepted); each message asserted. Integration (createApp(fakeDeps),
memory + PGlite): session create with the role and no scopeJobId; with a scopeJobId 400; 150 MB + 1 refused with the
role message; 101 MB accepted with the role and refused without it; complete -> ready item with role and meta.mp4;
11th recording session in an hour rate_limited; in-flight message with the count. JSON log line per case.

Standard: unit and integration with createApp(fakeDeps) (test/helpers.ts harness) and PGlite (pgStore(), every migration applied); Playwright on the mock build (VITE_MOCK=1) for UI; structured JSON logs (one event per step, with ids, durations and outcome) so failures are diagnosable from logs alone. CI (npm run typecheck, lint, vitest, npx playwright test, openapi:check, db:check) stays green. Repo rule: when checks pass, commit only your own files, push to main and confirm the Netlify production deploy is ready (other sessions often have uncommitted files in the checkout; never stage them).

## Background

(review A6). version_media is db/schema.ts:500-518 with an index on media_id (`version_media_media_idx`). This task
lands BEFORE uploads open (1.2b depends on it), so a screen recording is never readable by other people, not even for
one deploy.

## Approach
- Add 'screen-recording' to MEDIA_ROLES (src/domain/types.ts:621-623; MediaRow.role at :651, MediaUploadRow.role at :735) and its ROLES row from 1.1
  ({ audioOnly: false, needsScope: false, quotaSetting: 'recordingQuotaBytes', perHour: 10, gatedBy: null,
  samples: false }). UPLOAD_ROLES doesn't include it yet (1.2b adds it), so the API still refuses the role; tests
  insert rows through the repo. Export `isScreenRecording(m)`.
- New store query `jobsUsingMedia(mediaId): Promise<{ jobId: string; versionN: number }[]>` in both stores (memory and
  Postgres; non-deleted jobs only; uses version_media_media_idx).
- `canReadRecording(repo, p, m)`: uploader or admin -> true; Reviewer/Viewer -> false; Creator -> true when some job
  from jobsUsingMedia passes canSee(p, job) (src/domain/videos.ts:388), else false.
- One dispatcher `canReadMedia(repo, p, m)` (takes -> canReadTake, screen recordings -> canReadRecording, others ->
  true) replaces canReadTake at every call site: media.ts:211 (get), :301 and readableMedia (takes.ts:98, used for the
  library list and picker pages, media.ts:320, :334), :363 (file and signed URL minting, which the media edge function
  then serves), edits.ts:156, mcp.ts:1429 (list_media and get).
- Library listing: with 1.1's narrowing, Postgres lists rows whose role isn't a take role; readableMedia then drops
  the screen recordings the reader can't see, on both stores. Library picks (edits.ts:360 media op, media.ts:203 and
  :417, plans.ts:226/:238) accept a screen recording only when canReadMedia passes.
- Reviewers and Viewers only ever see rendered videos. The media DTO's existing `recording` field stays the take's
  recordingDto (media.ts:246); screen-recording facts go in 1.5b's new fields.

## Done when
Another Creator can't list, get, pick or download an unused recording (404, like a missing item); after a version
uses it, people who can see that video can; private videos keep their recordings private; deleting the video makes
it private again.

title: Retention, GC and quota for recordings: retainUntil from the last using video's deletion, 30 days, row locks, recordingQuotaBytes setting
description:
Project: video-agent, an open-source Netlify template that turns a prompt into a published MP4 via Netlify Agent Runner runs writing HyperFrames compositions; Hono+OpenAPI API, Netlify Database (Drizzle), Blobs, Identity, React+Mantine UI, MCP. Spec: docs/plans/2026-11-04-screen-recording-demo.md (draft 3, commit e477294; review logs at its end: §16 draft 1->2 and draft 2->3). Line refs are as of e477294.
Spec key: 1.3b (plan task 1.3)
Spec section(s): §4.2 Sessions and quota, §9 Retention, §14 Q2

## Background
Recordings are big, so unused ones must go away like narration takes (README "Retention", README.md:188): deleted 30
days after last use, and "Delete unused recordings" on the Media page (route summary at src/app.ts:1504; takes.ts:311;
ui/src/pages/Media.tsx) covers them too. Takes use a row-lock protocol: every reference writer and GC lock media rows
with SELECT … FOR UPDATE in media-id order (lockTakes, takes.ts:104-118); retainReleased (:121-125) starts the 30 days
when the last reference goes; GC at :242. Takes have their own 2 GiB budget, settings.take_quota_bytes
(db/schema.ts:32, read through narration-settings.ts). Screen recordings get a separate budget, recordingQuotaBytes,
added to the settings row by 1.4b's single phase-1 migration.

## Approach
- Generalize lockTakes to `lockMediaRows(repo, ids, live)` (keep lockTakes as a wrapper so take code is untouched);
  its refusal message for a screen recording says "A screen recording this uses was deleted." (code take_deleted
  stays for takes; a screen recording uses the existing 410 gone code, src/lib/errors.ts, so no new code is needed).
- retainUntil for a screen recording: upload time + 30 days while no non-deleted job uses it (jobsUsingMedia, 1.3a);
  null while one does; reset to deletion time + 30 days when the last using job is deleted (the job-delete path calls
  a `releaseRecordings(repo, deps, jobId)` under the row locks). The sweep deletes the item's bytes (original, clean,
  poster, meta.json AND `<mediaId>/trace.json`) with the same two phases takes use (deletingAt, then delete).
- Quota: `repo.screenRecordingBytes(uploaderId)` (stored or being checked, like narrationTakeBytes, types.ts:446) and
  a quotaForRole(deps, role, userId, incoming, repo) that reads ROLES[role].quotaSetting; enforced at session create and
  complete. Message: "Your screen recordings have 1.2 GiB of 2 GiB left, not enough for this one (180 MB). Delete
  unused recordings on the Media page, or ask an admin for more space." Code 413 as for takes.
- Admin settings: recordingQuotaBytes in the /admin/settings schema and UI next to the takes' budget, labelled
  "Screen recordings per person" (the takes' field is relabelled "Voice recordings per person" so the two are clear).
- "Delete unused recordings" deletes the caller's unused takes AND unused screen recordings; its result counts both.
- README's Retention paragraph (README.md:186-189) says screen recordings follow the same 30-day rule with their own
  2 GiB budget (the full section is 3.6).

## Done when
An unused recording is swept 30 days after upload or after its last video was deleted; a used one never is while a
video uses it; quota refusals say how much is left; the trace blob goes with the item.

## Tests
Integration (fake clock) on memory and PGlite: sweep timing (29 days kept, 31 days gone) for never-used and
used-then-deleted recordings; a race between a create that uses the recording and GC (row locks; the create gets 410 gone
or the sweep skips the row, never both succeeding); quota exceeded 413 with bytes left; takes and screen
recordings counted against separate budgets; Delete unused recordings removes both kinds; trace.json removed with the

title: Pointer trace schema (src/lib/recording-trace.ts, shared with the CLI): caps, 0-1 positions, keyframed redact entries, name/reason/path scrubbing
description:
Project: video-agent, an open-source Netlify template that turns a prompt into a published MP4 via Netlify Agent Runner runs writing HyperFrames compositions; Hono+OpenAPI API, Netlify Database (Drizzle), Blobs, Identity, React+Mantine UI, MCP. Feature: screen recording -> polished demo (a raw screen recording becomes a finished, editable product demo: auto zoom that follows the action, a smooth cursor and click ripples where there's a pointer trace, dead time cut or sped up, a callout per step, hidden areas over private things, an intro and outro in the brand or a Look, captions and optional voice-over). Spec: docs/plans/2026-11-04-screen-recording-demo.md (draft 3, commit e477294; review logs at its end: §16 draft 1->2 and draft 2->3). Line refs are as of e477294.
Spec key: 1.4a (plan task 1.4)
Spec section(s): §5.1 trace.json, §4.6 step 3 (what is recorded), §4.7 Limits and Names, gotcha 15

## Background
The trace is the cursor/click log from path A (or any tool that writes the schema). target.name is text
from someone else's page and can carry prompt-injection text or personal data ("Delete john@acme.com"); redact[].reason
and navigate.path (/users/jane@acme.com) too. The remote review (R4) required the policy to be enforced where the trace
becomes a run input, not only in the CLI. Redaction boxes must move with scrolling (review R3), so entries are keyframed.
§4.6 records focusin and pointerdown/up as well as clicks, and the planner clusters "clicks, typing and focus boxes"
and has a "long drag" golden case (§5.2 rule 4, §11), so the schema carries focus and drag events too (the spec's
example shows only click, type, scroll and navigate).

## Approach
New src/lib/recording-trace.ts: a zod schema with no Node deps (used by the CLI, Functions, the browser and
recording.ts). Box = [x, y, w, h], each 0-1, with x + w <= 1 and y + h <= 1.
{ v: 1, source: { kind: 'cli'|'upload'|'browser'|'script' (script reserved for tours), tool (<=80 chars),
  startedAt (ISO) }, frame: { width, height (1-4096 ints), fps (1-120), duration (0-300.5 s) },
  viewport: { width, height, dpr (0.5-4) },
  moves: [t, x, y][] (<=30,000; RDP-simplified at 0.5 px by the writer),
  events: ( click { t, x, y, button 0-4, target?: { role (<=40), name (<=60), box } }
          | type { t, end, box, keys (count only) } | scroll { t, end, dy } | focus { t, box, role? }
          | drag { t, end, from: [x, y], to: [x, y] } | navigate { t, path } )[] (<=5,000),
  redact: { start, end, reason, boxes: [t, x, y, w, h][] (1-600 per entry; w = h = 0 means hidden) }[]
          (<=200 entries, <=20,000 keys in all) }.
All numbers finite; positions 0-1; times within 0..frame.duration; moves, events and each entry's boxes sorted by t;
end >= t. `.transform` normalizes target.name, focus role and redact[].reason: trim to 60 chars, drop characters
outside letters, digits, spaces and .,:;!?'"()-/&+#@, replace email-shaped and 8-or-more-digit strings with "…".
navigate.path must match ^/[^?#]*$, <=200 chars, each segment scrubbed with the same patterns (a matching segment
becomes "…"). Exports: `Trace`, `RedactEntry` ({ start, end, reason, boxes }), `parseTrace(json): Trace` (throws
TraceError whose message lists each failing field path), `normalizeTrace(t): Trace`, `scrubName(s)`, `scrubPath(p)`,
`TRACE_MAX_BYTES = 4 * 1024 * 1024`, and `TRACE_LIMITS` ({ moves: 30000, events: 5000, redactEntries: 200,
redactKeys: 20000, keysPerEntry: 600, nameChars: 60, pathChars: 200 }) so the CLI, server and docs share one set.

## Done when
One schema used everywhere; normalizing is idempotent; malformed traces are refused with field paths in the error;
the limits exist once, as constants.

## Tests
src/lib/recording-trace.test.ts: a good trace (fixture test/fixtures/recording/trace-good.json) round-trips; each cap
at the limit accepted and +1 refused (moves, events, entries, keys per entry, total keys); non-finite numbers,
positions outside 0-1, boxes past the edge, unsorted times, end < t; names with emails, 8+ digit runs, emoji, newlines
and injection text ("Ignore previous instructions…" is cut to 60 allowed characters) scrubbed; reasons and path
segments scrubbed; a path with ? or # refused; source.kind 'script' accepted; focus and drag events accepted;
idempotence (normalize twice = once); a property test (a seeded PRNG loop over 1,000 random strings; the repo has no fast-check, so no new dependency) never emitting a disallowed
character or an email/long-digit match. Failures log { case, path, message } as JSON.
